statement: The a=1 Picard-kernel equality case is almost ruled, or has characteristic two with ample canonical bundle and a normalized K3 cover with rational double points.
exact_statement: [After Ekedahl]\label{prop:normalized-mup-ekedahl} In Proposition~\ref{prop:normalized-mup-conductor}, suppose $a=1$ and $2g(Y)-2=pY^2$. Then either $X$ is almost ruled, or $p=2$ and \[ \omega_X\text{ is ample},\qquad \chi(\OO_X)=1,\qquad \omega_X^{\otimes2}\simeq\OO_X(2Y). \] In the latter case $N$ has only rational double points, its minimal resolution is a K3 surface, and \[ 1\leq Y^2=K_X^2\leq9,\qquad g(Y)=Y^2+1. \] In this latter case the zero scheme $Z$ of Proposition~\ref{prop:normalized-mup-singularity-defect} has length $12+Y^2$, and the Fitting singular subscheme of $N$ has length $2(12+Y^2)$. In particular, when $p>2$ the stated equality forces $X$ to be almost ruled.

statement: Equality in the normalized order-p Picard-kernel conductor bound makes the normalization a torsor under the classical deformed multiplicative Kummer kernel, with nowhere-zero tangent action; for a=1 it must be singular off the ample curve.
exact_statement: \label{cor:normalized-equality-torsor} In the notation and hypotheses of Proposition~\ref{prop:normalized-mup-conductor}, suppose $2g(Y)-2=apY^2$. Let $L=\OO_X(aY)$ and let $s_a$ be its canonical section. Define $G_{s_a}$ by the formula in Corollary~\ref{cor:smooth-torsor}, with $L$ and $s_a$ in place of $\OO_X(Y)$ and $s$. Then $\pi:N\to X$ is a $G_{s_a}$-torsor. Its infinitesimal action is a homomorphism \[ \OO_N(-aD)\longrightarrow T_N \] that is nonzero on every fibre, is tangent to $D$, and restricts to an isomorphism $\OO_D(-aD)\simeq T_D$. If $a=1$, the surface $N$ has at least one singular point outside $D$.

statement: When a=1 in the equality case, every positive plurigenus of a smooth resolution is at most one; its Kodaira dimension is at most zero and a nonzero plurigenus forces the normal canonical bundle to be torsion.
exact_statement: \label{cor:normalized-mup-plurigenera} In Proposition~\ref{prop:normalized-mup-singularity-defect}, suppose $a=1$. statement: The normalized mu_p cover in the checked leading-form situation has ramification index one, residue degree p and exact generic conductor exponent a(p-1).
exact_statement: Let $X$ be a smooth projective integral surface over an algebraically closed field $k$ of characteristic $p>0$. Let $Y\subset X$ be a smooth ample integral curve, and let $M$ be a nontrivial line bundle of order $p$ with $M|_Y\simeq\OO_Y$. Choose a trivialization of $M^p$ and let $T\to X$ be its $\mu_p$-torsor. Let $N$ be the normalization of $T$ and $\pi:N\to X$ the resulting finite map. The logarithmic differential of $M$ has order $pa$ along $Y$ for an integer $a\geq1$, with nonzero tangential leading coefficient. The full inverse image $D=\pi^*Y$ is a reduced integral ample Cartier divisor. At its generic point the ramification index is one, the residue degree is $p$, and the conductor of $T$ in $N$ has coefficient $a(p-1)$. The normalization $\widetilde D$ of $D$ has genus $g(Y)$. Let $\mathfrak c\subset\OO_N$ be the conductor ideal, put $c=a(p-1)$, and set $\mathcal J=\mathfrak c\otimes\OO_N(cD)$. Then $\mathcal J$ is a reflexive ideal in $\OO_N$, and its restriction embeds in $\OO_D$ with finite-length quotient. Write $\ell$ for that length and put $\delta=p_a(D)-g(Y)$. Without any smoothness or Gorenstein assumption on $N$, one has \[ 2g(Y)-2=ap\,Y^2+\frac{\ell+2\delta}{p-1}, \qquad \ell\geq0,\quad\delta\geq0. \] If $2g(Y)-2=ap\,Y^2$, then $D$ is smooth, $N$ is regular near $D$, $\mathcal J=\OO_N$, and $N$ is Gorenstein. If $N$ is singular at a point of $D$, then $2g(Y)-2-apY^2\geq2/(p-1)$.

statement: In the equality case, the divided logarithmic differential has a finite zero scheme of length c2(X)+apY², its inverse image is the Fitting singular scheme, and the locally free tangent sheaf has Chern number -aD².
exact_statement: \label{prop:normalized-mup-singularity-defect} Keep the notation of Proposition~\ref{prop:normalized-mup-conductor}, and suppose that \[ 2g(Y)-2=apY^2. \] Let $\omega$ be the logarithmic differential of $M$, put $m=pa$, and let $s_Y$ be the canonical section of $\OO_X(Y)$. The section \[ \theta=\omega/s_Y^m\in H^0\bigl(X,\Omega^1_{X/k}(-mY)\bigr) \] has a finite zero scheme $Z$ disjoint from $Y$, and \begin{equation}\label{eq:normalized-mup-zero-length} \operatorname{length}_k Z=c_2(X)+apY^2=c_2(X)+aD^2. \end{equation} The singular subscheme of $N$ defined by $\operatorname{Fitt}_2(\Omega^1_{N/k})$ is $N\times_X Z$. Its length is $p\operatorname{length}_k Z$, and $N$ is smooth if and only if $Z$ is empty. The tangent sheaf $T_N$ is a vector bundle of rank two, even when $N$ is singular. The infinitesimal action of Corollary~\ref{cor:normalized-equality-torsor} gives an exact sequence of vector bundles \begin{equation}\label{eq:normalized-mup-tangent-sequence} 0\longrightarrow\OO_N(-aD)\longrightarrow T_N \longrightarrow\omega_N^{-1}(aD)\longrightarrow0, \end{equation} and \begin{equation}\label{eq:normalized-mup-tangent-chern} \deg c_2(T_N)=-aD^2. \end{equation} If $a=1$, then $Z$ is nonempty, so $c_2(X)+pY^2\geq1$.

statement: The exceptional K3 normalization has a uniquely split tangent bundle, s+2 global derivations with scalar square, rational quotients, and degree-two rational domination.
exact_statement: \label{prop:k3-picard-derivations} In the non-almost-ruled alternative of Proposition~\ref{prop:normalized-mup-ekedahl}, put $s=Y^2$. Every nonzero global derivation $v$ satisfies $v^2=c_vv$ for some $c_v\in k$. Its normal quotient is rational. There are dominant purely inseparable rational maps from rational surfaces to $N$ of degree two and to $X$ of degree four.

statement: A smooth integral purely inseparable horizontal multisection of a smooth projective quasi-elliptic surface over a positive-genus base has nonpositive self-intersection.
exact_statement: Let $k$ be algebraically closed of characteristic $p=2$ or $3$, and let $f:S\to C$ be a quasi-elliptic fibration from a smooth projective integral surface to a smooth projective integral curve. Thus $f_*\OO_S=\OO_C$ and the generic fibre is a regular geometrically integral curve of arithmetic genus one that is not smooth. Let $R\subset S$ be a smooth integral horizontal curve for which $R\to C$ is purely inseparable of degree $q=p^e\geq2$. If $g=g(C)$, then \[ R^2\leq\left(2-\frac{5q}{3}\right)(g-1). \] In particular, $R$ is not ample when $g\geq1$. The fibration need not be relatively minimal.

statement: A finite intersection of kernels of homomorphisms associated with global line bundles on the geometric closed fibre forces a local-base abelian torsor to be a scheme.
exact_statement: Let $S$ be the spectrum of a noetherian local ring, with closed point $s$, let $A/S$ be an abelian scheme, and let $Q$ be an fppf $A$-torsor algebraic space. Choose a geometric point $\bar s$ above $s$ and a point $q_0\in Q_{\bar s}$. For a line bundle $M$ on $Q$, put $L_M=\tau_{q_0}^*(M|_{Q_{\bar s}})$, where $\tau_{q_0}:A_{\bar s}\to Q_{\bar s}$ is the torsor isomorphism. If there are finitely many line bundles $M_1,\ldots,M_n$ on $Q$ such that \[ \bigcap_{i=1}^n\ker\phi_{L_{M_i}}\subset A_{\bar s} \] is finite, then $Q$ is a scheme.

statement: A base-flat fibrewise rank-one torsion-free sheaf on a smooth proper surface family is a line bundle tensored with the ideal of a finite flat subscheme.
exact_statement: Let $S$ be locally noetherian, and let $Y\to S$ be a smooth algebraic space of relative dimension two with geometrically integral fibres. Let $\mathcal F$ be a coherent $\OO_Y$-module, flat over $S$, whose restriction to every geometric fibre is torsion-free of rank one. There are an invertible sheaf $\mathcal D$ and a closed subspace $Z\subset Y$, flat over $S$ with zero-dimensional fibres, fitting into an exact sequence \[ 0\longrightarrow\mathcal F\longrightarrow\mathcal D \longrightarrow\mathcal D\otimes\OO_Z\longrightarrow0. \] The first map remains injective on every fibre. If $Y\to S$ is proper, then $Z\to S$ is finite locally free.

statement: A projective scheme modification of an abelian-surface torsor with proper flat geometrically integral source family forces the torsor to be a scheme.
exact_statement: Let $S$ be an arbitrary scheme, let $A$ be an abelian $S$-scheme of relative dimension two, and let $Q$ be an fppf $A$-torsor algebraic space. Let $X$ be a scheme, proper, flat and finitely presented over $S$, with geometrically integral fibres. Suppose that $f:X\to Q$ is a projective $S$-morphism and that one of the following conditions holds: \begin{enumerate} \item every geometric fibre $f_{\bar s}:X_{\bar s}\to Q_{\bar s}$ is birational; \item there is a dense open subspace $V\subset Q$ such that $f^{-1}V\to V$ is an isomorphism. \end{enumerate} Then $Q$ is a scheme.

statement: The band and its canonical decompositions [Proved under the stated Tate hypothesis; the group calculation is unconditional]. Put \[ \Gamma=W(p)=\{\lambda\in\overline\Q^{\times}:\ p^N\lambda\text{ is integral for some }N\geq0, \quad |\tau\lambda|=p^{w(\lambda)/2}\ (\tau),\quad w(\lambda)\in\Z\}. \] Then $G=D(\Gamma)$, where $D$ is the contravariant equivalence from Galois modules to groups of multiplicative type. Let $\mu_\infty$ be the group of roots of unity, $\Gamma^0=\ker(w)$, and $M=\Gamma^0/\mu_\infty$. There are canonical identifications \begin{align*} X^*(G^0)&=\Gamma/\mu_\infty=M\oplus\Z[\sqrt p],\\ G/G^0&=\widehat\Z,\qquad G^0=H^0\times\Gm, \qquad H^0=D(M),\\ X^*(H)&=\Gamma'=\Gamma/\langle\mu_\infty,p\rangle =M\oplus\Z/2\Z,\\ H&=H^0\times\mu_2. \end{align*} The maps $\epsilon:G\to\Gm$ and $i:\Gm\to G$ have character maps $1\mapsto p$ and $\lambda\mapsto w(\lambda)$, respectively, and $\epsilon i(t)=t^2$. The restriction $i|_{\mu_2}$ splits $H$. The group $M$ is a $\Q$-vector space, and complex conjugation acts as $-1$. Consequently $H^0$ is a protorus, an inverse limit of tori compact at the real place. It is not an algebraic torus of finite type.

statement: Dictionary between gerbes and groupoids [Proved]. Let $\mathscr P$ be a $P$-gerbe over $\Q$ and choose $x\in\mathscr P(\overline\Q)$. Its groupoid over $\Spec(\overline\Q)\times_{\Spec\Q}\Spec(\overline\Q)$ is the sheaf of isomorphisms between the two pullbacks of $x$. Its diagonal kernel is $P_{\overline\Q}$. For each place $v$, a realization functor induces a morphism of such groupoids; its map on kernels is $1\to P_{\Q_\ell}$ for $\ell\ne p$, $D(\Q)\to P_{\Q_p}$ at $p$, and $\Gm\to P_\R$ at infinity. Conversely fpqc descent for this groupoid recovers $\mathscr P$. Changing $x$ changes the groupoid by an isomorphism whose conjugacy ambiguity is exactly the change of the chosen identification of objects.

statement: The bare category and the category with local data [Bare classification proved; classification of arbitrary framed local data by the bare class refuted]. statement: The global class really is locally determined [Proved unconditionally for the band in Theorem~\ref{A:band]. } For $H^0=D(M)$ one has \[ \Sha^2(\Q,H^0)=0,\qquad H^2(\R,H^0)=0. \] For a finite place $v$, there is a canonical identification \[ H^2(\Q_v,H^0)=\Hom\bigl(M^{G_{\Q_v}},\Q/\Z\bigr). \] More precisely, for any cofinal countable increasing sequence of Galois-stable lattices $L_n\subset M$, and $T_n=D(L_n)$, \[ H^2(\Q,H^0)=\varprojlim_n H^2(\Q,T_n) =\varprojlim_n\bigoplus_v H^2(\Q_v,T_n). \] These equalities are conclusions of the proof, not definitions of cohomology. The assertion in A.3 that $\Sha^2$ of an arbitrary protorus is simply a limit of finite-level $\Sha^2$ is not a valid general rule.

statement: What the Lefschetz category actually supplies [Proved unconditionally; equality of its band with $P$ is refuted]. Let $\operatorname{LMot}(\overline{\F}_p)$ be the category generated by abelian varieties, with correspondences generated by divisor classes and with the ordinary Tannakian commutativity constraint. It is a semisimple Tannakian category. Its band is \[ L=\mathop{\prod}_{\Pi}^{\Gm} L_\Pi,\qquad X^*(L_\Pi)=\Z^{\Pi}/ \{f:c f=f,\ \textstyle\sum_{\pi\in\Pi}f(\pi)=0\}, \] where $\Pi$ runs through the geometric simple isogeny classes, identified with Galois orbits of integral weight-one Weil germs. The fibre product identifies every multiplier $[\pi]+[c\pi]$. In particular $L$ is commutative, but it is not the Weil-number protorus $P$ in general. Compatible powers of Frobenius generate a subgroup $P\hookrightarrow L$. Prime-to-$p$ realization and crystalline realization, the weight and Tate morphisms, and the real obstruction are available unconditionally. The claimed identification of the entire character group with Weil numbers, full Frobenius-centralizer faithfulness for arbitrary tensor objects, and the resulting formula for $H^0$ cannot simply be transferred to this smaller-correspondence category.

statement: An explicit extra Frobenius relation [Refuted: $L=P$ for all finite-field Lefschetz motives]. Take $p=5$, $\alpha=1+2i$, and $\beta=(3+\sqrt{-11})/2$. They are Frobenius numbers of the elliptic curves \[ E_\alpha:y^2=x^3+x,\qquad E_\beta:y^2=x^3+4x+2 \quad\text{over }\F_5, \] which have four and three rational points, respectively. Choose $\lambda^2=\alpha\beta$. This is an integral weight-one $5$-Weil number, with irreducible polynomial \[ x^8-6x^6+15x^4-150x^2+625. \] Honda--Tate supplies a simple abelian fourfold $B/\F_5$ with this Frobenius number. In \[ h^1(B)^{\otimes2}\otimes h^1(E_\alpha)^\vee \otimes h^1(E_\beta)^\vee \] there is a geometric eigenline on which Frobenius is $1$, but the Lefschetz group acts nontrivially. Thus its character is zero on $P$ and nonzero on $L$.

statement: The lower endpoint for abelian-type coefficients [Proved]. Let $K$ be a complete discretely valued field with finite residue field of characteristic $p$, and let $\ell\ne p$. Suppose that $V$ is the $\ell$-adic realization of a pure weight-$j$ motive which, after a finite extension of $K$, is a direct summand of tensor constructions on the $H^1$ of abelian varieties, their duals and Tate twists. Finite-image Artin factors are allowed. Then the eigenvalues of geometric Frobenius on $V^{I_K}$ have weights at most $j$. In particular this holds for the local realizations of pure absolute-Hodge or motivated motives of abelian type over number fields. The bound is attained for good reduction.

statement: Classification of the allowed zero-cycles on an abelian variety [Proved over every algebraically closed field]. Let $A/F$ be an abelian variety over an algebraically closed field of any characteristic, and let $o\in\CH_0(A)_\Q$ have degree one. The following are equivalent: \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)] \item all the cohomological point-and-diagonal relations hold in $T_k^{\CH}(A,o)$ for every $k$; \item $\Delta_*o=o\boxtimes o$ in $\CH_0(A\times A)_\Q$; \item $o=[a]$ in $\CH_0(A)_\Q$ for a point $a\in A(F)$. \end{enumerate} The point is unique modulo torsion in $A(F)$. In particular, specifying the origin is sufficient but is not necessary for the requested lifting.

statement: A gauged special bivariant system [Definition, with the corrected exchange axiom]. Over a characteristic-zero field $L$, a special bivariant system assigns to every finite set $I$ a finite-dimensional graded-commutative algebra $A(I)$, with $A(\varnothing)=L$, a trace $\kappa_I$ of degree $-D|I|$, and a perfect trace pairing. For a map $\alpha:I\to J$ it assigns \[ \alpha^*:A(I)\longrightarrow A(J),\qquad \alpha_*:A(J)\longrightarrow A(I). \] The first is a unital graded algebra homomorphism; the second has degree $D(|I|-|J|)$. Pullbacks compose covariantly in maps of indexing sets, pushforwards contravariantly, and \[ \kappa_I(\alpha_*x\,a)=\kappa_J(x\,\alpha^*a),\qquad \alpha_*(x\alpha^*a)=\alpha_*x\,a. \] For disjoint unions the exterior-product maps $A(I)\otimes A(J)\to A(I\amalg J)$ are isomorphisms compatible with associativity, units, traces, and the Koszul symmetry. These maps are compatible with pullback and pushforward. The exchange axiom is base change for product squares (a projection pulled back by a map on the other factor); arbitrary self-intersection squares are not included. The gauge is the chosen trace, not a quotient up to multiplication by a scalar. A morphism in the bivariant category from $A$ to $B$ is a pair $(f^*,f_*)$, with $f^*:B\to A$ a unital graded algebra map and $f_*:A\to B$ its trace adjoint. On powers these maps are tensor powers and satisfy the corresponding pullback and pushforward compatibilities. The adjoint need not preserve the unit.

statement: The precise conditional and categorical boundary [Proved sufficient-conjecture reduction; the general equivalence is open]. The hypothesis is a published, independently formulated independence-of-homological-equivalence conjecture over $\overline{\F}_p$, not a renamed version of C.6. The result proves only its implication to the stated C.6 assertion. It does not prove the converse: realizing an arbitrary finite-field correspondence as local monodromy of a number-field variety would require an additional geometric construction which is not supplied. The representative must be algebraic and homogeneous, but only its cohomological action must be idempotent. Inspecting the proof, idempotence is used on the realization and its $E_2$ graded pieces, never in the Chow group. No extension to an arbitrary absolute-Hodge, motivated, or numerical projector is inferred from Saito's algebraic-correspondence construction alone. The following theorem treats motivated projectors by an additional finite algebraic-and-Lefschetz construction. Thus this proposition gives a second exact sufficient hypothesis, alongside the purity reduction, but does not satisfy the requested general-motive proof or a two-way named-conjecture equivalence.

statement: A purity reduction for homogeneous Chow motives [Proved conditional implication]. Let $K$ be a number field, $v$ a finite place with residue field of cardinality $q$, and $p$ its residue characteristic. Let $M=(X,e,m)$ be a rational Chow motive over $K$, where $X$ is smooth projective of dimension $d$ and the rational algebraic projector $e\in\CH^d(X\times_KX)_{\Q}$ acts only in cohomological degree $i$. Suppose that, for one prime $\ell_0\ne p$, the representation $M_{\ell_0}$ is unramified at $v$ and the eigenvalues of geometric Frobenius on it are algebraic numbers all of whose complex conjugates have one common absolute value. Then $M_\ell$ is unramified at $v$ for every $\ell\ne p$. In particular, the asserted independence follows for such a motive if the weight--monodromy conjecture holds for $H^i(X_{\overline{K_v}},\Q_{\ell_0})$: its unramified direct summand $M_{\ell_0}$ is then pure of weight $i-2m$.

statement: Exact lifting for covariant polynomial tensors [Proved]. Let $V_0=\Q^{u|v}$, let $L_0$ be an even line, and set $G=\operatorname{GL}(V_0)\times\mathbb G_m$. Fix $q\geq1$ and put \[ W=\bigoplus_{m=1}^{q}(V_0^\vee)^{\otimes m}\otimes L_0, \qquad R=\mathcal O(W) =\operatorname{Sym}_{\mathrm{super}} \left(\bigoplus_{m=1}^{q}V_0^{\otimes m}\otimes L_0^{-1}\right). \] Grade $R$ by total $V_0$-degree $r$ and number $d$ of form factors. Every $R_{r,d}$ is finite and is a direct summand of a finite sum of copies of $V_0^{\otimes r}\otimes L_0^{-d}$. If $I\subset R$ is a $G$-stable ideal and $E\subset I$ is a finite homogeneous $G$-submodule generating $I$, then \begin{equation} \Hom_G\bigl(V_0^{\otimes r}L_0^{-d},(E\otimes R)_{r,d}\bigr) \longrightarrow \Hom_G\bigl(V_0^{\otimes r}L_0^{-d},I_{r,d}\bigr) \end{equation} is surjective. The same conclusion holds after a finite direct sum in the source. All the splittings and lifts can be found by rational linear algebra.

statement: The degree-one and semistable abelian-type cases [Proved in the stated cases]. Let $K$ be a number field, $v$ a finite place of residue characteristic $p$, and $\ell\ne p$. For $M=h^1(A)$, unramifiedness of $M_\ell$ at $v$ is independent of $\ell$ and is equivalent to good reduction of $A$. Then unramifiedness of $M_\ell$ at $v$ is independent of $\ell\ne p$. The same conclusion holds for potentially CM motives without a semistability assumption.

statement: The remaining general-motive claim [Unresolved in the general motivic category]. Theorem~\ref{c:ell-independence-abelian} settles the whole abelian-type assertion, including its finite-inertia descent. The direct argument from an arbitrary original generator would still be invalid: $\bigwedge^2H^1(E)=\Q_\ell(-1)$ is unramified at a place of residue characteristic different from $\ell$, even when $E$ has bad reduction. The weak-lift lemma and the trace argument are what repair that inference. For Andr\'e motivated motives, Theorem~\ref{c:motivated-unramified-rank-reduction} supplies a second named sufficient hypothesis: independence of homological equivalence for rational cycles on all smooth projective varieties over $\overline{\F}_p$. It controls the monodromy ranks and the finite inertia action, but remains conditional on that finite-field conjecture. Corollary~\ref{c:motivated-abelian-strata-unramified} gives the stated unconditional geometric case only when all auxiliary strata have the required algebraic abelian-type presentations. Neither result proves a converse to the finite-field conjecture. For general motives, another precise named sufficient conjecture is Fontaine's motivic Weil--Deligne compatibility conjecture: \citet[\S2.4.3, Conjecture $C_{\mathrm{WD}}(X,m)$, p.~342, and its motivic formulation in \S2.4.7, pp.~344--345]{c_fontaine1994pst}. The motivic formulation is required to retain the specified projector; compatibility of an unlabelled ambient cohomology representation alone does not identify every prescribed summand. Write the local Weil--Deligne data as $(r_\ell,N_\ell)$, with $r_\ell$ of finite inertial image. On an open subgroup of inertia the actual action is $\exp(t_\ell(\tau)N_\ell)$, where the tame character has infinite image. Consequently \[ M_\ell\text{ is unramified at }v \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad N_\ell=0\ \text{ and }\ r_\ell|_{I_v}=1. \] Both conditions are invariant under extension of coefficient fields and isomorphism of Weil--Deligne representations. Thus Fontaine's compatibility, which only requires isomorphism after common coefficient extension and not a chosen rational form, implies the requested independence. His weaker monodromy-graded character formulation in \S2.4.5 also suffices: the characters at the identity determine whether the monodromy filtration is concentrated in degree zero, equivalently $N=0$; after that, the finite inertia character detects triviality. This proves an implication, not the exact equivalence requested in the question. Algebraically, the representations trivial on a subgroup $J\subset G$ detect its closed normal closure, not the whole inertia representation. Even all tensor tests do not formally recover the nilpotent's Jordan type: in $\mathfrak{sl}_3$, both $E_{12}$ and $E_{12}+E_{23}$ act nontrivially in every nontrivial algebraic representation, since the differential's kernel is an ideal in the simple Lie algebra. Their ranks differ. The accompanying notes give compatible abstract Weil--Deligne pairs and a matrix certificate; no such pair is asserted to come from a global motive, and it is not a motivic counterexample. The theorem of \citet[Theorem 5.1]{c_commelin2019} concerns abelian motives and quasi-compatibility; by itself it does not supply finite-inertia traces for an arbitrary motive at a bad place. Similarly the $G$-valued expectation of \citet[Conjecture 1.1]{c_kisinzhou2025} is stronger than the asserted triviality test. A proof in the general motivic category, or an exact equivalence with a published named conjecture of precisely the required strength, remains an outstanding assertion, recorded separately from the now proved abelian-type theorem.

statement: An explicit abelian-surface counterexample at $p=2$ [Proved refutation of the unrestricted criterion]. Let $k=\overline\F_2$ and \[ R=W(k)[[u,v]]/(2-uv),\qquad K=\operatorname{Frac}(R),\qquad \mathfrak m=(u,v). \] Consider the elliptic schemes \begin{align*} E_1:&\quad Y^2Z+(u+v^2)XYZ+YZ^2=X^3,\\ E_2:&\quad Y^2Z+(v+u^2)XYZ+YZ^2=X^3, \end{align*} with origins $[0:1:0]$, and put $A=E_1\times_R E_2$. The sections \[ P_v=[-v:1:v^3]\in E_1(R),\qquad P_u=[-u:1:u^3]\in E_2(R) \] have order two on the generic fibre. statement: A finite exterior-power test for monodromy purity [Proved]. Let $V$ be a finite-dimensional mixed Frobenius module over $\Q_\ell$, with integral weights and a nilpotent operator $N:V\to V(-1)$. Fix an integer $m$. We use geometric Frobenius $\phi$ and $\phi N\phi^{-1}=q^{-1}N$. Suppose \[ \sum_w w\dim V_w=m\dim V, \] where $V=\bigoplus_wV_w$ is the decomposition by Frobenius weights; Frobenius need not be semisimple. Let $h$ be the largest length of a Jordan string of $N$, with $h=0$ if $V=0$. Then the following conditions are equivalent: \begin{enumerate} \item $V$ is pure of weight $m$ in the weight--monodromy sense; \item for every $1\leq r\leq h$, all weights of $\ker(N:\bigwedge^r V\to\bigwedge^r V(-1))$ are at most $rm$. \end{enumerate} Here the exterior power is the ordinary exterior power of vector spaces, and $N$ acts on it as a derivation. The determinant hypothesis holds in particular when $V$ has a nondegenerate Frobenius-equivariant pairing $V\otimes V\to\Q_\ell(-m)$.

statement: Scope of the finite criterion [Proved scope clarification; the arbitrary-pair classification remains unresolved]. Theorem~\ref{c:finite-even-criterion} applies to arbitrary cup-product algebras with pure-even cohomology, not only to surfaces. It gives a finite algebraic construction of the cycle conditions, without claiming to decide their rational equivalence by computation. For mixed cohomology the direct use of $\operatorname{GL}_{a|b}$ would require exactness of its invariant functor, which fails. Theorem~\ref{c:finite-super-criterion} replaces that step by projective lifting and an external algebraic parity correspondence. Corollary~\ref{c:finite-weil-criterion} also separates finite existence over an arbitrary Weil coefficient field from effective construction with specified coefficient data. Theorem~\ref{c:finite-unconditional-criterion} subsequently removes the sign hypothesis by first passing to scalar forms in the covariant polynomial category. These finite criteria do not decide the resulting Chow vanishings. The unrestricted classification of all $(X,o)$ therefore remains distinct from the specific K3 obstruction proved below.

statement: A finite cycle criterion when the cohomology is even [Proved in the pure-even case]. Let $X/\C$ be smooth projective and connected, with $H^{\rm odd}(X,\Q)=0$, let $n=\dim X>0$, and let $o\in\CH^n(X)_\Q$ have degree $1$. Put $d=\dim_\Q H^*(X,\Q)=\chi(X)$. There is a finite list of rational tensor expressions $P_1,\ldots,P_s$, constructed by the procedure below from the rational cup-product table and trace of $X$, for which the following criterion is necessary and sufficient for all the relations of Theorem~\ref{c:matrix-presentation} to hold in rational Chow groups on every power: \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)] \item $c_n(T_X)=d\,o$ and $\Delta_*o=o\boxtimes o$; \item $\bigwedge^{d+1}h(X)=0$ in rational Chow motives; \item $P_a(h(X),\mu,1,\operatorname{tr},o,\beta^{-1})=0$ for $1\leq a\leq s$. \end{enumerate} Here $\mu$ is the small-diagonal multiplication, $\operatorname{tr}:h(X)\to\Q(-n)$ is the trace, $\beta=\operatorname{tr}\circ\mu$, and $\beta^{-1}:\Q(-n)\to h(X)\otimes h(X)$ is its inverse pairing. Every condition is the vanishing of a specified finite linear combination of correspondence diagrams. Subject to (i), each can equivalently be written as a finite list of cycles in the requested point-and-diagonal rings. The construction uses finite-dimensional polynomial algebra, so is a finite criterion, rather than one separate test for each power of $X$.

statement: The finite-field analytic/algebraic distinction [Proved counterexample to the one-dimensional algebraic reading]. Let $E/\F_5$ have equation $y^2=x^3-x$. It is smooth since its discriminant $64$ is nonzero modulo $5$. It has eight rational points, so geometric Frobenius has polynomial $T^2+2T+5$ on $H^1$ and eigenvalues $\pi=-1+2i$, $\bar\pi=-1-2i$. Its algebraic Frobenius torus is \[ T=\operatorname{Res}_{\Q(i)/\Q}\Gm, \qquad\dim T=2. \] Indeed the two primes of $\Q(i)$ above $5$ give valuations $(1,0)$ and $(0,1)$ on $(\pi,\bar\pi)$; hence $\pi^a\bar\pi^b=1$ implies $a=b=0$. There is consequently no character cutting out a proper algebraic subgroup containing Frobenius. The adjoint action of $T$ is trivial, so its whole Lie algebra is algebraic, but it is two-dimensional. On the other hand, for $\ell=3$ a suitable positive power of $\pi$ belongs to $1+3\Z_3[i]$. The analytic closure of the cyclic Frobenius subgroup has Lie algebra $\Q_3\log(\pi^N)$, of dimension one. The logarithm is nonzero because $\pi$ is not a root of unity. This is the distinction made by Serre in his letter of 8 September 1964, printed p.~202 of \citet{c_grothendieckserre}. Thus ``tout'' on 12:59 is valid for the adjoint Lie algebra of a commutative algebraic motivic band, as in the finite-field category under the Tate hypotheses of Part A; the accompanying identification with a single $\Q(0)$ does not describe that algebraic Lie object. Treating an analytic one-dimensional image as the motivic Lie algebra is an error, not an unconditional proof of a finite-field motivic assertion.

statement: Corrected bounds and the margin question [Proved in the stated arithmetic finite-type setting]. Let $f:X\to Y$ be separated of finite type, with $X$ regular and $X,Y$ of finite type over $\Z[1/\ell]$ or over a field of characteristic different from $\ell$. Fix $y\in Y$ and put $n=d_y(f)$. Let $F$ be strictly special of weight $j$, in the dimension-normalized sense of the insertion on 12:111: it is a direct summand of $R^jg_*\Q_\ell$ for a smooth projective $g$ of relative dimension $j$. Set $\epsilon=1$ if no component of local dimension $n$ maps to $y$, and set $\epsilon=0$ otherwise. Put \[ L=\max(0,i-n+\epsilon),\qquad U=\min(i,n)+j. \] The stalk $(R^if_*F)_{\bar y}$ is effectively admissible, with a filtration into pieces of weights $w$ and levels bounded simultaneously by \begin{equation} 2L\leq w\leq2U, \qquad \operatorname{level}\leq\min\{w-2L,\,2U-w\}. \end{equation} Consequently \[ \operatorname{weight}\leq2\min(i,n)+2j, \qquad \operatorname{level}\leq \begin{cases} \min(i,2n-i)+j,&\epsilon=0,\\ \min(i,2n-1-i)+j,&\epsilon=1. \end{cases} \] For an open immersion at a boundary point, $\epsilon=1$. The condition that $f$ have relative dimension at most $n-1$ near $y$ also implies $\epsilon=1$. Hence the margin's replacement by $n-1$ is valid with its stated extra condition, since $\min(i,2n-1-i)\leq\min(i,n-1)$. Without that condition the corrected general bound is at most $\min(i,n)+j$, and Proposition~\ref{c:level-counterexample} prevents replacing $n$ by $n-1$ universally.

statement: The local dimension on 12:120 [Definition, with the punctured-trait correction verified]. For a finite-type morphism $f:X\to Y$ of universally catenary noetherian schemes we use \[ d_y(f)=\sup_{\substack{x\in X\\ f(x)\text{ generalizes }y}} \left\{\operatorname{trdeg}_{k(f(x))}k(x) +\dim\overline{\{f(x)\}}^{\,\Spec\mathcal O_{Y,y}}\right\}. \] The closure in the second summand is taken in the local base. This is the dimension function, normalized to be zero at $y$, pulled back to $X$. It is the formula visible in the supplied transcription, whose notation for the local spectrum is uncertain. It measures local source dimension, not maximum fibre dimension: for $\Spec K\hookrightarrow\Spec R$ with $R$ a discrete valuation ring and $y$ its closed point it equals $1$, although all nonempty fibres have dimension zero. After an equidimensional localization of the source and a compactification, its maximum is the local dimension of that compactification. Regular alterations preserve this maximum. The dimension-function convention and the corresponding local cohomological interpretation are made precise in \citet[\S1.1.1 and Corollary 1.2.2]{c_pillonistroh2014}.

statement: Finite-prime approximation by a number-field motive [Proved; a globalization reduction, not a proof of general independence]. Let $K/\Q_p$ be finite, and let $M$ be a homogeneous rational motive over $K$ in either the algebraic homological category or Andr\'e's motivated category. For every nonempty finite set $\Sigma$ of primes different from $p$ there exist a number field $F\subset K$, a place $w$ of $F$ with $F_w=K$, and a homogeneous motive $M'$ of the same kind and weight over $F$, such that \[ H_\ell(M')|_{G_{F_w}}\simeq H_\ell(M) \qquad(\ell\in\Sigma) \] as representations of $G_K$, under the specified identification $F_w=K$. Consequently, universal independence of unramifiedness for these motives over number fields is equivalent to the same assertion over all finite extensions of $\Q_p$, for all $p$. The number-field approximation may depend on $\Sigma$.

statement: Explicit dimension algorithms for projective spaces and abelian varieties [Proved]. The following finite integer matrices determine every dimension by ordinary exact rational rank; in particular they give a uniform computable answer for every $n,g,k,d$, with no geometric unknown in their entries. For $X=\mathbb P^n$, the columns are $P\in\mathcal P_k$ with $d(P)=d$, and the rows are $(a_1,\ldots,a_k)\in\{0,\ldots,n\}^k$ with $\sum a_i=nd$. The entry is $1$ precisely when \[ a_i=n\quad(i\in P(0)\setminus\{0\}),\qquad \sum_{i\in B}a_i=n(|B|-1)\quad(0\notin B), \] and is zero otherwise. Its rank is $\dim T_k[d]$. For an abelian variety of dimension $g>0$, use the exterior algebra on the $2gk$ symbols $e_{i,a}$, ordered lexicographically. statement: Products and the failure of the tautological parity converse [Product assertion proved; the proposed parity converse refuted]. Let $(X,o_X)$ and $(Y,o_Y)$ be pointed smooth projective complex varieties for which all the requested point-and-diagonal relations hold in rational Chow groups on every power. Then the same is true of $(X\times Y,o_X\boxtimes o_Y)$. statement: The R7 hypotheses used in this Part [Used and rechecked, with its internal-Hom counterexample confirmed]. We checked the proof in the supplied reading, \S\S2.1--2.3, against 12:150--158. The conditional construction there is not a construction of a faithful realization on all Chow motives: it first quotients by the chosen homological equivalence, assumes its equality with numerical equivalence and the stated positivity, and then takes the semisimple envelope. Our Chow assertions above do not use this conditional passage. In particular it cannot be used to kill the homologically zero K3 determinant. The sign correction is forced by the cross-product formula: interchanging a class of degree $a$ with one of degree $b$ multiplies it by $(-1)^{ab}$. Thus the original realization is symmetric into graded vector spaces with that commutativity constraint. This is the convention used in our Frobenius equivalence. A level filtration by thick subcategories yields a direct-sum level decomposition only when the ambient category is semisimple; then we group the simple constituents according to their least allowed twist. Thickness alone gives no splitting of extensions. The geometric level definition of C.4 therefore does not assert a canonical splitting or identify itself with coniveau. The internal-Hom error of 12:156 already occurs in the semisimple effective Tate category with objects finite sums of $\Q(-a)$, $a\geq0$. For every effective $Z$, \[ \Hom(Z\otimes\Q(-1),\Q)=0. \] Hence the effective internal Hom from $\Q(-1)$ to $\Q$ is the zero object. After adjoining all Tate twists the corresponding internal Hom is $\Q(1)$, which is nonzero. Thus effective internal Homs need not be preserved by Tate inversion. In a rigid tensor category the valid identity is \[ \underline{\Hom}(M,N(-i)) =M^\vee\otimes N(-i) =M^*\otimes N, \qquad M^*=M^\vee(-i). \] Evaluation and coevaluation give these isomorphisms and their inverse maps. Merely postulating the effective object $M^*$ without the duality identities does not prove them. These checks confirm precisely the restrictions of R7 needed here.

statement: A coefficient-independent recursive elimination bound [Proved]. For integers $v,d\geq1$, let $\mathcal B(v,d)$ be the tree of finite sequences $(\alpha_0,\ldots,\alpha_{r-1})$ in $\Z_{\geq0}^v$ satisfying \[ |\alpha_i|\leq d2^i, \qquad \alpha_j\not\leq\alpha_i\quad(0\leq j<i<r), \] where $\leq$ is coordinatewise. This is a finite tree. Its maximum sequence length $\mathcal L(v,d)$ is a total computable integer-valued function. Put \[ \mathcal D(v,d)=d\,2^{\mathcal L(v+1,d)}. \] Over any field, an ideal in $v$ ordinary polynomial variables generated in degrees at most $d$ has, for every monomial order, a Gr\"obner basis in degrees at most $\mathcal D(v,d)$. In particular this bound applies to an elimination order.

statement: Lead C3 with its arithmetic action [Proved under the stated Serre-quotient hypothesis]. Let $K$ be finitely generated over $\Q$, embedded in $\C$, and let $K_0$ be the algebraic closure of $\Q$ in $K$. Suppose that the geometric connected motivic group is pro-reductive, that its maximal protorus quotient is the full Serre protorus $S$, and that the action of $\Gal(\overline K/K)$ on this quotient is the usual action through $\Gal(\overline\Q/K_0)$. If $E$ is the largest CM subfield of $K_0$, then \[ \dim_\Q (\Lie G)^G= \begin{cases}1+[E:\Q]/2,&E\text{ exists},\\1,&K_0\text{ has no CM subfield}. \end{cases} \] These hypotheses hold for the full category of motivated motives of abelian type, including Artin motives. The conclusion concerns the full arithmetic adjoint invariants; the centre of the geometric connected group alone is generally an infinite-dimensional pro-vector space.

statement: One exterior test can miss a failure [Proved formal counterexample; no geometric realization asserted]. Take $K=\Q_2$, $\ell=3$, $q=2$, and an unramified Weil representation over $\Q_3$ with basis $u_6,v_4,x_4,y_2$, subscripts denoting weights. statement: What fails to extend [Proved clarification]. The abstract finite group $D_U$ already extends as $D$. It is its closed immersion into $A_U$, and consequently the exact sequence defining the isogeny, that cannot extend as a finite flat subgroup. Indeed finite locally free group schemes on a punctured regular local surface extend as objects by extending their coordinate bundles to reflexive modules, which are free in dimension two; multiplication and comultiplication extend by Hartogs. Exactness and closed-immersion conditions need not survive. This is the precise content of the finite-subgroup reduction in R6, rather than a failure to extend the abstract group. The source proof of Vasiu--Zink Lemma 27 reverses the Cartier-dual arrows in its printed embedding sentence; our displayed maps avoid that typing error. Lead C5 is therefore valid as an identification of the extension obstruction, while the unrestricted good-reduction claim is false.

statement: What the additional finite criterion settles [Proved scope clarification; unrestricted classification remains unresolved]. Theorem~\ref{c:finite-super-criterion} supplies a finite cycle criterion for mixed cohomology whenever $C^+(X)$ is known. The parity correspondence may be completely external to the requested ring, as it is for the positive pair of Proposition~\ref{c:product-parity}. Thus that example's obstruction to a tautological parity projector does not obstruct this proof. We do not infer $C^+(X)$ from the point-and-diagonal relations. Theorem~\ref{c:finite-unconditional-criterion} below removes that hypothesis from the finite criterion by a different scalar-form construction, which needs no cancellation step. Corollary~\ref{c:finite-weil-criterion} removes the rational Betti restriction for finite existence; its effectiveness qualification is essential. The criterion does not prove the finite Chow vanishing conditions for an arbitrary input variety. The general classification in C.1(c), and in particular the K3 vanishing below, remain open items of this task rather than consequences of finite generation. Condition (ii) retains a precise finite-dimensionality obstruction. Under $C^+_H(X)$ it is equivalent to Kimura finite-dimensionality, by \citet[Theorem~3.2, p.~286]{c_delpadronemazza2005}. To check the input, their Proposition~3.1 applies the partial-trace identity of Theorem~2.1 to an algebraic even projector: all its power traces equal $a$, which lies outside the forbidden contents for the minimal $(a+1)$-by-$(b+1)$ rectangle. The numerical ideal is therefore nilpotent. The same rectangle identity propagates to tensor powers by the super tensor relations, so their numerical ideals are nilpotent as well. The even and odd cohomological projectors lift across these nilpotent ideals, and the cohomologically zero exterior and symmetric projectors on their tensor powers are nilpotent idempotents and hence zero. This gives the Kimura decomposition. Conversely its even and odd dimensions give the rectangular Schur vanishing. In particular, arbitrary Schur-finiteness with an unspecified larger partition is not being substituted for this exact condition.

statement: Rational projective mixed tensors [Proved]. Let $A=\Q^{a|b}$ be a finite supervector space, let $L$ be an even line, and put $G=\operatorname{GL}(A)\times\mathbb G_m$. We use even morphisms and the category $\mathcal R$ of rational $G$-supermodules on which $\epsilon=(\operatorname{diag}(1_a,-1_b),1)$ acts as intrinsic parity. Every finite object $E$ of $\mathcal R$ is a quotient of a finite projective-injective object $P$ of $\mathcal R$. statement: The exact surface-pairing obstruction in dimension three [Proved reduction; the remaining primitive pairing is unresolved]. Let $\mathcal X$ be a projective strictly semistable model of a smooth projective threefold $X$ over a mixed-characteristic local field with finite residue field $k$, and let $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}k$. Write $Y^{(r)}$ for the disjoint union, over $\bar k$, of the $r$-fold intersections of distinct components of its special fibre. All cohomology below has coefficients $\Q_\ell$. Put \[ A=H^2(Y^{(1)}),\quad U=H^2(Y^{(2)}),\quad B=H^0(Y^{(3)})(-1),\quad Z=H^0(Y^{(4)})(-1). \] Use the signed restriction and Gysin maps of the weight spectral sequence, and define \[ \begin{split} R&=\operatorname{im}\bigl(\rho_A:A\longrightarrow U\bigr),\\ K_0&=R\cap\gamma_B \ker\bigl(\rho_B:B\longrightarrow Z\bigr),\\ b(u,v)&=\sum_{S\subset Y^{(2)}}\operatorname{Tr}_S(u_Sv_S) \ \in\Q_\ell(-2). \end{split} \] Then $K_0\subset\operatorname{rad}(b|_R)$, and there is a Galois-equivariant isomorphism \begin{equation} \ker\!\left( N:\operatorname{Gr}^W_4H^3(X_{\bar K})(1) \longrightarrow\operatorname{Gr}^W_2H^3(X_{\bar K}) \right) \simeq \frac{\operatorname{rad}(b|_R)}{K_0}. \end{equation} Consequently the first remaining C.4 endpoint assertion is equivalent to nondegeneracy of the induced form on $R/K_0$. Choose a relatively ample class $L$. The same assertion is equivalent to nondegeneracy of the surface intersection form on \begin{equation} R_{\rm prim} =R\cap \ker\bigl( L:H^2(Y^{(2)})\longrightarrow H^4(Y^{(2)})(1) \bigr). \end{equation} In particular the remaining condition involves only a primitive restriction image in the degree-two cohomology of the double-intersection surfaces. It does not require the unknown nondegeneracy of an additional Gysin image.

statement: The geometric content not removed by the pairing criterion [Proved scope clarification; the primitive nondegeneracy is open]. The radical formula is an exact identification of the existing kernel. The primitive criterion additionally removes the nonprimitive Lefschetz pieces and the Gysin-image condition. It does not prove the resulting nondegeneracy. In particular, containment of a $\Q_\ell$-subspace in the span of divisor classes does not allow one to apply rational Hodge-index positivity to that subspace without establishing its rational origin. For example, over $\Q_5$, choose $\iota^2=-1$ with $\iota\equiv2\pmod5$. The line $\Q_5(1,\iota)$ is isotropic for $-x^2-y^2$ although this form is negative definite over $\Q$. It is stable under the scalar Frobenius $2I$. This is a counterexample to that linear-algebra inference, not a geometric counterexample to weight--monodromy. For the same reason, an isomorphism of a stratum motive with an abelian motive would not alone identify its geometric primitive form with a positive polarization. The conditional image-projector and positivity inputs in \citet[Theorem~0.4 and \S\S4.1--4.3]{c_msaito2003positivity} remain separate hypotheses. We have not silently supplied either input from Frobenius purity or from the 2026 theorem for CM abelian varieties. The corresponding warning is explicit in \citet[submitted version, Remark~4.10 and footnote~3, p.~14]{DMilne2002Polarizations}: equality of motive categories under a Tate hypothesis does not by itself transfer the positivity of the geometric forms. The published-version Theorem~3.3 and Corollary~3.4 concern abelian varieties.

statement: A simple-spectrum substitute for target positivity [Proved sufficient condition; the universal threefold gate remains open]. We keep the threefold semistable notation of Proposition~\ref{c:threefold-pairing-kernel}. After fixing a finite residue field $\F_q$ over which all the components and the chosen ample classes are defined, put \[ V=Y^{(1)},\qquad S=Y^{(2)},\qquad f=\rho:H^2(V,\Q_\ell)\longrightarrow H^2(S,\Q_\ell), \qquad P=H^2(S,\Q_\ell)_{\rm prim}. \] Here primitivity is imposed separately on each surface component, using the restrictions of the fixed ample class. Assume that numerical and $\ell$-adic homological equivalence agree on $V\times S$, and that the characteristic polynomial of geometric Frobenius on the entire space $P$ is squarefree. Then the cup-product pairing on \[ \operatorname{im}(f)\cap P \] is nondegenerate. Consequently the first threefold monodromy condition in Proposition~\ref{c:threefold-pairing-kernel} holds. The squarefreeness condition concerns the union of all surface components, including possible coincidences between their eigenvalues. It is not enough to impose squarefreeness separately on each component. We do not assume the standard conjecture of Hodge type on $S\times S$, or a semisimplicity statement for the source motive. The proof uses algebraic projectors that are idempotent on cohomology; it does not require idempotence modulo rational equivalence.

statement: A uniform arity bound for rational cohomology tables [Proved in the stated rational-table scope]. Suppose the graded Weil cohomology algebra in Theorem~\ref{c:finite-unconditional-criterion} has a rational table. This includes rational Betti cohomology over $\C$. Put $q=2n$, $u=a-1$, $v=b$, $s=u+v$, and \[ M_0=\frac12\sum_{m=1}^{q}\bigl(s^m+(u-v)^m\bigr),\qquad M_1=\frac12\sum_{m=1}^{q}\bigl(s^m-(u-v)^m\bigr). \] Define the following integers using the function of the preceding lemma: \[ O=M_1+4uv,\qquad E=M_0+2(u^2+v^2)+2,\qquad J=2^O,\qquad P=E+J, \] \[ D=\mathcal D(P,q+2),\qquad B_{n,a,b}=\max\{2,\ q+1,\ 2a(b+1),\ q(D-1+M_1)\}. \] Then all the point-and-diagonal cohomological relations hold in rational Chow on all powers if and only if the cycle map is injective on $T_{B_{n,a,b}}^{\CH}(X,o)$. The bound depends only on $(n,a,b)$, and is a total computable integer. It is not a practical or minimal bound, and does not decide the required Chow injectivity.

statement: The coefficient qualification in the uniform bound [Proved scope clarification]. The finite criterion and finite cut-off of Theorem~\ref{c:finite-unconditional-criterion} and Corollary~\ref{c:finite-power-cutoff} apply to an arbitrary Weil field. The displayed bound depending only on $(n,a,b)$ has the additional rational-table hypothesis. For a presented coefficient algebra whose $h$ named generators include every coordinate of $t=(\kappa_1,\ldots,\kappa_q)$, with its exact defining ideal generated in degrees at most $e$, the same proof gives a bound by adding $h$ to $E$ and replacing the generator-degree input $q+2$ by $\max(q+3,e+1)$. The extra one accounts for a structure constant occurring as a variable in an orbit equation. These $h$ coefficient variables are eliminated together with the group variables, so the result is the rational contraction $I_\Q$. We make no uniform rational-contraction claim for unspecified elements of an arbitrary coefficient field. The accompanying exact certificate exhausts only $\mathcal L(1,d)=d+1$ for $1\leq d\leq4$ and $\mathcal L(2,1)=4$, and checks the square-zero elimination mechanism for the explicit super map $z=x$, $\theta_1=\eta$, $\theta_2=x\eta$. It does not evaluate the enormous geometric cut-off above. No closed Dub\'e degree formula is used in its proof.

statement: The universal trait endpoint and weight--monodromy [Proved equivalence; the universal assertions remain unresolved]. Fix a residue characteristic $p$ and a prime $\ell\ne p$. We consider finite extensions $K/\Q_p$, with finite residue field, and geometric $\ell$-adic cohomology. The following universal assertions are equivalent: \begin{enumerate} \item Weight--monodromy holds for $H^j(Z_{\bar K},\Q_\ell)$ for every smooth projective $Z/K$ and every $j\geq0$. \item For every smooth projective $j$-fold $Z/K$, $H^j(Z_{\bar K},\Q_\ell)^{I_K}$ has weights at most $j$. \item The assertion in (2) holds for the generic fibres of projective strictly semistable models over $\mathcal O_K$. \end{enumerate} In (2) the stated space is the closed geometric stalk of $u_*H^j(Z_{\bar K},\Q_\ell)$ for the open immersion $u:\Spec K\hookrightarrow\Spec\mathcal O_K$. Thus it is exactly the dimension-normalized, degree-zero trait endpoint. For an individual $j$-fold, after a finite extension making its inertia action unipotent, it suffices to test the bound $rj$ on $\ker N$ in $\bigwedge^r H^j(Z_{\bar K},\Q_\ell)$ for $1\leq r\leq j+1$. Each such test is a direct-summand test in the middle cohomology $H^{rj}(Z^r_{\bar K},\Q_\ell)$. A failure of weight--monodromy therefore yields a trait-endpoint failure on one of these powers, or on a projective semistable alteration of that power.

statement: The positive purity range [Known, with its application proved]. Let $(R,\mathfrak m)$ be a two-dimensional regular local ring of mixed characteristic $(0,p)$ and let $U=\Spec R\setminus\{\mathfrak m\}$. Every abelian scheme over $U$ extends uniquely over $R$ if $p\notin\mathfrak m^p$. In particular the sufficient absolute ramification bound is $e\leq p-1$, including equality. More generally the same conclusion holds under the complete faithfully flat quotient condition of Vasiu--Zink Theorem 3. If an abelian variety over $K=\operatorname{Frac}(R)$ has good reduction at every height-one prime, these conclusions apply to it. Equivalently, at each such prime one may use the prime-to-residue-characteristic unramifiedness test of the N\'eron--Ogg--Shafarevich criterion.

statement: The separated Milnor quotient is free [Proved intermediate structural consequence; no new universal gate]. In the notation of Proposition~\ref{prop:B-Milnor-divisible-kernel}, set \[ D_\ell(K_n)=\bigcap_{r\ge1}\ell^rK_n^M(K),\qquad M_n(K)=K_n^M(K)/D_\ell(K_n). \] Then $D_\ell(K_n)$ is $\ell$-divisible and $M_n(K)$ is a free abelian group of at most countable rank. Moreover, $D_\ell(K_n)$ is independent of the prime $\ell\ne p$. Thus one canonical quotient $M_n(K)$ induces the canonical isomorphisms of completions \[ \widehat{K_n^M(K)}_\ell\simeq\widehat{M_n(K)}_\ell \qquad(\ell\ne p), \] equivariant for the Frobenius action from any finite-field model. No saturated residue embedding or equivariant permutation basis is asserted, and a common integral module does not by itself make its completed Frobenius spectra independent of the prime.

statement: Relative Brauer finiteness over every finite-type base [Proved equivalence with the universal surface-Tate assertion]. Assume the equivalent assertions of Theorem~\ref{thm:B-all-bases-Brauer-units}. Conversely, the universal assertion for those curve families implies divisor Tate for all smooth projective surfaces over finite extensions of \(\F_p\).

statement: Canonical surfaces suffice, with arbitrary numerical thresholds [Proved strict test-class reduction; the restricted Tate conjecture remains unresolved]. Fix a finite field \(k\), a prime \(\ell\ne\operatorname{char}k\), an integer \(N\ge1\), and a real number \(\varepsilon>0\). Divisor Tate at \(\ell\) for every smooth projective geometrically integral surface over \(k\) is equivalent to its restriction to surfaces \(Y/k\) with \[ H^1(Y,\mathcal O_Y)=0,\qquad \omega_Y\text{ very ample}, \qquad K_Y^2\ge N,\qquad p_g(Y)\ge N, \] and, if desired, the simultaneous extra conditions \[ c_2(Y)>0,\qquad \left|\frac{K_Y^2}{c_2(Y)}-1\right|<\varepsilon. \] Here \(c_2(Y)=\deg c_2(T_Y)\). Thus the preceding universal Brauer and abelian-torsor gates can be confined to an intrinsic class of canonically embedded surfaces of general type. This does not assert Tate for those surfaces.

statement: A precise conjectural replacement for requirement 4) [Conjectural formulation; its stated specializations are proved below]. The following is a comparison \emph{package}, rather than a claim that Bloch--Kato's degree-one conjecture already constructs an absolute category. statement: A fully specified nonzero degree-two group on 12:78 [Proved]. Let \(C/\F_2\) be the good reduction of the displayed \(X_0(11)\) model, and let \(A=C\times C\to C\) be its constant Jacobian scheme. Take \(\ell=3\). Direct enumeration gives \(\#C(\F_2)=5\), so Frobenius on \(V_3C\) has polynomial \(t^2+2t+2\). Its two roots are distinct, and the centralizer of a companion matrix has dimension two. Kummer, the constant-case result just proved, and Hochschild--Serre give \[ V_3H^2_{\et}(C,A) \simeq H^2_{\Bcts}(C,V_3A) \simeq H^1_{\Bcts}(\bar C,V_3A)_\Gamma \simeq\End_{\F_2}(C)\otimes\Q_3, \] of dimension two. The geometric degree-two term has weight one, so contributes no invariants; in the degree-one term, \(H^1(\bar C,\Q_3)\otimes V_3C=(V_3C)^\vee\otimes V_3C\). Semisimplicity identifies its coinvariants with its invariants, and Tate's Main Theorem identifies the latter with endomorphisms. The point count and exact centralizer calculation are reproduced in \texttt{part\_b/code/finite\_field\_checks.py}. This verifies the intended nonvanishing in R6. If a dual Tate module is replaced in the transcription by the Tate module of the dual abelian variety, a twist must be retained: \((V_\ell J)^\vee=V_\ell(J^t)(-1)\). An integral isomorphism also cannot be read off from a displayed \(\Q_\ell\)-vector-space calculation without tracking finite Kummer kernels.

statement: A certified irregular-prime instance [Proved by a complete arithmetic certificate]. Let \(L=\Q(\zeta_{37}+\zeta_{37}^{-1})\), with \(\zeta_{37}\) a primitive thirty-seventh root of unity. The preserved PARI/GP computation constructs its degree-eighteen real cyclotomic polynomial, returns the trivial computed class group, and returns \(1\) from \texttt{bnfcertify(B,1)}. The documented meaning of that flag is that the actual class group is a quotient of the computed group; since the latter is trivial, the actual class group is trivial \cite{BPariClass2026}. statement: The counterexample in R6, without a BSD assumption [Refuted; corrected statement proved]. Take \[ E=X_0(11):\quad y^2+y=x^3-x^2-10x-20. \] Its discriminant is \(-11^5\), its conductor is \(11\), and it has good reduction over \(\Z[1/11]\). The reproducible algebraic two-descent in \texttt{part\_b/code/x011.gp} gives \[ \operatorname{ellrank}(E)=[0,0,0,[]],\qquad E(\Q)_{\rm tors}\cong\Z/5, \] with torsion generator \((5,5)\). Thus its rank is certified to be zero; this uses no analytic-rank computation or BSD. PARI's official description of \texttt{ellrank} specifies that the lower and upper bounds and the two-descent data are unconditional. The model of \(X_0(11)\) is also derived explicitly in Elkies's October~13, 2021 lecture notes~\cite{BElkies2021,BPari2026}. For any prime \(\ell\), let \(X=\Spec\Z[1/(11\ell)]\). The Kummer sequence gives \[ 0\longrightarrow E(\Q)\otimes\Q_\ell \longrightarrow H^1_{\Bcts}(X,V_\ell E) \longrightarrow V_\ell H^1_{\et}(X,E)\longrightarrow0. \] The first term is zero. The global Euler characteristic of \(V_\ell E\), whose complex-conjugation eigenspaces both have dimension one, is \(-1\). Its \(H^0\) is zero, so \(\dim H^1=1+\dim H^2\ge1\). It follows that \(H^1_{\et}(X,E)[\ell^\infty]\) is infinite for every \(\ell\). For \(\ell=2\) the zero two-Selmer calculation additionally gives \(\Sha(E)[2]=0\), hence \(\Sha(E)[2^\infty]=0\); then (B.20) gives exact corank one. All hypotheses of the boxed assertion on 12:75 hold, including invertibility of \(\ell\) on \(X\), and its conclusion fails.

statement: Why the positive-degree argument retains its regularity hypothesis [Proved counterexample to an extension beyond the stated manuscript scope]. There is a reduced projective surface \(S/\F_2\) and a smooth proper genus-one scheme \(f:X\to S\) for which every global line bundle has relative degree zero. Thus the positive-degree class used in Proposition~\ref{prop:B-relative-curve} cannot be asserted on an arbitrary singular base. This example does not assert that the Brauer quotient is infinite. Take \[ E:\ y^2z+yz^2+x^3+x^2z=0\ \subset T=\mathbf P^2_{\F_2}, \qquad O=[0:1:0], \qquad S=T\amalg_E T. \] The derivatives of the cubic are \(x^2,z^2,y^2+x^2\), with no common projective zero, so \(E\) is an elliptic curve. The pushout is the explicit finite \(T\)-scheme \[ S=\operatorname{Spec}_T(\mathcal O_T\oplus\mathcal O_T(-3)), \qquad R[t]/(t(t-f_E))\simeq R\times_{R/(f_E)}R \] on each trivializing affine, where multiplication on the second summand uses the cubic section \(f_E\). It is reduced because the displayed algebra embeds in the product of two domains, and projective because it is finite over \(T\). Let \(A=E\times S\). The closed-cover sequence on the small etale site is \[ 0\longrightarrow A\longrightarrow i_{1*}A_T\oplus i_{2*}A_T \xrightarrow{\mathrm{res}_1-\mathrm{res}_2}i_{E*}A_E \longrightarrow0. \] For surjectivity it suffices to pass to a strict henselian local ring. A section into the smooth curve \(E\) on its closed quotient lifts across the resulting henselian pair; see the Stacks Project, Lemma~15.13.3~\cite{BStacksSmoothLift}. The kernel is the fibre-product description of \(S\). Every map \(\mathbf P^2\to E\) is constant, since its restriction to each projective line is constant, whereas the rigidity lemma gives \[ A(T)=E(\F_2),\qquad A(E)=E(\F_2)\oplus\operatorname{End}_{\F_2}(E). \] The cohomology boundary therefore injects \(\operatorname{End}_{\F_2}(E)\) into \(H^1_{\et}(S,A)\). In particular \(\alpha=\delta(1_E)\) has infinite order: \([m]:E\to E\) has degree \(m^2\) and is nonconstant for every nonzero integer \(m\). To represent this class by a scheme, glue two copies \(X_i=E\times T\) along \(E\times E\), using the identity on one side and \((a,t)\mapsto(a+t,t)\) on the other. Both attaching maps are closed immersions, so the pushout is a scheme by the Stacks Project, Lemma~37.67.8; Lemma~37.67.9(4) gives smoothness over \(S\)~\cite{BStacksClosedPushout,BStacksPushoutMorphisms}. The same local lifting just used trivializes the translation cocycle on an etale cover. Thus this scheme is the \(A\)-torsor of class \(\pm\alpha\), locally isomorphic to \(E\times S\), and is proper with geometrically connected genus-one fibres. Under the principal polarization \(E\simeq E^\vee\), translation by \(a\) acts on \(\operatorname{Pic}^d(E)\) by translation by \(\pm da\): represent a divisor by its sum in \(E\). Consequently \(\operatorname{Pic}^d_{X/S}\) is a torsor of class \(\pm d\alpha\). A global line bundle of degree \(d\) would give a section of that torsor, forcing \(d\alpha=0\), hence \(d=0\). This proves the assertion, and also shows that \(X\to S\) is not projective. The cubic smoothness, its five \(\F_2\)-points, and the displayed fibre-product algebra were checked exactly by \texttt{part\_b/code/singular\_genus\_one\_checks.py}; its output is preserved with the computations. The infinite-order and torsor claims are proved above, not inferred from the finite computation.

statement: Verified: a non-Betti form with all finite comparisons. Take $F=\Q(\sqrt5)$ and $K=F(i)$. The quaternion algebra $(-1,-1)_F$ is nonsplit at both real embeddings. It is split at every finite place: over $\Q$ Hamilton's algebra is ramified only at $2$ and infinity, and $2$ is inert in $F$ because $x^2-x-1$ is irreducible modulo two. The degree-two local extension at $2$ multiplies the invariant $1/2$ by two. The algebra is split by $K$, and its corestriction to $\Q$ is trivial since its two real invariants sum to zero in $\Q/\Z$. It is the nonzero element of $\Sha^1_f(\Q,S^K)\simeq\Z/2$. Equivalently, the corresponding $U$-torsor is $x^2+y^2=-1$ over $F$. Twisting Betti by its lift to an $S^K$-torsor supplies the asserted different rational fibre functor. The irreducibility calculation is recorded in the program.

statement: The finite-field coefficient-duality criterion [Proved equivalence for all Chow-heart coefficients; the universal hypothesis remains conjectural.]. Fix a finite field \(k\), and let \(\mathcal H\) be the rational Chow heart in \(\mathcal D=DM_{\rm gm}(k,\Q)\). For a smooth projective \(X/k\) of dimension \(d\), use the conventions \[ h_{\rm coh}(X)=M(X)^\vee=M(X)(-d)[-2d],\qquad P_{X,n}=h_{\rm coh}(X)(n)[2n]. \] Thus \(\mathcal H\) is generated by the \(P_{X,n}\) under finite sums and direct summands, and is closed under duality. Use the prescribed rational Weil extension of ordinary geometric motives, normalized by a generator \(e\) of degree one at \(\Spec k\). The following are equivalent. \begin{enumerate} \item For every \(P\in\mathcal H\) and every integer \(i\), the evaluation--trace pairing \[ W^i(P)\times W^{1-i}(P^\vee)\longrightarrow\Q \] is perfect between finite-dimensional spaces. \item Beilinson's rational--numerical equality and Parshin's rational vanishing hold for every smooth projective variety over \(k\). \item For every \(P\in\mathcal H\), the prescribed constant coefficient on \(\mathbf P^1_k\) has perfect finite-dimensional pairings \[ W^i(\mathbf P^1,\pi^*P)\times W^{3-i}(\mathbf P^1,\pi^*(P^\vee(1)))\longrightarrow\Q \quad\text{for every }i, \] with the usual projective-bundle formula, cup product and Gysin trace. \end{enumerate} Here ``Chow heart'' does not mean a single homogeneous cohomological weight. statement: A source error avoided in the preceding proof [Refuted; corrected statement proved]. Keller's Lemma~2.17 claims that the closure of a generic-fibre point of a proper relative curve is finite over an integral base. This is false in the printed generality. Over any finite field take \(S=\mathbb A^2_{x,y}\), \(Y=\mathbb P^1_{[u:v]}\times S\), and the generic point \([u:v]=[x:y]\). Its closure is \(uy-vx=0\), the blowup of the origin, whose fibre over \((0,0)\) is the whole \(\mathbb P^1\). On its two standard charts the coordinate rings are \(k[x,t]\), \(y=xt\), and \(k[y,s]\), \(x=ys\); it is integral and has no additional irreducible component. This explicitly contradicts the lemma's quasi-finiteness step. The degree of the associated line bundle, which is all the proof above uses, remains one on every fibre. Thus the section-free part of the preceding proposition is not inherited from that lemma or from its use in Corollary~2.18 and Theorem~4.27~\cite[Lemma~2.17]{BKeller2016}.

statement: Whole prime-to-characteristic Brauer finiteness and the exact gate [Proved equivalence; the surface-Tate condition remains unresolved]. statement: All twists for motives of abelian type, using the current theorem [Proved from the cited current theorem]. Let \(X/\F_q\) be smooth projective, and suppose that its rational Chow motive belongs to the thick rigid category generated by abelian varieties and Artin motives. statement: Finite absolute duality, with the coefficient category specified [Proved]. Let \(X\) be regular, separated, and of finite type over \(\Spec\Z\), of pure absolute dimension \(d\). Let \(F\) be a bounded constructible complex of \(\Z/m\)-sheaves on \(X_{\et}\). The real-place modification disappears for odd \(m\), for schemes with no real fibre, and for schemes over a finite field; properness over \(\Spec\Z\) alone does not remove it.

statement: An integral generator specified by finite searches [Proved as an effective construction]. For each odd integer \(m\ge3\), the following procedure specifies an higher Chow cycle \(\gamma_m\) over \(\Q\) with integer coefficients whose canonical integral-base class generates \[ H^1_{\et}(\Spec\Z,\Z(m))/\mathrm{tors} \simeq\Z. \] Every search terminates. The procedure requires the finite arithmetic computation of \(C_m\) in Theorem~\ref{thm:B-effective-odd-torsion} and Proposition~\ref{prop:B-two-primary}, but requires no uniform vanishing conjecture for these groups. Its output is a cycle given by rational polynomial equations and integer multiplicities, together with an explicitly found boundary certifying the saturation step.

statement: Rational duality for the Tate cases proved here [Proved]. For \(X=\Spec\mathcal O_K\), the Flach--Morin compactified complexes have perfect rational pairings \[ H^i_{\BW}(\bar X,\Q(n))\times H^{3-i}_{\BW}(\bar X,\Q(1-n))\longrightarrow\Q. \tag{B.27} \] For \(U=\Spec\mathcal O_K[1/S]\), the same assertion pairs the localized rational absolute complex with the compact-support complex, with the archimedean completion inherited from \(\bar X\). For a smooth projective geometrically connected curve \(C/\F_q\), the corresponding Weil--etale pairing is \[ H^i_{\BW}(C,\Q(n))\times H^{3-i}_{\BW}(C,\Q(1-n)) \longrightarrow\Q. \tag{B.28} \] Both statements hold for every integral twist \(n\), including negative twists, and for finite direct sums of these Tate objects.

statement: The prime-to-characteristic relative-curve gate is a surface gate [Proved equivalence; the equivalent surface Tate assertion remains unresolved]. Fix primes \(p\ne\ell\). The following statements are equivalent. \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)] \item The Tate conjecture for divisors holds for every smooth projective surface over \(\F_p\), including connected surfaces whose field of constants is a finite extension of \(\F_p\). \item For every finite field \(k/\F_p\), every smooth separated finite-type \(k\)-scheme \(S\), and every smooth projective morphism \(f:X\to S\) with geometrically connected curve fibres, the cokernel of \[ f^*:\Br(S)[\ell^\infty]\longrightarrow\Br(X)[\ell^\infty] \] is finite. Here \(\Br=H^2_{\mathrm{et}}(-,\Gm)_{\mathrm{tors}}\) is the cohomological Brauer group. \item The assertion in (ii) holds just for smooth curve families with a section over nonempty opens of \(\mathbb P^1_k\), for all finite \(k/\F_p\). \item The single birational invariant vanishes: \[ H^3(F_0\mathbb P^3_{\overline{\F}_p},\Q_\ell(2))^ {\operatorname{Gal}(\overline{\F}_p/\F_p)}=0. \] Here \(F_0\) denotes the colimit over dense open subsets, as in Proposition~\ref{prop:B-diagonal-Chow-gate}. \end{enumerate} Thus the universal regular separated-base relative-curve question in its intended \(\ell\ne p\) form is already equivalent to a fixed-dimensional surface conjecture. This theorem does not identify the characteristic-primary assertion with that conjecture, and does not extend its surface equivalence to arbitrary singular or nonseparated bases.

statement: A geometrically simply connected surface test [Proved strict intrinsic test-class equivalence; restricted Tate unresolved]. Fix a finite field \(k\) of characteristic \(p\), a prime \(\ell\ne p\), an integer \(N\geq1\), and a real number \(\varepsilon>0\). Divisor Tate for all smooth projective geometrically integral surfaces over \(k\) is equivalent to divisor Tate for just those surfaces \(Y/k\) satisfying \[ \pi_1^{\et}(Y_{\overline k})=1, \qquad H^1(Y,\mathcal O_Y)=0, \qquad \omega_Y\text{ very ample}, \] and, simultaneously, \[ K_Y^2\geq N,\qquad p_g(Y)\geq N,\qquad c_2(Y)>0, \qquad \left|\frac{K_Y^2}{c_2(Y)}-1\right|<\varepsilon. \] No extension of the fixed field \(k\) is needed in the reduction. Consequently the universal prime-to-characteristic torsor and relative-Brauer finiteness assertions of Theorem~\ref{thm:B-Brauer-prime-uniform} and Corollary~\ref{cor:B-torsors-prime-uniform} have this smaller intrinsic surface test class, when quantified over finite constant extensions as before. The numerical conditions are inherited from Corollary~\ref{cor:B-canonical-surface-gate}, not independent additional reductions.

statement: Proved: the complete lattice and rank answer to 15:151. The image $I_\Sigma$ of $\psi_\Sigma$ is the connected $\Q$-torus with character and cocharacter lattices \begin{align*} X^*(I_\Sigma)&=\Z^{I_E}/\ker(A^{\mathsf t}) \simeq\im(A^{\mathsf t})\subset\Z^{I_K},\\ X_*(I_\Sigma)&=(\im A\otimes\Q)\cap\Z^{I_E}. \end{align*} In particular $\dim I_\Sigma=\operatorname{rank}_\Q(A)$. If $E$ is CM of degree $2g$, put \[ C_E=\{x\in\Res_{E/\Q}\Gm: x\overline x\in\Gm\subset\Res_{E^+/\Q}\Gm\}. \] Then $I_\Sigma\subset C_E$, and the following conditions are equivalent: \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)] \item $I_\Sigma=C_E$; \item $\operatorname{rank}_\Q(A)=g+1$; \item every rational row relation of $A$ is generated by $e_\sigma+e_{c\sigma}-e_\tau-e_{c\tau}$. \end{enumerate} These are effective necessary and sufficient conditions for every CM type, including non-Galois and imprimitive types. For the CM type $\Phi$ represented by $\Sigma$, $I_\Sigma=\MT(E,\Phi)$.

statement: Proved: finite-place kernel and fibre functors. There is a canonical identification \[ \Sha^1_f(\Q,S^K) \simeq \left\{(\epsilon_v)_{v\mid\infty}\in\F_2^r: \sum_v\epsilon_v=0\right\}. \] For the geometric neutral category of CM motives whose CM fields are subfields of $K$, with Betti functor as origin, this group classifies the isomorphism classes of rational fibre functors that become isomorphic to Betti at every finite completion. It has $2^{r-1}$ elements. Thus finite comparisons single out Betti only when $r=1$. Adding a real comparison singles it out for every $r$.

statement: Proved: D.2(a) for abelian type and its general equivalent. For a motive $M$ of abelian type, in either category, \[ G_{\mathrm{mot}}(M)^\circ\text{ is commutative} \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad M\in\CM(k). \] For arbitrary motives the same classification is equivalent to the following restricted Hodge-class assertion: \emph{CM comparison case of the absolute-Hodge (respectively motivated Hodge) conjecture.} If $G_{\mathrm{mot}}(M)^\circ$ is commutative and $N$ is a CM abelian motive over $\overline k$, every rational Hodge morphism $H_B(M_{\overline k})\to H_B(N)$ is induced by an absolute Hodge (respectively motivated) correspondence. It is enough in this assertion to require one Hodge isomorphism to some such $N$ to lift. In the absolute-Hodge case this is a precise restriction of \citet[Conjecture 8.24]{c_delignehodge1982}, rather than a claim of equivalence with the unrestricted conjecture.

statement: A.1d (Proved: geometric determination of the Deuring rule).. For a pair $(M,O)$ over $k$, define an orientation $\zeta_M:O\to k$ by the action of $a$ on $M/FM$. Choose a supersingular elliptic curve $E/k$ and an oriented isomorphism $\eta:O\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{End}(E)$, and choose an $O$-linear crystalline isomorphism $b:D(E)\xrightarrow{\sim}M$. Then \begin{equation} \boxed{\quad u_D(M,O)= [\,b_E\circ\bigwedge^2 b^{-1}\,] \ \in\operatorname{Isom}_{F}(\bigwedge^2M,T)/\mathbb Z_p^{*2}. \quad} \end{equation} The right side exists and is independent of all these choices. All such rules form a simply transitive set under $\mathbb Z_p^*/\mathbb Z_p^{*2}$: two elements if $p$ is odd, and four if $p=2$. Lead A1 is correct on this qualified domain; it is not a repair of A.1a without changing its domain.

statement: A.1e (Proved: an evaluation prescription and its scope).. Formula \eqref{eq:A-Deuring} determines a choice-independent output. One way to evaluate it is to enumerate supersingular Weierstrass models over finite subfields, enumerate endomorphisms with the degrees of a chosen integral basis of $O$, test the multiplication table and the orientation, and solve the $O,F$-intertwining equations for $b$. The search terminates by A.1c and the oriented Deuring theorem. Choose a symplectic crystalline basis $(x,y)$ of $D(E)$ with $b_E(x\wedge y)=t$; if $b$ has matrix $B$ in a basis of $M$, the coefficient in that basis is $(\det B)^{-1}$, taken modulo squares. The pairing can be evaluated by the de Rham trace on any smooth lift and the residue pairing at the origin. Different lifts and symplectic bases give the same expression by the proof of A.1d. More explicitly, first solve the $O$-intertwining equations for an integral module isomorphism $C:D(E)\to M$. The matching residue orientation and A.1c ensure that such a $C$ exists. The two semilinear operators differ by a scalar unit: $F_M C=aC F_{D(E)}$. Solve $\sigma(r)/r=a^{-1}$ in $W(k)^*$ by the successive equations in A.1b; then $b=Cr$ is the required $F$-intertwiner. All its choices differ by $\mathbb Z_p^*$ and hence disappear in the specified square quotient. This is a prescription on the input crystal and oriented order, with the geometric curve recovered by the preceding terminating search; it is not a choice of an extra polarization on the input. We have not implemented this all-$p$ crystalline evaluation algorithm. The executable certificates in this package establish the explicit counterexamples and finite counts, not numerical values of this geometric formula for arbitrary input orders. No unrun computation is used as a verification event.

statement: A.1g (Proved: a corrected equivalence at the level of rules).. Although the claimed equivalence of \emph{all descent objects} is false, restriction of the geometric determinant rules of A.1d to the nonempty maximal-$R$ locus of A.8c is a bijection onto rules compatible with its isomorphisms and invertible $R$-ideal action. Indeed the ideal action is transitive by Waterhouse's Theorem 4.5, so the ratio of two rules is a single unit squareclass. The polarization rule restricts to such a rule, giving an origin on both sides and identifying restriction with the identity on $\mathbb Z_p^*/\mathbb Z_p^{*2}$. Its compatibility follows from the positive norm of an isogeny, as in A.1d. The determinant normalization in this description is really $\bigwedge^2_{\mathbb Z}P_0\otimes (\bigwedge^2_{\mathbb Z}R)^{-1}$, the quadratic norm line. Writing it simply as $\det_{\mathbb Z}P_0\simeq\mathbb Z$ requires the fixed ordered basis $(1,\sqrt{-p})$, or $(1,(1+\sqrt{-p})/2)$ in the odd discriminant case, of $R$. The norm-line formulation avoids an unmentioned orientation choice. This statement covers $p=2,3$ as well; it does not identify their additional nonzero-trace supersingular forms with these triples.

statement: A.2b (Proved under the geometric comparison interpretation).. For a positively determinant-rigidified Deuring category $C$ of type $B_p$, take isomorphism classes of comparison equivalences with the prime-to-$p$ Tate category, the crystalline category, and the real quaternionic category. Their product $\mathcal T'(C)$ is a right $\Gamma'$-torsor. Global precomposition uses the unrigidified $\operatorname{Eq}(C)$ equipped with its canonical positive determinant transport, as in the map on 15:48. It does not use every possible rigidification in $\operatorname{Eq}(C,T)$. Precomposition by the nontrivial Brandt class acts by $f$. The quotient $\mathcal T=\mathcal T'(C)/\langle f\rangle$ is a right $H^1(A_{\rm int},\mu_2)$-torsor, independent of $C$ through the specified comparison maps. Frobenius acts trivially on this quotient.

statement: A.2c (Proved: what the comparison gerbe is).. Fix the crystalline determinant rule of A.1d. Over $A''=A'\times\mathbb R$ let $h$ be the $\mu_2$-gerbe of determinant-rigidified splittings of $B_p$, and let $h_{\rm std}$ be the square-root gerbe of the Tate line on $A'$ and the nonneutral standard $\mu_2$-gerbe on $\mathbb R$. Put \[ \mathfrak G(\xi_p)|_{A''}=\operatorname{Eq}_{\mu_2}(h,h_{\rm std}), \qquad \mathfrak G(\xi_p)|_{\mathbb Z_p}=B\mu_2. \] This is a neutral fppf $\mu_2$-gerbe over $A_{\rm int}$. The set of its sections up to isomorphism is a torsor under $H^1(A_{\rm int},\mu_2)$. With the comparison construction of A.2b it is $\mathcal T$. Its geometric section is the Tate-module realization with the Weil pairing at every $\ell\ne p$, the unit object of $B\mu_2$ at $p$, and the positive quaternionic realization at infinity. Its image in the crystalline factor torsor is $\xi_p$, not a numerical unit without the choice of an origin in that torsor.

statement: A.3a (Proved: the two meanings of the real sign).. There are two classes of unpolarized determinant comparison at infinity, a torsor under $H^1(\mathbb R,\mu_2)=\{\pm1\}$. Positivity selects one of these classes: a quaternionic linear isomorphism has strictly positive reduced norm and cannot identify a positive norm form with its negative. The chosen class still has automorphism group $H^0(\mathbb R,\mu_2)=\{\pm1\}$. Consequently positivity fixes the \emph{class} of the real component of $|\xi|$, but does not select one natural isomorphism between its realizations. A claim of uniqueness up to \emph{unique} isomorphism for A.4 would be false because $-1$ is a nonidentity unitary natural automorphism.

statement: A.4a (Proved: quaternionic realization).. Choose $E_0/k$ supersingular and an $\mathbb R$-algebra isomorphism $\beta:\operatorname{End}^0(E_0)\otimes\mathbb R\to\mathbb H$. For an elliptic curve $E$ in the supersingular category put \[ V_E=\operatorname{Hom}(E_0,E)\otimes_{\mathbb Z}\mathbb R, \qquad \langle x,y\rangle=\beta(x^\vee y). \] Transport the right action along $\beta$. Then $V_E$ is a right quaternionic line with positive Hermitian form, and $f:E\to E'$ acts by $x\mapsto fx$. It has adjoint $f^\vee$ and norm multiplier $\deg f$. Any two such realizations are isomorphic by a unitary natural transformation, and exactly two such transformations exist. They differ by the central sign $-1$.

statement: A.5a (Proved under condition (C), including nonzero Picard groups).. Let the unrigidified Brandt categories of two equivalent Deuring categories carry the symmetric Picard structure obtained from commuting two-sided fractional ideals. Let $N$ be their reduced-norm functor to $\operatorname{Pic}(A')$. statement: A.6a (Proved: the positive, or $\Phi$-normalized, determinant).. Let $A$ be a Dedekind domain, $K$ its fraction field, $O$ a maximal order in a central simple $K$-algebra $B$, and $\Phi=\operatorname{Nrd}(B^*)$. If \[ \operatorname{Pic}(A)=0,\qquad \Phi\cap A^*=\{1\}, \qquad \Phi A^*=K^*, \] the norm line of every rank-one right projective $O$-module has a unique generator in its distinguished $\Phi$-coset. Sending that generator to $1$ defines natural, multiplicative trivializations of norm lines. These give the transitive determinant identifications of 15:21--22. For $A=\mathbb Z$, $B=B_p$, the distinguished generator is the positive generator, and the construction exists for every $p$.
