statement: The rational exceptional spectrum of the ordered tetrahedron (audited auxiliary calculation).. Let $k_0=\overline{\mathbf F}_p$, and let $E_0/k_0$ be the reduced exceptional surface in the ordered resolution TG.1--TG.5. Thus its four components are the blowups of $\mathbf P^2$ at $15,10,5,0$ nonvertex edge points, respectively. In this paragraph the subscript $0$ denotes the field of definition, not the unresolved first blowup used in TG.2. For every quasi-compact separated $k_0$-scheme $P$ for which the indicated products are Noetherian, the external-product map is a natural equivalence of rational $K(P)$-module spectra \begin{equation} K(E_0)_{\mathbf Q}\otimes_{K(k_0)_{\mathbf Q}}K(P)_{\mathbf Q} \ \xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }\ K(E_0\times_{k_0}P)_{\mathbf Q}. \tag{TS.1} \end{equation} Here $K$ is ordinary Bass-completed $K$-theory of perfect complexes. There is a noncanonical, parameter-independent splitting \begin{equation} K(E_0\times_{k_0}P)_{\mathbf Q} \simeq K(P)_{\mathbf Q}^{\oplus33} \oplus \Sigma^{-2}K(P)_{\mathbf Q}. \tag{TS.2} \end{equation} The equivalence (TS.1), unlike the displayed choice of splitting, is natural in $P$. No equivalence with a base change of $K(Z)$ is asserted. \emph{Step 1: a comparison of the entire restriction diagrams.} For each nonempty intersection $E_I$ of components, consider its canonical external-product map \[ K(E_I)_{\mathbf Q}\otimes_{K(k_0)_{\mathbf Q}}K(P)_{\mathbf Q} \longrightarrow K(E_I\times P)_{\mathbf Q}. \] It is an equivalence. For projective spaces and points this follows from the projective-bundle formula. For the blown-up planes it follows successively from the blowup formula in a smooth point. The formulas are induced by actual pullback, tensor, and perfect proper pushforward functors; hence their comparison with the external product is the projection formula, not a comparison of ranks. We use \citet[Corollaries 3.6 and 4.4, author pp.~12 and 16] {D_Khan2020Blowup} only for these ordinary regular projective bundles and blowups. The comparison maps themselves commute with all restriction maps and all their coherences, because external product is natural before choosing any projective-bundle bases. Thus there is an objectwise equivalence of the full finite cubical restriction diagrams. This avoids choosing incompatible cellular flags or discarding gluing automorphisms at the nodes. \emph{Step 2: descent for the closed union.} For a binary closed union in characteristic $p$, the local square is a Milnor square of rings. Theorem C of \citet[p.~30]{rootGeisserHesselholt2011} makes its birelative spectrum zero after inverting $p$, and finite affine Mayer--Vietoris globalizes this assertion. Nilpotent reductions are harmless by their Theorem A. Iterating over the four components and their intersections therefore expresses $K(E_0)_{\mathbf Q}$ and $K(E_0\times P)_{\mathbf Q}$ as the finite homotopy limits of their closed-cover diagrams. Tensor product of module spectra is exact and hence commutes with finite homotopy limits. Applying it to the objectwise equivalence in Step~1 proves (TS.1). This argument uses ordinary $K$ after rationalization; it does not substitute $KH$ without a comparison. \emph{Step 3: the finite rational complex over $k_0$.} The rational $K$-spectrum of $k_0$ is $H\mathbf Q$: the positive groups are torsion and the negative groups of a field vanish. For the positive statement one may use Quillen's finite-field calculation and filtered colimits; the exact displayed calculation is recorded in \citet[Chapter~IV, Corollary~1.13 and Example~2.6] {D_Weibel2013KbookIV}. Only rational vanishing is required here. Consequently every stratum's rational spectrum has homotopy solely in degree zero. Its canonical identification with the Eilenberg-- MacLane spectrum of its $K_0$ is natural in all restriction maps. The entire diagram, including its higher coherences, can therefore be computed in rational vector spaces. There are no discarded positive $K_1(k_0)_{\mathbf Q}$ entries. The normalized cochain complex is \begin{equation} \bigoplus_{i=0}^3 K_0(E_i)_{\mathbf Q} \longrightarrow \bigoplus_{i<j}K_0(E_i\cap E_j)_{\mathbf Q} \longrightarrow \bigoplus_{i<j<l}K_0(E_i\cap E_j\cap E_l)_{\mathbf Q}. \tag{TS.3} \end{equation} Rational Chern character on these smooth rational strata splits this complex into its codimension-zero, one, and two parts, compatibly with pullback. The codimension-zero part is the ordinary cochain complex of the boundary of the tetrahedron. Its cohomology is $\mathbf Q$ in degrees zero and two and is zero in degree one. The codimension-one part is the restriction-degree map \[ \bigoplus_i\operatorname{Pic}(E_i)_{\mathbf Q} \longrightarrow \mathbf Q^{6}. \] It is surjective: on each edge choose one of the five point-exceptional curves on the earlier endpoint component. Its intersection with that edge's strict transform is one and its intersection with every other edge is zero, because its centre is a nonvertex point. Its Picard class therefore supplies the corresponding signed standard basis vector. The source has rank $4+30=34$, so the kernel has rank~28. The codimension-two part is $\mathbf Q^4$ in degree zero, since each component has $CH_0=\mathbf Z$ and the edges have no codimension-two Chow group. We conclude \[ \pi_0K(E_0)_{\mathbf Q}=\mathbf Q^{33},\qquad \pi_{-1}K(E_0)_{\mathbf Q}=0,\qquad \pi_{-2}K(E_0)_{\mathbf Q}=\mathbf Q, \] with all other rational groups zero. A finite complex of rational vector spaces splits as its cohomology. Choosing that splitting once over $k_0$, then applying (TS.1), proves (TS.2). \emph{Step 4: the exact residual coefficient, and what is not proved.} For $P=\operatorname{Spec}k$, where $k/k_0$ is algebraically closed, the summand in degree zero arising from the final term of (TS.2) is an actual ordinary $K_2(k)_{\mathbf Q}$ coefficient. A generator $\kappa\in K_{-2}(E_0)_{\mathbf Q}$ has Adams weight zero, and this coefficient is its product with $K_2(k)$, which has Adams weight two. The remaining weight-two part is the four component-degree classes. For a smooth proper curve $P/k$, the same chosen summand is $K_2(P)_{\mathbf Q}$ and evaluation at a point is the ordinary $K_2$ specialization. This parameter compatibility follows from (TS.1), not just from the dimensions of (TS.3). The product restriction $K(Z\times P)\to K(E\times P)$ has not been computed by this argument. Its precise characteristic-$p$ cokernel is FF.1, and on the displayed coefficient its boundary is FF.3. There is an important separate point-parameter conclusion: \citet[Theorem~3.7 and Remark~(ii), author p.~8]{frDrinfeld2004Tate} give $K_{-1}(R)=0$ for every commutative henselian local ring. Thus, for the strict-local version of TG, FF.1 with a point parameter does prove that every individual coefficient lifts after inverting $p$. The KST sequence also proves injectivity: $K_0(R)=\mathbf Z$ maps by the identity to $K_0(k)=\mathbf Z$, so a pair $(z,0)$ in its diagonal image must be zero. Hence $K_0(Z)[1/p]\simeq K_0(E)[1/p]$. In particular the point coefficient product with $\partial\kappa$ vanishes in degree $-1$ after strict henselization. This corrects the earlier prospective point-faithfulness test. The fixed proper product $\operatorname{Spec}R\times P$ is not a henselian local scheme. Drinfeld's local theorem does not make its $K_{-1}$ vanish. Neither (TS.2) nor the point isomorphism just proved lifts the prescribed whole proper-curve $K_2$ class to $Z\times P$. That full-family boundary remains outside this calculation. The subsequent endpoint theorem EL computes the ordinary quotient for this tetrahedral example without asserting that the prescribed whole perfect family lifts.

statement: An intersection identity for the degree-unit SNC gluing term.. Let $Z$ be regular of dimension $d+1$, with $d\ge2$, and let $E=\bigcup_iE_i$ be a projective simple normal crossing divisor. Let $D=\sum_i a_iE_i$, where all $a_i>0$ are rational. Choose an ample line bundle $H$ on $E$. Suppose that for every irreducible double stratum $C_{ij}\subset E_i\cap E_j$, \[ \lambda_{ij} =\deg\bigl((-D)|_{C_{ij}}\,H^{d-2}\bigr)>0. \] This holds, in particular, if $\mathcal O_Z(-D)|_E$ is ample after clearing the denominators of $D$. Choose an orientation for each double stratum. Then the restriction-degree map \[ \bigoplus_i N_1(E_i)_{\mathbb Q} \longrightarrow\bigoplus_{\text{double strata}}\mathbb Q, \qquad (z_i)_i\longmapsto \bigl(\deg(z_i\cdot C_{ij})- \deg(z_j\cdot C_{ij})\bigr)_{i\to j} \] is surjective. Here each double stratum is a divisor on both adjacent components; if an intersection is disconnected, we index its components separately.

statement: Fixed-parameter negative-$K$ obstruction (proved auxiliary statement).. Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field of characteristic $p>0$, let $(R,\mathfrak m)$ be a noetherian local $k$-algebra with residue field $k$, and let $g:Z\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ be a proper morphism from a regular noetherian scheme which is an isomorphism away from the closed point. Put $E=(Z\times_R k)_{\mathrm{red}}$. Let $P$ be a fixed smooth proper $k$-scheme; in the intended application $P$ is a connected curve. All $K$-groups below are Bass-completed nonconnective groups of perfect complexes. We have a natural isomorphism \begin{equation} \operatorname{coker}\!\left( K_0(Z\times_k P)[1/p]\longrightarrow K_0(E\times_k P)[1/p] \right) \ \simeq\ K_{-1}(\operatorname{Spec}R\times_k P)[1/p]. \tag{FF.1} \end{equation} Thus an actual class on the fixed product $E\times_k P$ lifts to an actual class on $Z\times_k P$, after inverting $p$, if and only if its image under the connecting map in (FF.1) is zero. This is a statement about $K_0$ classes, not about a compatible system of chosen vector bundles.

statement: An exceptional perfect-$K_0$ presentation of the ordinary top quotient (audited comparison).. Retain all hypotheses of the general endpoint theorem EL: $k$ is algebraically closed of characteristic $p>0$; $R$ is an excellent henselian local coefficient-$k$ ring of algebraizable dimension three; $Z\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ is a regular projective modification, an isomorphism away from its closed point; its reduced closed fibre $E$ is a simple normal crossing divisor; and an effective Cartier divisor $D$ with full support $E$ has ample conormal $\mathcal O_D(-D)$. Put $X=Z\setminus E$. Define \[ S(E)=F_\gamma^2K_0(E)_{\mathbf Q}. \] Let $J_K(E)\subset S(E)$ be generated by all differences \begin{equation} u^*\beta-v^*\beta, \qquad \beta\in F_\gamma^2K_0(E\times P)_{\mathbf Q}, \quad u,v\in P(k), \tag{EP.1} \end{equation} where $P/k$ runs over smooth connected projective curves and the pullbacks are along the actual two product sections. This definition uses perfect $K$-theory on the possibly singular projective product. It does not replace it by coherent $G$-theory or by cycles on the individual normal-crossing strata. Restriction and the rational Chern character give an isomorphism \begin{equation} \rho:\mathrm{CH}^2(Z)_{\mathbf Q} \xrightarrow{\sim}S(E). \tag{EP.2} \end{equation} Let \[ \theta:\mathrm{CH}_1(E)_{\mathbf Q}\longrightarrow S(E) \] be the composite of proper cycle pushforward into $Z$ with $\rho$. The comparison is \begin{align} \rho\bigl(\mathrm{CH}^2(Z)_{\mathrm{alg},\mathbf Q}\bigr) &=J_K(E), \tag{EP.3}\\ B^2(X)_{\mathbf Q} &\simeq S(E)\big/ \bigl(J_K(E)+\theta\mathrm{CH}_1(E)_{\mathbf Q}\bigr). \tag{EP.4} \end{align} Here ordinary algebraic equivalence means actual fixed-product families. In particular the subgroup on the right of (EP.3) no longer involves a lift of a parameter family to the resolution. The exceptional pushforward $\theta$ still records the given embedding $E\subset Z$, as it should. \emph{1. The point restriction and the weight-two identification.} FF.4 gives $K_0(Z)_{\mathbf Q}\simeq K_0(E)_{\mathbf Q}$ by actual restriction. Its proof uses KST and levelwise nilpotent invariance, together with $K_{-1}(R)=0$ for the henselian local ring, by \citet[Theorem 3.7 and Remark (ii), p.~8]{frDrinfeld2004Tate}. Restriction commutes with lambda and Adams operations. Since $E$ is a projective surface, $F_\gamma^3K_0(E)=0$. The Adams action on $F_\gamma^i/F_\gamma^{i+1}$ is $2^i$ for $\psi^2$\citep[Chapter II, Proposition 4.9 and Remark 8.8.5] {D_Weibel2013KbookII}. Over $\mathbf Q$ the three distinct roots $1,2,4$ give the eigenspace decomposition. Explicitly $(\psi^2-1)(\psi^2-2)/6$ is the projector onto $F_\gamma^2$. Thus $S(E)$ is exactly the Adams-weight-two subgroup. For $Z$, the rational Chern character identifies the weight-two subgroup with $\mathrm{CH}^2(Z)_{\mathbf Q}$. The strict-local use is justified as in TC: the projective resolution and every finite collection of bundles, cycles, relations and Chern operations descend to one pointed etale finite-type model. After shrinking around its proper exceptional fibre the model is regular, hence smooth over the perfect field $k$. The smooth rational Chern-character isomorphism \citep[Chapter II, Corollary 8.9.1, p.~84]{D_Weibel2013KbookII} passes to this filtered limit. Restriction therefore gives (EP.2). The same reasoning applies to $Z\times P$ and its finite cycle families; it does not require that the singular base be smooth. \emph{2. Every exceptional perfect-family relation lifts at its endpoints.} The map \[ K_0(D\times P)_{\mathbf Q} \longrightarrow K_0(E\times P)_{\mathbf Q} \] is an isomorphism by nilpotent invariance in characteristic $p$ \citep[Theorem A]{rootGeisserHesselholt2011}. It is a lambda-ring map by perfect pullback. Its inverse preserves rank and the rational gamma filtration: one may either use the inverse lambda-ring map, or lift each rank-zero generator in an expression for $F_\gamma^2$ and apply its gamma operations. Rational gamma operations are determined by the universal special lambda-ring identities after clearing denominators. This verifies the filtration assertion without identifying ordinary cycles on the nonreduced scheme. Given $\beta$ in (EP.1), let $\widetilde\beta$ be its preimage in $F_\gamma^2K_0(D\times P)_{\mathbf Q}$. EL constructs an actual $b\in K_0(Z\times P)_{\mathbf Q}$ whose two endpoint restrictions to $E$ are precisely those of $\beta$. Since these endpoints lie in $S(E)$, the point isomorphism in Step~1 forces the two endpoint classes of $b$ on $Z$ to be of weight two. The actual cycle $\operatorname{ch}_2(b)\in\mathrm{CH}^2(Z\times P)_{\mathbf Q}$ therefore has the prescribed endpoint difference under $\rho$. It is an ordinary algebraic-equivalence relation. This proves $J_K(E)\subset\rho(\mathrm{CH}^2(Z)_{\mathrm{alg},\mathbf Q})$. The full exceptional class $\beta$ need not lift on the whole product: only its endpoints were used. No assertion about $K_{-1}(\operatorname{Spec}R\times P)$ is needed. \emph{3. Every ordinary cycle relation restricts to such a perfect family.} Conversely consider a relation given by a cycle family $z\in\mathrm{CH}^2(Z\times P)_{\mathbf Q}$ and two fibres. On a finite-type smooth model, take the inverse rational Chern character of the element having codimension-two component $z$ and all other components zero. Pull it to $Z\times P$. This is an actual class $b\in F_\gamma^2K_0(Z\times P)_{\mathbf Q}$ with $\operatorname{ch}_2(b)=z$; it has pure weight two. Restriction to $E\times P$ preserves $F_\gamma^2$, so its endpoint difference belongs to $J_K(E)$. Chern character and pullback commute, which proves the reverse inclusion in (EP.3). It suffices here to use projective parameter curves. Any ordinary relation originally given over a smooth nonproper curve can be compactified: extend that curve smoothly to a projective curve, and close the finitely many horizontal integral cycle components in the product. They remain flat over the regular parameter curve near the two chosen points, and their refined fibres there are unchanged. This closure operation is made on a single finite type model if necessary and then pulled to the strict-local scheme. No henselized parameter product is substituted. \emph{4. Localization preserves the exact ordinary relation subgroup.} Cycle localization gives \[ \mathrm{CH}_1(E)_{\mathbf Q}\longrightarrow \mathrm{CH}^2(Z)_{\mathbf Q}\longrightarrow \mathrm{CH}^2(X)_{\mathbf Q}\longrightarrow0. \] Moreover the image of $\mathrm{CH}^2(Z)_{\mathrm{alg},\mathbf Q}$ is exactly $\mathrm{CH}^2(X)_{\mathrm{alg},\mathbf Q}$. One inclusion is restriction of actual families. For the other, close an actual family on $X\times P$ in $Z\times P$; refined pullback along either parameter point then restricts to the original fibre on $X$. This can again be performed on one smooth finite-type model with finitely many cycle components. Thus each ordinary relation on $X$ is the restriction of an ordinary relation on $Z$, up to the allowed exceptional cycles. Quotienting the localization sequence by these subgroups, and using (EP.2)--(EP.3), gives (EP.4). \emph{Scope of the reduction.} The nontrivial input is EL: (EP.3) proves that every actual proper perfect-family relation on the exceptional surface is realized by an ordinary cycle relation on the regular resolution, even when the original family itself has a nonzero negative-$K$ boundary. This removes the ambient endpoint-lifting obstruction under the displayed three-dimensional resolution hypotheses. It does not compute $J_K(E)$ for an arbitrary normal-crossing surface. In particular families assembled separately on double curves can have nonzero restrictions at triple points and need not glue to a class on $E\times P$; those compatibility conditions are still part of (EP.1). The comparison is therefore stronger than retaining the original liftability condition, but does not by itself prove universal vanishing or finiteness of the right side of (EP.4).

statement: Auxiliary proposition for C.3bl (Proved): the primitive relative Milnor invariant kills the entire exceptional image.. Let $k$ be algebraically closed of characteristic $p>0$, let $s\geq1$ and $m\geq0$, and put $r=s+1$. Let $W_1,\ldots,W_s$ be smooth cubic surfaces, $A_i=\mathcal O_{W_i}(1)=-K_{W_i}$, and let $C/k$ be a smooth projective connected curve of genus at least two. Set \[ \begin{gathered} T=\mathbb P^m\times\prod_{i=1}^sW_i, \qquad L_T=\mathcal O_{\mathbb P^m}(1)\boxtimes A_1\boxtimes\cdots\boxtimes A_s, \qquad b=c_1(L_T),\\ V=T\times C,\qquad L=L_T\boxtimes K_C. \end{gathered} \tag{PB.1} \] Suppose $R$ is an excellent henselian local $k$-algebra obtained by strict henselization from an algebraic local $k$-scheme, and $\mathcal Z\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ is projective and regular. Suppose that its closed fibre is the smooth Cartier divisor $i:V\hookrightarrow\mathcal Z$, that \[ \mathfrak m_R\mathcal O_{\mathcal Z}=I_V, \qquad I_V/I_V^2=L, \qquad q:\mathcal Z\longrightarrow T, \quad q|_V=\operatorname{pr}_T. \tag{PB.2} \] Write $E=V_2$ and $X=\mathcal Z\setminus V$. We require the given scheme and morphism to descend to the algebraic local model, as they do in the total-line construction of C.3bj. Every finite list of line bundles and Chow relations used below can then be considered on one smooth finite-type model after a pointed etale base change. Define the following direct K\"unneth summand: \[ \mathcal M_k= H^0(\mathbb P^m,\mathcal O(1))\otimes_k \bigotimes_{i=1}^s H^1(W_i,A_i\otimes\Omega^1_{W_i/k}) \otimes_k H^1(C,K_C) \subset H^r(V,L\otimes\Omega^s_{V/k}). \tag{PB.3} \] Let $P$ be the projection onto this summand, with the indicated order of the cubic factors. If $\mathcal A$ is a line bundle on $\mathcal Z$ trivialized on $V$, write $a\in H^1(V,L)$ for its first relative jet. For $D_i\in\operatorname{Pic}(W_i)$ form the actual Chow class \[ \beta=c_1(\mathcal A)\prod_{i=1}^s c_1(q^*D_i) \in\mathrm{CH}^{r}(\mathcal Z). \tag{PB.4} \] Here $q^*D_i$ abbreviates pullback through the $i$th projection of $T$. If \[ P\left(a\smile\prod_i d\log D_i\right)\ne0, \tag{PB.5} \] then $\beta|_X\ne0$ integrally. More precisely, the projected relative Milnor invariant in (PB.5) vanishes on every exceptional class $i_*\gamma$ whose restriction to $V$ is zero. We do not assert that all Hodge components of every exceptional class vanish.

statement: The rational Chow group of the punctured tetrahedral germ (audited auxiliary calculation).. Let $k_0=\overline{\mathbf F}_p$, let $k/k_0$ be algebraically closed, and take the exact ordered tetrahedral construction TG.1--TG.5 over $k_0$, followed by base change to $k$ and strict henselization at its vertex. Write $R$ for that strictly henselian normal local ring, $\pi:Z\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ for the regular projective resolution, $E=\bigcup_{i=0}^3E_i$ for its reduced exceptional divisor, and $X=Z\setminus E$. Then, after choosing the orientation and splitting of TS.2, there is an isomorphism \begin{equation} \mathrm{CH}^{2}(X)_{\mathbf Q} \simeq K_2(k)_{\mathbf Q}. \tag{TC.1} \end{equation} This statement concerns rational equivalence. It neither identifies the ordinary algebraically trivial subgroup nor computes $B^2(X)_{\mathbf Q}$. \emph{Step 1: the weight-two group on the regular resolution.} By the point-parameter isomorphism FF.4, using Drinfeld's Theorem~3.7 and Remark~(ii)\citep[author p.~8]{frDrinfeld2004Tate}, restriction induces \[ K_0(Z)_{\mathbf Q} \xrightarrow{\sim}K_0(E)_{\mathbf Q}. \] It commutes with Adams operations. The rational Chern character identifies $\mathrm{CH}^{2}(Z)_{\mathbf Q}$ with the weight-two part of $K_0(Z)_{\mathbf Q}$. Here is the finite-type justification in the present strict-local setting. The original resolution is defined over a finite-type $k$-scheme; its base changes over pointed etale neighbourhoods of the vertex are regular after shrinking around the proper exceptional fibre. Since $k$ is perfect, these regular finite-type models are smooth. Every finite collection of perfect complexes, cycles, rational equivalences, Chern classes and relations descends to one such neighbourhood. The rational Chern character isomorphism on those smooth models \citep[Example~15.2.16, pp.~294--295]{frC4Fulton1998} therefore passes to the filtered strict-local limit, as in C.3ad. The whole-diagram comparison of TS, with its compatible Adams decomposition, now gives \begin{equation} \mathrm{CH}^{2}(Z)_{\mathbf Q} \simeq \mathbf Q^4\oplus K_2(k)_{\mathbf Q}. \tag{TC.2} \end{equation} The first four coordinates are restriction to each $E_i$ followed by the degree of its zero-cycle Chern character. The last coordinate is the chosen $\kappa K_2(k)$ coefficient from TS.4. On a field, $K_2(k)$ has Adams weight two \citep[Chapter~IV, Example~5.9.1, p.~51]{D_Weibel2013KbookIV}. There is no support or Thom shift here: the operations on the closed restriction diagram commute with its homotopy-fibre boundaries. The exact-category construction and its scope were spelled out in C.3bc, Step~2; this does not apply a regular-ambient theorem directly to a singular scheme. \emph{Step 2: exceptional curves have zero coefficient in $K_2(k)$.} The cycle map from the disjoint union of the four components gives a surjection \[ \bigoplus_i\mathrm{CH}_1(E_i) \longrightarrow\mathrm{CH}_1(E). \] Each $E_i$ is a blowup of $\mathbf P^2$ in $15,10,5,0$ specified $k_0$-points, respectively. Its divisor group modulo rational equivalence is freely generated by a pulled-back line and the point-exceptional curves. Every one of these generators is defined over $k_0$. Their pushes into $Z$, and subsequent restrictions to $E$ in $K$-theory, are base changes of the same perfect proper-pushforward and pullback operations on the regular finite-type construction over $k_0$. Indeed $Z$ is obtained from that construction by flat base change and strict localization, so flat base change for these perfect closed immersions applies. The corresponding rational class on $E_0$ has no $K_2$ coefficient, because $K_2(k_0)_{\mathbf Q}=0$. Naturality of TS.1 under this base change therefore proves that every exceptional curve has zero last coordinate in (TC.2). Taking the weight-two Chern component gives precisely the ordinary Chow pushforward of its divisor class. This argument uses the actual $k_0$-defined generators; it does not assume that $K(Z)$ is a tensor base change of $K(Z_{k_0})$. \emph{Step 3: exceptional curves span all four degree coordinates.} TG.5 supplies an effective exceptional divisor $D=\sum_i a_iE_i$, with all $a_i>0$, such that $\mathcal O_Z(-D)|_E$ is ample. Choose a relatively ample line bundle $\mathcal H$ for $Z/\operatorname{Spec}R$, and let $H=c_1(\mathcal H)$. It can be chosen from the construction over $k_0$. Set \[ M_{ij}=\deg(E_iE_jH),\qquad A=\operatorname{diag}(a_i). \] All intersections are proper numerical intersections supported on the projective exceptional fibre. The matrix $M$ is symmetric. statement: B.1b. Explicit construction data and the semisimple motive (Proved, using Honda--Tate and numerical semisimplicity).. The preceding prescription specifies $X$ by a uniquely determined isogeny class and a product operation; every member of that class works. There is also a terminating, although inefficient, construction by equations. Compute the minimal polynomial $P_\alpha$ and the division algebra index $d$ from the local invariants in \citet[Th\'eor\`eme~1(ii)]{Tate1971}. The desired class has Frobenius polynomial $P_\alpha^d$ and dimension $g=d[\mathbb Q(\alpha):\mathbb Q]/2$. Enumerate projective equations over $\mathbb F_q$ together with regular group-law and inverse-law presentations, retaining smooth, geometrically connected, commutative group varieties of dimension $g$. These tests reduce to ideal membership, smoothness, and finite-type algebra over a finite field. Every abelian variety has such a finite presentation. Choose $\ell^a$ larger than twice every coefficient bound $\binom{2g}{j}q^{j/2}$ for its Frobenius polynomial. The finite \'etale group scheme $A[\ell^a]$ and its Frobenius action can be computed by finite algebra over finite fields. Its characteristic polynomial modulo $\ell^a$ has a unique integral lift within those bounds. Stop at the first polynomial $P_\alpha^d$. Honda--Tate proves termination. This gives an effective specification for every input $\lambda$; the general enumeration has not been run. The numerical motive $N=h^1(A_\alpha)^{\otimes i}$ is semisimple by \citet[Theorem~1]{Jannsen1992}. It is homogeneous of weight $i$ and has $\lambda$ as an intrinsic Frobenius eigenvalue. One does not need an unproved realization functor on all numerical motives for this last assertion. The K\"unneth projectors of an abelian variety are algebraic; the kernel from homological to numerical endomorphisms is nilpotent by \citet[Corollary~1]{Jannsen1992}. Frobenius acts semisimply on the cohomology of $A_\alpha^i$. Its nonzero spectral idempotent belonging to the minimal polynomial of $\lambda$ therefore cannot disappear in a nilpotent ideal. Consequently that eigenvalue remains on $N$. This proves the semisimple-motive form of the weak conjecture with $m=1$.

statement: B.2a. The exact set and the first weights (Proved).. The exact set of eigenvalues occurring in degree $i\geq0$, as $X$ varies, is the set of Weil $q$-integers of weight $i$. statement: B.3a. Products of weight-one numbers and the role of the field (Proved; Lead B2 refuted as an obstruction to realization).. For $i>0$, every such $\lambda$ is a product of exactly $i$ weight-one Weil $q$-integers: take $\alpha,\ldots,\alpha$ from B.1a. The additional root of unity may be $1$. For $i=0$, the Artin construction gives the root of unity itself. Thus every eigenvalue in question occurs in an effective tensor construction from abelian and Artin motives over the original field $\mathbb F_q$. There is no class-group obstruction to this assertion, because the weight-one factors were not required to lie in the original number field. Even if we insist that the factors lie in that field after changing the finite field, an explicit power is immediate: for $i>0$, $\lambda$ itself is a weight-one Weil $q^i$-integer, and $\lambda^i$ is the product of $i$ copies of it. This proves the proposed conclusion of Lead B1 with $m=i$ without splitting any divisors; B.1a is stronger. The unrestricted root argument also explains why the earlier study's designation of the strong conjecture in weights above one as open is incorrect.

statement: B.3b. The $\mathbb Q(\sqrt{-23})$ test, including an equation (Proved and computed).. Put $L=\mathbb Q(\sqrt{-23})$, $\omega=(1+\sqrt{-23})/2$, $\lambda=1+\omega$, and $q=2$. Then \[ \omega^2-\omega+6=0,\qquad \lambda^2-3\lambda+8=0,\qquad \lambda\bar\lambda=8. \] The prime $\mathfrak p=(2,\omega-1)$ satisfies $(\lambda)=\mathfrak p^3$: the conjugate prime $(2,\omega)$ does not divide $\lambda$, and its absolute norm is $8$. No algebraic integer of $L$ has norm $2$, since \[ N(a+b\omega)=a^2+ab+6b^2 =\left(a+\frac b2\right)^2+\frac{23b^2}{4} \] cannot equal $2$ for integers $a,b$. Hence the fixed-field factorization into weight-one Weil $2$-integers is impossible, although unrestricted realization is possible. We can also verify $h_L=3$ without relying on a table of quadratic forms. The Minkowski bound is $(2/\pi)\sqrt{23}<4$, so every ideal class has a representative of norm $1$, $2$, or $3$. Both $2$ and $3$ split, and $(\omega)=(2,\omega)(3,\omega)$ identifies the class of one prime over $3$ with the inverse class of one prime over $2$. The latter class is nontrivial by the norm-$2$ calculation and has cube one by $(\lambda)=\mathfrak p^3$. The possible representative classes are exactly its three powers. Here is an actual variety over $\mathbb F_2$. Let $\mathbb F_8=\mathbb F_2[t]/(t^3+t+1)$ and let \[ E/\mathbb F_8:\quad y^2+xy=x^3+x^2+(t+1). \] Its projective closure is nonsingular: in the affine chart a singular point would have $x=0$ and then $y=0$ from the two derivatives, which contradicts $t+1\ne0$; the unique point at infinity is nonsingular. Thus it is a smooth plane cubic with a rational origin. Exhaustive enumeration gives five affine points and the point at infinity, so $\#E(\mathbb F_8)=6$. The Frobenius polynomial is $T^2-3T+8$. Set $A=\operatorname{Res}_{\mathbb F_8/\mathbb F_2}E$, an abelian threefold. Its $H^1$ is the induced representation, so its Frobenius polynomial is $T^6-3T^3+8$; this is precisely the restriction-of-scalars calculation of \citet[\S3, Lemma~1]{Tate1971}. In fact $X=A$ already suffices. On $H^3(A)=\bigwedge^3H^1(A)$ the characteristic polynomial is \[ (T^2-3T+8)(T^6-24T^3+512)^3. \] To verify this identity without approximating roots, the supplied program forms the $20\times20$ exterior-cube matrix of the integral companion matrix of $T^6-3T^3+8$ and factors its characteristic polynomial over $\mathbb Q$. This proves that $\lambda$ occurs on $H^3(A_{\overline{\mathbb F}_2},\mathbb Q_\ell)$ for every $\ell\ne2$. The same program enumerates the three reduced primitive forms of discriminant $-23$, agreeing with $h_L=3$.

statement: B.4b. A finite presentation suitable for computation (Proved).. Choose one prime in each conjugate pair and identify $D^-=\mathbb Z^s$. statement: B.4c. The purported unpowered canonical point is not defined (Refuted; correction to R7).. There is no inclusion-valued homomorphism $M_0/\mu(L)\to L^\times$, $[u]\mapsto u$. Already $[1]=[-1]$ while $1\ne-1$. Consequently the ``point of $D(M_0/\mathrm{torsion})$ whose evaluation on $M_0$ is the inclusion'' used in R7 and its cited proof does not exist. This is a type error, independently of any class-group issue. More invariantly, the genuine tautological point is $f_0\in D(M_0)(\mathbb Q)$, the Galois-equivariant map $u\mapsto u$. It does not lie in $D(M_0)^0$, because its restriction to $\mu(L)$ is not trivial. Thus it has no lift from a connected norm-one torus into that identity component, for any $q$. For a concrete counterexample with vanishing divisor cokernel take $L=\mathbb Q(i)$ and $p=5$. With $a=(2+i)/(2-i)$ we have $M_0=\mu_4\times\langle a\rangle$, $C_{L,5}=0$; nevertheless $f_0(i)=i\ne1$, while every point of $D(M_0)^0$ evaluates $i$ as $1$. The assertion cannot be repaired merely by assuming that the divisor isogeny is an isomorphism. There is a second distinction. If $M=M(q,L)$ and $G=D(M)$, with $\varepsilon$ corresponding to $q\in M$, then \[ X^*((G/j(\mathbb G_m))^0)=M_0/\mu(L),\qquad X^*((\ker\varepsilon)^0)=(M/\mathbb Z q)/\mathrm{torsion}. \] These lattices are naturally isogenous, but cannot be identified without accounting for the possible factor $2$. On $M_0$ the natural anti-divisor map $m\mapsto\operatorname{div}(m/\bar m)$ is $2\operatorname{div}$, not $\operatorname{div}$.

statement: B.4d. Canonical powered points and an exact lifting criterion (Proved).. Put $r=|\mu(L)|$ and $T=D(M_0/\mu(L))$. For every integer $k$ divisible by $r$ there is a canonical point $g_k\in T(\mathbb Q)$ defined by $[u](g_k)=u^k$. Divisibility by $r$ is necessary and sufficient for this formula to be independent of the representative. Suppose $\tau\mathfrak p\ne\mathfrak p$, let $D_{\mathfrak p}\subset\operatorname{Gal}(L/\mathbb Q)$ be its decomposition group, and put $L_0=L^{D_{\mathfrak p}}$, $K_0=L_0\cap K$. Set \[ S_0=\operatorname{Res}_{K_0/\mathbb Q} \operatorname{Res}^{1}_{L_0/K_0}\mathbb G_m. \] The inclusion $\Lambda\subset D^-$ defines a $\mathbb Q$-isogeny $\phi:S_0\to T$. For $z\in L_0^\times$ with $z\bar z=1$ and $D=\sum n_{\mathfrak s}\mathfrak s\in D^-$, define \[ e_z(D)=\prod_{\mathfrak s\in S/\langle\tau\rangle} \sigma_{\mathfrak s}(z)^{n_{\mathfrak s}}, \qquad\sigma_{\mathfrak s}\mathfrak p=\mathfrak s. \] The product is independent of orientations and of representatives of the cosets $\sigma_{\mathfrak s}D_{\mathfrak p}$. Then the full set of rational lifts of $g_k$ is \[ \boxed{\ \{z\in L_0^\times: z\bar z=1,\quad e_z(\operatorname{div}u_j)=u_j^k\ (1\leq j\leq s)\}\ }, \] where $u_1,\ldots,u_s$ is any basis of $M_0/\mu(L)$ with chosen representatives. When nonempty it is a right torsor under $\ker\phi(\mathbb Q)$, acting by multiplication.

statement: C.1b (Refuted: $A,A',A''$ and algebraic up to torsion $=$ numerical).. The letter's $A$ fails by \eqref{eq:quintic-cokernel}. If $i:Y\hookrightarrow V$ is \emph{any} smooth hyperplane section, $A^1_{\mathrm{alg}}(Y)=\mathrm{NS}(Y)_{\mathbb Q}$ is finite dimensional, whereas $A^2_{\mathrm{alg}}(V)$ is infinite dimensional. Thus $i_*:A^1_{\mathrm{alg}}(Y)\to A^2_{\mathrm{alg}}(V)$ is not onto, which refutes $A'$. For $U=V\setminus Y$ there is an exact sequence \begin{equation} A^{r-1}_{\mathrm{alg}}(Y)\longrightarrow A^r_{\mathrm{alg}}(V)\longrightarrow A^r_{\mathrm{alg}}(U)\longrightarrow0. \end{equation} Consequently $A^2_{\mathrm{alg}}(U)$ is infinite dimensional, refuting $A''$ in its stated range $2r>\dim U$. To justify the equivalence relation in \eqref{eq:alg-localization}, we first use Chow localization. If the restriction of a cycle becomes algebraically equivalent to zero on $U$, we express that relation by fibres of finitely many cycles on $U\times T$, with $T$ smooth connected curves. We close these cycles in $V\times T$ and take their refined fibres. Their differences are algebraically trivial on $V$; the residual cycles restrict to zero on $U$, so Chow localization puts them on $Y$. This proves the required equality of kernels. It is not an argument for the corresponding assertion modulo homological equivalence. Every nonzero $g\in G$ is homologically, hence numerically, zero, but is nonzero modulo algebraic equivalence with rational coefficients. Thus the identification with numerical equivalence also fails for $\tau$-equivalence understood as algebraic equivalence up to torsion.

statement: C.1c (Proved: the precise divisor-to-curve statement over $\mathbb C$).. For every smooth projective complex $n$-fold, $n\ge2$, the map \[ L^{n-2}:\mathrm{NS}(X)_{\mathbb Q}\longrightarrow A^{n-1}_{\mathrm{alg}}(X) \] is injective and has cokernel canonically isomorphic to $G^{n-1}(X)$. Indeed, hard Lefschetz makes its cohomological realization injective. The inverse of the cohomological map carries a rational class of Hodge type $(n-1,n-1)$ to one of type $(1,1)$. The Lefschetz $(1,1)$ theorem represents the latter by a rational divisor. The image of every algebraic curve class is therefore the image of a unique rational divisor; after subtracting that image, its residue lies in $G^{n-1}(X)$. The intersection of this Griffiths group with the Lefschetz image is zero. This proves the assertion without assuming the full Hodge conjecture. The surjectivity criterion here is exactly $G^{n-1}(X)=0$. For each $n\ge3$, $X=V\times\mathbb P^{n-3}$ gives a counterexample: the projective bundle formula puts $G^2(V)t^{n-3}$ inside $G^{n-1}(X)$, where $t$ is the hyperplane class on the second factor. Thus $A$ fails universally in the divisor case in every dimension at least three, although it holds for an individual variety precisely under the stated vanishing condition.

statement: C.1f (Proved: the complete universal surjectivity classification for $A$).. Among the pairs $0\le i\le n/2$, the letter's $A$ holds for every smooth projective complex $n$-fold exactly when $i=0$ or $2i=n$. For every $1\le i<n/2$ there is a smooth projective counterexample with finite-dimensional $A^i_{\mathrm{alg}}$ and infinite-dimensional $A^{n-i}_{\mathrm{alg}}$. Thus it is surjectivity that fails in these examples. We now give one construction for every pair. Start with $X_3=V$ as in C.1a, embedded as a smooth Cartier divisor in $R_4=\mathbb P^4$. We inductively construct $X_{2i+1}$ as a smooth Cartier divisor in a smooth projective $R_{2i+2}$ whose Chow motive is a sum of Tate motives. Suppose that $X_{2i-1}\subset R_{2i}$ is already constructed, and write $D=X_{2i-1}$ for its divisor class. Set \[ S=R_{2i}\times\mathbb P^1, \qquad Z=X_{2i-1}\times\{0\}\subset S, \qquad X_{2i+1}=\operatorname{Bl}_Z(S). \] The centre is smooth of codimension two. It is the regular zero scheme of the section $(s_D,s_0)$ of \[ F=\operatorname{pr}_1^*\mathcal O_{R_{2i}}(D) \oplus\operatorname{pr}_2^*\mathcal O_{\mathbb P^1}(1). \] Let $R_{2i+2}=\mathbb P_{\mathrm{lines}}(F)$ over $S$. In this projective line bundle, the locus where the section of $F$ lies in the tautological line is a Cartier divisor, locally given by $s_0u-s_Dv=0$. Since $(s_D,s_0)$ is a regular sequence, this locus is exactly the blow-up $X_{2i+1}$. This is the elementary Rees-algebra presentation of the blow-up of a two-generated regular ideal. It is smooth because both $S$ and $Z$ are smooth. The ambient $R_{2i+2}$ is a projective bundle over $S$, so its Chow motive remains Tate, by the projective-bundle formula \citep[Lemma 45.6.1, Tag 0FGQ]{cyStacksProject}. The construction therefore iterates without requiring an unproved low-codimension projective-space embedding of a blow-up. The codimension-two blow-up formula, whose maps are algebraic correspondences and hence preserve algebraic equivalence \citep[Theorem 2.8(3)]{cyJiang2023}, gives \begin{equation} A^r_{\mathrm{alg}}(X_{2i+1}) \simeq A^r_{\mathrm{alg}}(S) \oplus A^{r-1}_{\mathrm{alg}}(X_{2i-1}). \end{equation} More explicitly, if $\pi:X_{2i+1}\to S$, $j:E\hookrightarrow X_{2i+1}$ and $q:E\to Z$ are the blow-up maps, the forward map is $(a,b)\mapsto\pi^*a+j_*q^*b$ and the inverse is $c\mapsto(\pi_*c,-q_*j^*c)$. We have $\pi_*j_*q^*=0$, $q_*j^*\pi^*=0$, and $j^*j_*q^*b=-\xi q^*b$ with $q_*\xi=1$. These identities check both projections directly; surjectivity is the blow-up formula. In particular all four maps commute with cycle classes and preserve algebraic equivalence. The analogous decomposition holds for cycle classes. Thus the only nonzero rational Griffiths group of $X_{2i+1}$ is \[ G^{i+1}(X_{2i+1})\simeq G^2(V)=G, \] and every $A^r_{\mathrm{alg}}(X_{2i+1})$ with $r\ne i+1$ is finite dimensional. This follows by induction from C.1a and the Tate property of $S$, and proves failure for $n=2i+1$. The same codimension-two decomposition for the quotient of any two adequate equivalence relations is already stated and proved in \citet[Proposition 13, p.~482]{cySamuel1960}; in particular it applies directly to the Griffiths quotient used here. For arbitrary $n\ge2i+1$, take $X=X_{2i+1}\times\mathbb P^{n-2i-1}$. The projective bundle formula puts its copies of $G$ exactly in codimensions $i+1,i+2,\ldots,n-i$. Consequently $A^i_{\mathrm{alg}}(X)$ is finite dimensional and $A^{n-i}_{\mathrm{alg}}(X)$ is infinite dimensional. No linear map between these spaces is onto, in particular no ample Lefschetz map is onto. The positive cases were proved in C.1d. It is useful to record why the simpler attempted construction $V\times\mathbb P^r$ does not prove all these pairs. Its Griffiths string has degrees $2,\ldots,r+2$. For $2\le i<(r+3)/2$, both $Gt^{i-2}$ and $Gt^{r+1-i}$ exist, and $L^{r+3-2i}$ maps one isomorphically to the other. Over $\mathbb C$, each of the following properties holds for every smooth projective connected $n$-fold exactly when $r\in\{0,1,n\}$, with repeated or inadmissible entries omitted: \begin{enumerate} \item the map $A^r_{\mathrm{alg}}(X)\to H^{2r}(X,\mathbb Q)$ is injective; \item algebraic equivalence up to torsion equals numerical equivalence in codimension $r$; \item $A^r_{\mathrm{alg}}(X)$ is finite dimensional over $\mathbb Q$. \end{enumerate} The corresponding assertion that cycles modulo algebraic equivalence up to torsion form a finitely generated abelian group has the same universal range. For $r=0,n$, degree gives the assertions. For $r=1$, the group is the N\'eron--Severi group modulo its finite torsion, which is finitely generated. The divisor cycle map is injective after tensoring with $\mathbb Q$; the Hodge index theorem identifies numerical and homological equivalence for divisors. These are the usual N\'eron--Severi and Lefschetz $(1,1)$ statements, also used in C.1c--d and \citet[\S3, especially 3.4 and 3.10]{cyKleiman1968}. Every remaining pair has $n\ge3$ and $2\le r\le n-1$. Take the very general quintic $V$ of C.1a and $X=V\times\mathbb P^{n-3}$. The projective-bundle formula supplies the direct summand \[ G^2(V)t^{r-2}\ \subset\ G^r(X), \qquad 0\le r-2\le n-3. \] It is infinite dimensional by the opened Clemens theorem. Every element is numerically trivial, and a nonzero one disproves (1) and (2); the infinite-dimensional summand disproves (3) and finite generation. This proof concerns universal assertions. For a specified variety the first property is exactly $G^r(X)=0$, while equality with numerical equivalence may additionally require the homological standard conjecture $D$. The letter's image criterion also fails in each of these target codimensions, even for the zero correspondence: its cohomological image contains the class of every $g\in G^r(X)$, but its cycle image does not contain a nonzero $g$. More generally, that criterion for all correspondences into a fixed $A^r_{\mathrm{alg}}(X)$ necessarily implies $G^r(X)=0$. This necessary condition alone does not prove the criterion, since an arbitrary cohomological preimage must still be represented by an algebraic cycle.

The divisor cycle map is injective, so there are no further off-diagonal components. The middle identification is the classical Picard-correspondence identification used in C.4a. Poincar'e complete reducibility makes $\operatorname{End}(J(C))_{\mathbb Q}$ a finite product of matrix algebras over division algebras. Hence the displayed algebra is finite and semisimple. For a specified surface counterexample, let the fourteen $t_\alpha$, indexed by $|\alpha|=4$ and $\alpha
e(4,0,0)$, be algebraically independent over $\mathbb Q$, and put \[ K=\mathbb Q(t_\alpha),\qquad F=x_0^4+\sum_{\substack{|\alpha|=4\\alpha
e(4,0,0)}} t_\alpha x^\alpha. \] Let $C\subset\mathbb P^2_{\overline K}$ be $F=0$. It is smooth, since the discriminant is not identically zero on this coefficient chart, as the Fermat quartic shows. e0$ modulo algebraic equivalence with rational coefficients. e a\in\operatorname{Jac}(R_S)$. No nilpotence conjecture or finite-dimensional-motive hypothesis is used. The universal auxiliary-product hypotheses in the letter's motivic argument cannot be replaced by hypotheses on $S$ alone. Finally take $X=S	imes\mathbb P^{n-2}$ for $n\ge2$, with projection $f:X	o S$ and a constant section $s:S	o X$. The class $a_X=f^*a s^*$ is nonzero because $s^*a_X f^*=a$. This gives the counterexample in every dimension $n\ge2$ and proves the stated universal range. statement: C.1n (Proved: the endpoint image criterion is exactly the universal standard conjecture $D$).. We first work over $\mathbb C$ with rational coefficients. Fix integers $n\ge0$ and $0\le r\le n$. Let $\mathcal I_{n,r}$ mean the following assertion: for every smooth projective connected $n$-fold $X$, every smooth projective connected $d$-fold $Y$, every $0\le j\le d$, and every correspondence \[ \Gamma\in\mathrm{CH}^{d+r-j}(Y\times X)_{\mathbb Q}, \] an element $z\in A^r_{\mathrm{alg}}(X)$ belongs to the image of $\Gamma_*:A^j_{\mathrm{alg}}(Y)\to A^r_{\mathrm{alg}}(X)$ if and only if its cycle class belongs to the image of \[ \Gamma_*:H^{2j}(Y,\mathbb Q(j)) \longrightarrow H^{2r}(X,\mathbb Q(r)). \] These are the source and degree-shift quantifiers of the image criterion on manuscript page $14{:}46$: its source degree is arbitrary, and the correspondence need not have degree zero. Write $D_{\mathbb C}$ for equality of numerical and Betti homological equivalence on rational cycles of every smooth projective complex variety. Then \begin{equation} \mathcal I_{n,r}\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad D_{\mathbb C} \qquad\text{if }r\in\{0,1,n\}. \end{equation} For every $2\le r\le n-1$, the assertion $\mathcal I_{n,r}$ is false by C.1k. If we restrict the target to $X=\mathbb P^n$, its image criterion is equivalent to $D_{\mathbb C}$ for \emph{every} $0\le r\le n$. More precisely, for a \emph{fixed} $X$ and $r$, let $\mathcal I(X,r)$ require the displayed criterion for every source $Y$, source degree $j$, and correspondence $\Gamma$. Then \begin{equation} \mathcal I(X,r)\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \bigl(D_{\mathbb C}\ \text{and}\ G^r(X)=0\bigr). \end{equation} \emph{Necessity, including the restricted projective-space target.} Suppose that $D_{\mathbb C}$ fails. Then some smooth projective $d$-fold $Y$ has a numerically trivial rational cycle $a\in\mathrm{CH}^s(Y)_{\mathbb Q}$ with $\mathrm{cl}(a)\ne0$. Put $j=d-s$, let $h$ be the hyperplane class on $\mathbb P^n$, and set \[ \Gamma=a\times h^r\in \mathrm{CH}^{s+r}(Y\times\mathbb P^n)_{\mathbb Q}. \] The codimension is $s+r=d+r-j$, as required. The action on cycles is \[ \Gamma_*b=\deg(a\cdot b)h^r=0 \qquad\bigl(b\in A^j_{\mathrm{alg}}(Y)\bigr), \] by numerical triviality. In contrast, Poincar\'e duality supplies $v\in H^{2d-2s}(Y,\mathbb Q(d-s))$ with $\int_Y\mathrm{cl}(a)v=1$. Hence $\Gamma_*v=\mathrm{cl}(h^r)$, although the nonzero cycle class $h^r\in A^r_{\mathrm{alg}}(\mathbb P^n)$ is not in the cycle image. This contradicts the proposed criterion. Notice that we neither need nor assert that this cohomological preimage $v$ is algebraic: the criterion itself would force an algebraic preimage, which numerical triviality excludes. The same construction works for any fixed target $X$: take $h$ ample on $X$; its power $h^r$ has nonzero cohomology class, since $\int_Xh^n>0$. Thus $\mathcal I(X,r)$ also implies $D_{\mathbb C}$. Taking $\Gamma=0$ shows separately that $\mathcal I(X,r)$ implies $G^r(X)=0$. \emph{Sufficiency.} Assume $D_{\mathbb C}$. By \citet[Theorem~1, pp.~448--449] {Jannsen1992}, the category of rational numerical motives is semisimple abelian. Betti realization on this category is well defined and faithful: $D_{\mathbb C}$ applies on every product, and K\"unneth together with Poincar\'e duality identifies a correspondence's total cohomology class with its action on all cohomological degrees. Here K\"unneth is only the cohomological decomposition; we do not assume algebraic K\"unneth projectors. We use the convention \[ \begin{split} \operatorname{Hom}(\mathbf1,h(X)(r)) &=A^r_{\mathrm{num}}(X),\\ \operatorname{Hom}(h(Y)(j),h(X)(r)) &=A^{d+r-j}_{\mathrm{num}}(Y\times X). \end{split} \] Thus $\Gamma$ induces a morphism $f:M=h(Y)(j)\to N=h(X)(r)$, and the numerical class of $z$ is a morphism $\beta:\mathbf1\to N$. Semisimplicity gives $g:N\to M$ for which $p=fg$ is a projector onto $\operatorname{im}(f)$ and $pf=f$. If $\mathrm{cl}(z)$ is in the stated cohomological image, then $H((1-p)\beta)=0$. Indeed realization in degree zero of $h(Y)(j)$ and $h(X)(r)$ is precisely the pair of groups in the displayed image criterion. Faithfulness gives $(1-p)\beta=0$, so \[ \beta=f(g\beta). \] Choose a rational cycle $b\in\mathrm{CH}^j(Y)_{\mathbb Q}$ representing $g\beta$. We have proved that $\Gamma_*b$ and $z$ are numerically equivalent. In target codimensions $r=0,n$, numerical and algebraic equivalence with rational coefficients are both determined by degree. In codimension $r=1$, the same equality follows from the N\'eron--Severi theorem and the divisor intersection pairing, as recalled in C.1k. Therefore $\Gamma_*b=z$ in $A^r_{\mathrm{alg}}(X)$ in every asserted endpoint case. The converse implication is always given by functoriality of the cycle class. For $X=\mathbb P^n$, the map $A^r_{\mathrm{alg}}(X)\to A^r_{\mathrm{num}}(X)$ is an isomorphism in every codimension, so the same proof gives the final restricted-target assertion. For the fixed-target assertion, $D_{\mathbb C}$ identifies numerical and homological equivalence, and $G^r(X)=0$ identifies homological and algebraic equivalence in the specified target group. The same numerical preimage therefore proves \eqref{eq:fixed-target-image-D}. These two equivalences are not restricted to complex geometry. Let $k$ be any algebraically closed field and let $H$ be a fixed Weil cohomology with characteristic-zero coefficient field $F$. Keep rational cycle coefficients, use $F$ in the cohomological image, and define $D_{k,H}$ by equality of numerical and $H$-homological equivalence for rational cycles on every smooth projective $k$-variety. The identical argument proves \[ \mathcal I_{n,r}^{k,H}\ \Longleftrightarrow\ D_{k,H} \qquad(r\in\{0,1,n\}), \] \[ \mathcal I^{k,H}(X,r)\ \Longleftrightarrow\ \bigl(D_{k,H}\ \text{and}\ G_H^r(X)=0\bigr), \] where $G_H^r(X)$ is the kernel of the rational-cycle class map into $H^{2r}(X)(r)$. The source functional is evaluated using Poincar\'e duality over $F$; the numerical-motive category and its image splitting still have rational coefficients. Numerical and algebraic equivalence agree rationally for divisors over any algebraically closed field, and degree handles codimensions zero and top. The intermediate-codimension universal counterexamples cited above remain assertions over $\mathbb C$; this extension does not transfer their nonvanishing to positive characteristic. Equations~\eqref{eq:endpoint-image-D}--\eqref{eq:fixed-target-image-D} isolate an exact remaining standard-conjecture gate. It does not prove $D_{\mathbb C}$ and does not replace homological equivalence by algebraic equivalence in intermediate target codimension. It also explains why the absence of a target Griffiths group by itself was insufficient for the image argument in C.1k: the unrestricted source can still detect a failure of $D$.

Then some smooth projective $d$-fold $Y$ has a numerically trivial rational cycle $a\in\mathrm{CH}^s(Y)_{\mathbb Q}$ with $\mathrm{cl}(a)\ne0$. Put $j=d-s$, let $h$ be the hyperplane class on $\mathbb P^n$, and set \[ \Gamma=a\times h^r\in \mathrm{CH}^{s+r}(Y\times\mathbb P^n)_{\mathbb Q}. \] The codimension is $s+r=d+r-j$, as required. The action on cycles is \[ \Gamma_*b=\deg(a\cdot b)h^r=0 \qquad\bigl(b\in A^j_{\mathrm{alg}}(Y)\bigr), \] by numerical triviality. In contrast, Poincar\'e duality supplies $v\in H^{2d-2s}(Y,\mathbb Q(d-s))$ with $\int_Y\mathrm{cl}(a)v=1$. Hence $\Gamma_*v=\mathrm{cl}(h^r)$, although the nonzero cycle class $h^r\in A^r_{\mathrm{alg}}(\mathbb P^n)$ is not in the cycle image. This contradicts the proposed criterion. Notice that we neither need nor assert that this cohomological preimage $v$ is algebraic: the criterion itself would force an algebraic preimage, which numerical triviality excludes. In codimension $r=1$, the same equality follows from the N\'eron--Severi theorem and the divisor intersection pairing, as recalled in C.1k. Therefore $\Gamma_*b=z$ in $A^r_{\mathrm{alg}}(X)$ in every asserted endpoint case. The converse implication is always given by functoriality of the cycle class. For $X=\mathbb P^n$, the map $A^r_{\mathrm{alg}}(X)\to A^r_{\mathrm{num}}(X)$ is an isomorphism in every codimension, so the same proof gives the final restricted-target assertion. For the fixed-target assertion, $D_{\mathbb C}$ identifies numerical and homological equivalence, and $G^r(X)=0$ identifies homological and algebraic equivalence in the specified target group. The same numerical preimage therefore proves \eqref{eq:fixed-target-image-D}. These two equivalences are not restricted to complex geometry. statement: C.1q (Proved: the exact exceptional polynomial and the ample-pencil test).. statement: C.2b (Proved: affine vanishing; the missing localization step).. For a smooth affine complex variety $U$ of dimension $n$, $H^j(U,\mathbb Q)=0$ for $j>n$. The algebraic de Rham complex has terms only in degrees $0,\ldots,n$; all its terms are quasi-coherent and thus acyclic on $U$. Its hypercohomology is consequently computed by a complex of global sections of length $n$. Comparison with analytic de Rham cohomology proves the assertion. In arbitrary characteristic the corresponding $\ell$-adic vanishing is Artin's affine theorem \citep[Expos\'e XIV, Corollaire 3.2]{cySGA4XIV}; passing from finite coefficients to $\mathbb Q_\ell$ gives the claimed range. Hence $A''_H$ is a theorem. The cohomological localization sequence yields, in that range, a surjection \[ H^{2r-2}(Y)(-1)\longrightarrow H^{2r}(X). \] Its surjectivity does not say that an \emph{algebraic} class on $X$ has an \emph{algebraic} preimage on $Y$. Chow localization applies only when the restricted cycle is zero in the Chow group, whereas $A''_H$ merely says that its restricted \emph{cohomology class} is zero. Accordingly the proof of \eqref{eq:alg-localization} cannot be reused for homological equivalence. This identifies a precise logical gap in the proposed deduction $A''_H\Rightarrow A'_H$; it is not a geometric counterexample to $A'_H$ itself.

statement: C.2c (Known comparison and proved positivity implication).. Hard Lefschetz proves injectivity in $A_H$; its surjectivity is the standard conjecture $A$. The global equivalence with algebraicity of the inverse Lefschetz operator is recorded in \citet[Corollary 2.14]{cyKleiman1968}. More precisely, $A(X\times X)$ implies $B_{\mathrm{std}}(X)$, whereas $B_{\mathrm{std}}(X)$ implies $A(X)$ and the algebraicity of the K\"unneth projectors \citep[Theorem 4-1]{cyKleiman1994}. The product hypothesis is material. Assume $A_H(X)$ and $H_{\mathrm{std}}(X)$ in all the degrees used in the Lefschetz decomposition. Each algebraic class decomposes into algebraic primitive classes: the inverse powers of $L$ needed in the recursive decomposition preserve algebraic classes by $A_H$. Define the usual Lefschetz star by reversing each $L$-string with its Hodge--Riemann sign. It again preserves algebraic classes. Positivity says that, for a nonzero algebraic class $x$, the complementary algebraic class $*x$ satisfies $\deg(x\,*x)>0$. Such an $x$ cannot be numerically zero. Thus homological and numerical equivalence agree under these two hypotheses. This is the mechanism behind the implication $A+H_{\mathrm{std}}\Rightarrow D$; removing algebraicity of the Lefschetz decomposition removes a used premise. Conversely, if $D(X)$ holds in complementary degrees, the numerical pairing identifies the two finite-dimensional numerical cycle spaces as duals. They therefore have the same dimension. Hard Lefschetz injectivity then makes $A_H(X)$ an isomorphism. This argument is about the full numerical pairing, not the asserted positivity of a single primitive middle space.

statement: C.2h (Proved): middle positivity and the positive trace form.. For homological cycle classes, the universal middle-dimensional positivity assertion $B_H$ in 14:45 implies the Hodge standard positivity assertion in every algebraic degree. We give the reduction, then specify exactly the additional Lefschetz hypothesis needed for its consequences on correspondences. Let $x\in A_H^r(X)$ be primitive, with $\dim X=n\ge2r$, and let $i:Y\hookrightarrow X$ be a smooth complete intersection of dimension $2r$ formed from the chosen hyperplanes. statement: C.2i (Proved under the preceding standard-conjecture hypotheses): semisimplicity and algebraic preimages.. Under C.2h's hypotheses, $E$ is semisimple. Indeed its Jacobson radical is preserved by the anti-involution $\dagger$. If $u$ belonged to that radical, then $u^\dagger u$ would be nilpotent and would have zero trace in cohomology. Positivity implies $u=0$. Thus the radical is zero. This proves the finite-algebra assertion of \citet[Corollary 3.12 and Lemma 3.13]{cyKleiman1968} in the present trace realization. With the hypotheses on all products, the same argument, or the numerical identification and \citet[Theorem 1]{Jannsen1992}, gives the semisimplicity of the idempotent-complete pure homological motive category. We also prove the full image criterion in 14:46, without assuming that a cohomological image automatically has an algebraic preimage. Let $u:H^a(X)\to H^b(Y)$ be induced by a rational algebraic correspondence, with the Tate twist matching its codimension. Work in the algebra of blocks on the direct sum of these two realizations. Put $x=u^\dagger u$. Left multiplication by $x$ on this finite-dimensional real algebra is self-adjoint for the trace inner product, so $x$ is semisimple. Its minimal polynomial has rational coefficients and no repeated root. By the Chinese remainder theorem there is $p(T)\in\mathbb Q[T]$ which is zero at $T=0$ and agrees with $1/T$ at every nonzero root of that minimal polynomial. Let \[ e_0=1-p(x)x,\qquad v=p(x)u^\dagger. \] The element $e_0$ is a self-adjoint idempotent with $xe_0=0$. Therefore \[ (ue_0)^\dagger(ue_0)=e_0xe_0=0, \] and trace positivity forces $ue_0=0$. It follows that \[ uvu=u. \] Every operator used is algebraic. If an algebraic class $z$ lies in the cohomological image of $u$, then $u(vz)=z$, and $vz$ is an algebraic class. The converse is immediate. This proves exactly the surjectivity-on-algebraic-images consequence, including maps that are neither injective nor surjective. It also constructs the projectors onto the image and kernel; the faithful realization verifies their idempotent identities. The argument is the explicit pseudo-inverse form of \citet[Corollary 3.14]{cyKleiman1968}. These assertions require both algebraic Lefschetz operators and the product positivity used above. Since universal middle $B_H$ gives $H_{\rm std}$, the remaining implication ``$B_H$ alone implies $D$'' has, under weak and hard Lefschetz, the exact further requirement $A_H$: C.2c gives $A_H+H_{\rm std}\Rightarrow D$ and $D\Rightarrow A_H$. Over $\mathbb C$, where Hodge--Riemann positivity already proves $B_H$, that requested implication has the full force of the universal standard conjecture $A_H$. We have not proved it by silently strengthening the meaning of the letter's $B$.

statement: C.2j (Proved under explicit hypotheses): the conditional Weil consequences.. Let $X/\mathbb F_q$ be smooth projective and geometrically connected of dimension $n$. Use geometric Frobenius on $\ell$-adic cohomology, $\ell\nmid q$, equivalently the pullback operator of the $q$-power Frobenius endomorphism. Suppose $B_{\rm std}(X)$ and Hodge standard positivity on $X\times X$ for the product polarization. Then its operators $F_i$ on $H^i(X_{\overline{\mathbb F}_q},\mathbb Q_\ell)$ are semisimple, their characteristic polynomials have integer coefficients, and every complex conjugate of every eigenvalue on $H^i$ has absolute value $q^{i/2}$. We give the argument in order to separate these conditional consequences from the already proved Weil conjectures themselves. First, $B_{\rm std}$ makes the cohomological projectors $\pi_i$ algebraic. Choose an integer $N>0$ clearing the denominators of a cycle representing $\pi_i$. For every $m\ge1$, the trace formula gives \[ \operatorname{Tr}(F_i^m)\in N^{-1}\mathbb Z. \] Indeed the supertrace of the composition of $\pi_i$ with the integral Frobenius correspondence of power $m$ is an intersection number; only degree $i$ survives, so the ordinary trace differs by $(-1)^i$. The same fixed $N$ works for every $m$. Newton's identities imply $P_i(t)=\det(1-tF_i)\in\mathbb Q[t]$. We include the bounded-denominator argument that removes every prime denominator, including the characteristic prime. If a finite multiset of algebraic numbers $\lambda_j$ has power sums in $N^{-1}\mathbb Z$ for all positive powers, each $\lambda_j$ is an algebraic integer. Otherwise, at some nonarchimedean place one of them has absolute value greater than one. The power series \[ \sum_{m\ge1}\left(\sum_j\lambda_j^m\right)t^m =-\frac{tP'(t)}{P(t)}, \qquad P(t)=\prod_j(1-\lambda_jt), \] has bounded coefficients at that place and is analytic on $|t|<1$. The rational function on the right has a pole at the reciprocal of such a $\lambda_j$, which lies in that disk. There is no cancellation: a nonzero root of $P$ of multiplicity $e$ contributes a logarithmic pole with nonzero residue proportional to $e$ in characteristic zero. This contradicts the power-series identity. Thus all eigenvalues are integral, and the rational elementary symmetric functions are integers. This is the mechanism in \citet[Proposition 2.6]{cyKleiman1968}; it requires no unproved removal of $p$-denominators. Let $L$ be an ample class defined over $\mathbb F_q$, and extend the scalar algebra from $\mathbb Q$ to $\mathbb Q(\sqrt q)\subset\mathbb R$. The normalized degree-wise operator \[ g=\sum_i q^{-i/2}F_i\pi_i \] is multiplicative, fixes $L$ because $F^*L=qL$, and acts as the identity on top cohomology because the Frobenius morphism has degree $q^n$. Poincar\'e duality therefore gives its transpose as $g^{-1}$. Since $g$ commutes with $L$, with the primitive projectors, and with Lefschetz star, its adjoint in C.2h is also $g^{-1}$: \[ g^\dagger g=1. \] Left multiplication by $g$ on the finite real correspondence algebra is an isometry for the positive trace inner product, since \[ \operatorname{Tr}((ga)^\dagger gb) =\operatorname{Tr}(a^\dagger b). \] It is consequently diagonalizable over $\mathbb C$, with eigenvalues on the unit circle. The left regular representation and the faithful cohomological representation have the same minimal polynomial for an algebra element: a polynomial in that element vanishes in one exactly when it vanishes in the algebra. Hence the same semisimplicity and absolute-value statement holds for $g$ in cohomology. On the invariant left ideal $\pi_iE_{\mathbb R}$, left multiplication by $g$ equals $q^{-i/2}$ times left multiplication by the rational algebra element $F_i\pi_i$. The latter has a rational minimal polynomial; every complex root occurs in its faithful left regular representation on that ideal. The isometry therefore controls every complex conjugate of $F_i$, not just one chosen embedding. Multiplying back by the positive real number $q^{i/2}$ proves the claimed weights. This supplies the linear algebra of \citet[Lemma 4.6 and Theorem 4.7]{cyKleiman1968}, with the product positivity and algebraic-projector premises visible. Finally the fixed-point formula and the formal identity \[ -\log\det(1-tF_i)=\sum_{m\ge1}\operatorname{Tr}(F_i^m)t^m/m \] give \[ Z(X,t)=\exp\left(\sum_{m\ge1}\#X(\mathbb F_{q^m})\frac{t^m}{m}\right) =\prod_{i=0}^{2n}P_i(t)^{(-1)^{i+1}}. \] Thus the numerator and denominator factors lie in $\mathbb Z[t]$; $P_0(t)=1-t$, $P_{2n}(t)=1-q^nt$, and the zeros of $P_i$ have absolute value $q^{-i/2}$. Poincar\'e duality pairs eigenvalues in complementary degrees by $\alpha\leftrightarrow q^n/\alpha$, yielding \[ Z\left(X,\frac1{q^nt}\right) =\epsilon\,q^{n\chi/2}t^\chi Z(X,t), \qquad \chi=\sum_i(-1)^i\dim H^i(X),\quad \epsilon\in\{1,-1\}. \] More precisely, with $\Delta=\prod_i\det(F_i)^{(-1)^{i+1}}$, the sign is $\epsilon=(-1)^\chi q^{n\chi/2}\Delta$; duality gives $\Delta^2=q^{-n\chi}$. We retain this determinant sign instead of assuming that it is fixed independently of Frobenius. Also $n\chi$ is even: when $n$ is odd, middle Poincar\'e duality is alternating and its dimension is even, while the other terms occur in complementary pairs. Rationality and the functional equation follow formally from the trace formula and duality; the extra standard-conjecture input above supplies the positive-involution proof of the absolute values and semisimplicity. It is not a proof of the general standard conjectures.

statement: C.3a (Proved exact obstruction sequence).. For $2r\le n$, put $q=n-2r$. The cycle class maps give a commutative diagram with exact rows \[ \begin{array}{ccccccccc} 0&\to&G^r(X)&\to&A^r_{\mathrm{alg}}(X)&\to&A^r_{\mathrm{hom}}(X)&\to&0\\ &&\downarrow L^q&&\downarrow L^q&&\downarrow L^q\\ 0&\to&G^{n-r}(X)&\to&A^{n-r}_{\mathrm{alg}}(X)&\to&A^{n-r}_{\mathrm{hom}}(X)&\to&0. \end{array} \] The last vertical map is injective by hard Lefschetz. The snake lemma therefore gives \[ \begin{split} \ker(L^q|A^r_{\mathrm{alg}})&=\ker(L^q|G^r),\\ 0\longrightarrow\operatorname{coker}(L^q|G^r)&\longrightarrow \operatorname{coker}(L^q|A^r_{\mathrm{alg}}) \longrightarrow\operatorname{coker}(L^q|A^r_{\mathrm{hom}}) \longrightarrow0. \end{split} \] Thus the general question contains two separate gates: the Lefschetz map on Griffiths groups, and standard-conjecture surjectivity on algebraic cohomology. Neither is disposed of by hard Lefschetz on the ambient cohomology. C.1c proves injectivity for $r=1$ over $\mathbb C$; C.1a identifies the requested quintic cokernel exactly. The higher injectivity problem has not been settled here.

statement: C.3aa (Refuted): every non-top positive-codimension local finiteness assertion over $\mathbb C$.. In particular the integral group $B^r(X)$ is not finite. Together with the divisor examples C.3v and C.3y, this settles every non-top positive-codimension pair $1\le r\le N-2$ over $\mathbb C$. This is a nonvanishing assertion; no infinite-dimensionality claim for these higher rational groups is made. The remaining top pair $r=N-1$, $N\ge3$, is not decided by this argument.

statement: C.3ab (Proved): integral top-cycle finiteness for surface cones with an explicit vanishing hypothesis.. Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero, $V$ a smooth projective integral surface over $k$, and $L$ a very ample line bundle whose full section ring \[ S=\bigoplus_{j\ge0}H^0(V,L^j) \] is normal and generated in degree one. Put \[ R=(S_{S_+})^{\mathrm{sh}},\qquad X=\operatorname{Spec}R\setminus\{\mathfrak m_R\},\qquad g=\gcd\{\deg(c_1(L)\cdot C):C\subset V \text{ an integral curve}\}. \] Assume the following cohomological condition, with \emph{absolute} K\"ahler differentials over $\mathbb Q$: \begin{equation} H^2(V,\Omega^1_{V/\mathbb Q}\otimes L^j)=0 \qquad(j\ge1). \end{equation} Then the natural maps from C.3e are isomorphisms, integrally: \begin{equation} \mathrm{CH}^2(X)\simeq \frac{\mathrm{CH}_0(V)}{c_1(L)\mathrm{CH}^1(V)}, \qquad B^2(X)\simeq\mathbb Z/g\mathbb Z. \end{equation} Here $B^2$ uses ordinary algebraic equivalence on actual fixed products with parameter curves. The integer $g$ is positive. Condition \eqref{eq:C3ab-absolute-vanishing} holds for every such surface over $\overline{\mathbb Q}$. Over an arbitrary $k$ as above, it holds if $H^2(V,L^j)=0$ for all $j\ge1$; in particular this includes $K3$ surfaces and surfaces with $p_g=0$. This statement does not settle arbitrary three-dimensional strict local germs, arbitrary complex surface cones, or the top groups in local dimension at least four.

statement: C.3ac (Known finite-field theorem and proved deductions; the strengthened cycle-class conclusion uses the cited 2026 input).. Let $k=\overline{\mathbb F}_p$, let $A/k$ be an abelian variety of dimension $g$, and let $h$ be any ample divisor class. Independently of the 2026 input in D.4c--e, we have \begin{equation} \begin{gathered} \mathrm{CH}^r(A)_{\mathbb Q,(s)}=0\quad(s\ne0),\qquad J^r(A)=0,\\ h^{g-2r}:\mathrm{CH}^r(A)_{\mathbb Q} \xrightarrow{\ \sim\ } \mathrm{CH}^{g-r}(A)_{\mathbb Q} \quad(2r\le g). \end{gathered} \end{equation} Consequently both abelian injectivity assertions of C.3h hold over this field; the first map is an isomorphism. The letter's $A$, $A'$ and $A''$ hold for these abelian varieties, with the same rational coefficients and degree ranges as in C.1. If we additionally invoke Theorem I of \citet{D_VanHoftenSempliner2026}, with exactly the source qualification in D.4c--e, then for every $r$ we also have \begin{equation} \mathrm{CH}^r(A)_{\mathbb Q} \xrightarrow{\ \sim\ } \mathrm{CH}^r(A)_{\mathrm{num},\mathbb Q}, \qquad G^r(A)=0. \end{equation} Under this same input the letter's strict $B$ holds for $A$. The analogous rational--numerical comparison holds on every product of abelian varieties and, more generally, on every smooth projective variety over a finite field whose \emph{Chow} motive is of abelian type. In the category generated by these Chow motives, numerical passage is an equivalence onto the corresponding semisimple numerical category. This last assertion does not include correspondences from arbitrary varieties outside that category.

statement: C.3ad (Proved in the stated rational smooth-cone scope): the top quotient over algebraic numbers..
