statement: F.2b (Known, with the supplied version corrected): numerical positivity cones.. The published \citet[Theorem 2.1 and Corollary 2.2, pp.~1799--1801]{rootDELV2011} give, on an $n$-fold power of a CM elliptic curve over $\mathbb C$, pseudoeffective classes equal to strongly positive forms and nef classes equal to weakly positive forms. The resulting strict difference has range $2\le k\le n-2$; the supplied early TeX's Corollary 2.2 instead prints the incorrect upper endpoint $n$. The published proof also correctly uses the \emph{closure} of the cone of rank-one forms from CM-lattice directions. Indeed the CM fraction field is dense in $\mathbb C$; approximate the coefficients of a one-form, clear denominators, and rescale its rank-one positive form. Each approximating form is a positive multiple of the pullback of the origin under a homomorphism $E^n\to E$. Closedness gives the asserted pseudoeffective limit. This verifies the step without the early version's stronger finite-combination wording. These are numerical cycle cones, distinct from the character cones in E.1.

statement: [Realization of invariant abelian subgroups] Choose the preceding data and put \[ P=\operatorname{Pic}^{\tau}_{Y/l},\qquad \mathcal R=\operatorname{Res}_{l/k}(P),\qquad \mathcal A=\mathcal R^\Gamma. \] Let $H\hookrightarrow\mathcal A$ be an abelian variety over $k$. More precisely, let $\Gamma_0$ be the kernel of the action on $l$, put $n=|\Gamma_0|$, and choose $q=p^e$ with $K'^q\subset K$. We may take $Q$ to be a torsor under $(H^\vee)^{(q)}$, and the resulting homomorphism is \[ H^{(q)}\xrightarrow{V_H^e}H\xrightarrow{[n]}H \hookrightarrow\mathcal R. \tag{B.2.14} \] Here $V_H^e$ is the dual of the $e$-fold relative Frobenius of $H^\vee$; it is an isogeny. In particular the image assertion does not require either $n$ or $q$ to be prime to $p$.

statement: [Proved: a complete intrinsic criterion for C.1(iii)] Let $S$ be a connected reduced noetherian $k$-scheme, with its fixed geometric point $a$, and put $A=\Gamma(S,\mathcal O_S)$. The objects of $\mathcal C$ are all finite groups $G_0\times_k S$, and its maps are all $S$-group homomorphisms. The following alternatives give a necessary and sufficient criterion for Proposition~4 for every such $S$, including every nonnormal $S$. \begin{enumerate} \item If $\operatorname{char}k=p>0$ and $A$ is not a field, the assertion is false. \item If $\operatorname{char}k=p>0$ and $A=L$ is a field, use this field $L$ in the criterion below. \item If $\operatorname{char}k=0$, let $L\subset A$ be the field of elements algebraic over $k$, and use this $L$ in the criterion below. There is no requirement that $A$ itself be a field. \end{enumerate} In alternatives (2) and (3), view $S$ as an $L$-scheme and let $\Pi=\pi^{\mathrm{fin},L}_{S,a}$ be the pro-finite $L$-group representing geometrically pointed torsors under \emph{all} finite $L$-groups and $L$-homomorphisms. Its existence follows from Theorem~\ref{C:k-morphisms} and Proposition~\ref{C:criterion}. Then Proposition~4 holds if and only if the following condition holds: \smallskip \noindent\emph{For every finite $k$-group $G_0$ and every proper closed $L$-subgroup $J\subsetneq G_{0,L}$ that is a faithfully flat finite quotient of $\Pi$, there exists a proper closed subgroup $H\subsetneq G_{0,L}$ containing $J$ such that $H\simeq H_0\times_k L$ for a finite $k$-group $H_0$.} \smallskip The isomorphism in this condition is an isomorphism of group schemes; its embedding into $G_{0,L}$ may be defined over $L$. In particular, the condition is automatic if $L=k$. Equivalently, the condition says that every torsor minimal among the constant $k$-group objects has full monodromy in the category of all finite $L$-groups. It is an exact descent criterion, not a claim that the field $L$ alone determines the answer.

statement: [Proved: an exact categorical criterion] Fix a connected base and a category $\mathcal C$ of finite locally free groups with the specified allowed group maps. Suppose the category contains the trivial group and zero homomorphisms, and has products and equalizers represented by its scheme-theoretic group equalizers, with their universal maps allowed. For the pointed-torsor functor $Z_a$, the following are equivalent: \begin{enumerate} \item Proposition 4 holds for every minimal class in $Z_a$. \item For every pair $u,v\colon G\rightrightarrows G'$ in $\mathcal C$ and $E=\operatorname{Eq}(u,v)$, the map \[ Z_a(E)\longrightarrow \{\alpha\in Z_a(G):u_*\alpha=v_*\alpha\} \] is surjective. \end{enumerate} If in addition every allowed homomorphism has its scheme-theoretic image factorization in $\mathcal C$, with both the map onto the image and the closed immersion allowed, these conditions are equivalent to pro-representability of $Z_a$ by an inverse system of objects of $\mathcal C$ with faithfully flat transition maps. This is a necessary and sufficient criterion for an arbitrary such triple of base, category, and allowed morphisms; the preceding theorem verifies it under the actual manuscript hypotheses. All these requirements on the factor maps hold for the $k$-defined and all-$S$ homomorphism categories used below. Membership of the image object alone would not suffice for an arbitrary restricted collection of allowed maps.

statement: [Proved: a degree-linear total jet budget on A-blocks] Consider a negative-definite exceptional configuration on a regular surface, partitioned into a complementary set of curves $\{C_a\}$ and pairwise disjoint $A$-chain blocks. Assume the intersections between the complementary curves and each block are transverse, occur at pairwise distinct smooth points of that block, and are away from its nodes. After contracting a block, regard these fixed formal branches on its resolution as the $B_i$ of the preceding proposition. For comparisons of full sheaves of reflexive modules on the contracted rational double points, their branch compatibility is determined by finite subschemes whose total length satisfies \[ \sum_{\text{blocks }\alpha}\operatorname{length}(T_\alpha) \le 2\sum_a(-C_a^2). \tag{D.JF.10} \] An entire isolated rational double point component with no attachments contributes no jet conditions. If it is not of type $A$, this last assertion is still the unframed vanishing of Lemma~\ref{D:RDP-full-Hom-vanishing}; the framed estimate here is asserted only for the stated $A$-blocks. In the degree-$n$ punctured-cover setting of Proposition~\ref{D:punctured-cover-linear-resolution}, whenever the stated transverse block conditions and full-sheaf comparison hold, (D.JF.10) is $O(n)$. The corresponding total number of linear conditions for maps between ranks $r,s$ is $O(nrs)$. This is a finite-jet placement and dimension estimate; it does not construct an effective hereditary object atlas.

statement: [Proved: finite jets for transverse A-chain framings] Let $k$ be algebraically closed, let $N\ge2$, and let $\pi:Y\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ be the minimal resolution of $A=k[[u,v,w]]/(uv-w^N)$. statement: [Proved: an exact two-end framing bound on an A-chain] Let $k$ be algebraically closed, let $N\ge2$, and put \[ A=k[[u,v,w]]/(uv-w^N). \] Let $\pi:Y\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ be the minimal resolution. Let $B_-$ and $B_+$ be the strict transforms of the two reduced coordinate branches $(v,w)$ and $(u,w)$, respectively, and put $B=B_-+B_+$. For any reflexive modules $M,N'$ of ranks $r,s$, with full sheaves $\mathcal F,\mathcal G$, one has \[ \dim_kH^1(Y,\mathcal Hom(\mathcal F,\mathcal G)(-B)) \le2rs. \tag{D.HF.3} \] This bound is independent of the chain length and of the characteristic, including when it divides $N$. More precisely, set $I_0=A$ and $I_a=(u,w^a)$ for $1\le a<N$. There are decompositions \[ M\simeq\bigoplus_{a=0}^{N-1}I_a^{r_a},\qquad N'\simeq\bigoplus_{a=0}^{N-1}I_a^{s_a}, \] and the dimension in (D.HF.3) is exactly \[ rs+r s_0-r_0s. \tag{D.HF.4} \] This is a classification and calculation for individual modules; no decomposition of arbitrary Artinian families is asserted.

statement: [Proved: cohomologically flat full-neighbourhood realization] Let $A$ be a complete excellent normal local surface with algebraically closed coefficient and residue field $k$. Let $\pi:Y\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ be a projective regular resolution, an isomorphism on the puncture, and let $Z$ be a reduction cycle of full exceptional support in the sense of Theorem~\ref{D:reduction-cycle-full-module-correspondence}. The characteristic of $k$ is arbitrary. Let $T$ be a finite-dimensional local Artinian $k$-algebra with residue field $k$, put $A_T=A\otimes_kT$ and $Y_T=Y\times_kT$, and let $V_2$ be a vector bundle on $(2Z)_T$. Write $V=V_2|_{Z_T}$ and $V_0=V\otimes_Tk$. Assume: \begin{enumerate} \item $V_0$ is generically generated by its global sections; \item for $W=V$ and $W=V(Z)$, both $H^0(Z_T,W)$ and $H^1(Z_T,W)$ are finite free over $T$, and their formation commutes with every homomorphism from $T$ to a finite local Artinian $k$-algebra with residue field $k$; \item the actual sequence \[ 0\longrightarrow V\longrightarrow V_2(Z) \longrightarrow V(Z)\longrightarrow0 \] has a split injective boundary \[ \delta_0:H^0(Z_T,V(Z))\longrightarrow H^1(Z_T,V). \tag{D.AR.1} \] \end{enumerate} There is a vector bundle $\mathcal F_T$ on $Y_T$ restricting to the given $V_2$. Every such vector-bundle extension has the following properties. Its module $M_T=H^0(Y_T,\mathcal F_T)$ is finite over $A_T$, is flat over $T$, and has maximal Cohen--Macaulay closed fibre. There are natural identifications \[ \begin{split} M_T&=H^0(Y_T\setminus Z_T,\mathcal F_T),\\ (\pi_T^*M_T)^{\vee\vee}&\simeq\mathcal F_T , \end{split} \tag{D.AR.2} \] where the double dual is taken over $\mathcal O_{Y_T}$. Moreover, for every homomorphism $T\to T'$ as in item~(2), \[ M_T\otimes_TT'\ \simeq\ H^0(Y_{T'},\mathcal F_T\otimes_TT'). \tag{D.AR.3} \] In particular these are actual relative maximal Cohen--Macaulay modules with their full vector-bundle pullbacks, not only fibrewise realizations. The hypotheses retain the second neighbourhood and the cohomology base-change conditions. The theorem does not assert that arbitrary families of bundles on $Z$ satisfy them, that a prescribed map on $Z$ lifts, or that a choice of extension $\mathcal F_T$ is functorial in $V_2$.

statement: [Proved: Gorenstein log canonical exceptional configurations] Let $(S,s)$ be a normal Gorenstein log canonical surface singularity over an algebraically closed field $k$, in arbitrary characteristic. On its minimal regular resolution, precisely one of the following possibilities occurs: \begin{enumerate} \item the exceptional fibre is empty, or it is a simple normal crossings tree of smooth rational curves, each of self-intersection $-2$, and every discrepancy is zero; \item the exceptional fibre is one smooth elliptic curve, of discrepancy $-1$; \item the exceptional fibre is a nodal cycle of rational curves, and every discrepancy is $-1$. A single irreducible nodal rational curve is allowed in this description. \end{enumerate} After blowing up the node in the last single-component case, the cycle has smooth components. On every further regular resolution, the elliptic or cyclic core persists; point blowups only subdivide edges of the cyclic core or attach rational trees. Every component of a cyclic core still has discrepancy $-1$.

statement: [Proved: arbitrary SNC residues and mixed-root coefficient gerbes] Let \(R\) be a complete excellent normal local surface algebra over an algebraically closed coefficient and residue field \(k\) of characteristic \(p>0\). Let \(Y\to\operatorname{Spec}R\) be a projective regular resolution, an isomorphism on the puncture \(U\), whose nonempty reduced exceptional divisor \(E=\bigcup_{i=1}^{v}E_i\) is strict normal crossings. Its connected dual graph \(G\) may have cycles or parallel edges. Write \(g_i=g(E_i)\), \(b_1=b_1(G)\), and \(N=(-(E_i\cdot E_j))_{ij}\). For every \(n\) prime to \(p\), there is an exact sequence \[ 0\longrightarrow\bigoplus_iH^1(E_i,\mathbb Z/n) \longrightarrow\operatorname{Br}'(U)[n] \longrightarrow H_1(G,\mathbb Z/n)(-1) \longrightarrow0, \tag{D.GG.1} \] and \[ |H^2(U,\mu_n)| =|\operatorname{coker}(N\bmod n)|\, n^{\,2\sum_i g_i+b_1} \leq|\det N|\,n^{\,2\sum_i g_i+b_1}. \tag{D.GG.2} \] The last map in (D.GG.1) records the secondary residues. Fix \(\alpha\in H^2(U,\mu_n)\) whose Brauer image \(\beta\) is represented by an Azumaya algebra on \(U\); in particular this holds for a projective finite local system. Let \(m_i\) be the order of the generic residue of \(\beta\) on \(E_i\), with \(m_i=1\) for zero residue. Then \(M=\operatorname{lcm}_i m_i\) is the order of \(\beta\), and the actual coefficient class \(\alpha\) extends to the mixed-root stack \[ \mathcal X=\prod_Y\sqrt[m_i]{(Y,E_i)}. \tag{D.GG.3} \] At an edge \(x\in E_i\cap E_j\), let \(h_x\) be the order of its secondary residue. Then \(h_x\mid\gcd(m_i,m_j)\). The inertia of the extended \(\mu_n\)-gerbe at \(x\) is a central extension \[ 1\longrightarrow\mu_n\longrightarrow D_x \longrightarrow\mu_{m_i}\times\mu_{m_j} \longrightarrow1, \tag{D.GG.4} \] whose scalar-weight-one commutator has order \(h_x\). It need not be commutative. There is an algebraic scalar-weight-one generating bundle on the coefficient gerbe. Its rank is not used in a coordinate bound.

statement: [Proved: tree residues and the actual coefficient gerbe] Let $R$ be a complete excellent normal local surface over an algebraically closed coefficient and residue field $k$ of characteristic $p>0$. Let $Y\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ be a projective regular resolution, an isomorphism over the puncture $U$, and let $E=\bigcup_{i=1}^v E_i$ be its reduced exceptional divisor. Suppose $E$ is strict normal crossings and its dual graph is a tree. Write $g_i=g(E_i)$ and $N=(-(E_i\cdot E_j))_{ij}$. For every $n$ prime to $p$, residue gives an isomorphism \[ \operatorname{Br}'(U)[n]\simeq \bigoplus_i H^1(E_i,\mathbb Z/n),\qquad |H^2(U,\mu_n)|=|\operatorname{coker}(N\bmod n)| n^{2\sum_i g_i}. \tag{D.TR.1} \] In particular the latter order is at most $|\det N|n^{2\sum_i g_i}$. All secondary residues at the nodes vanish. A class $\beta$ of prime-to-$p$ order $m$ is killed by a connected cyclic degree-$m$ cover $Y'\to Y$ which is etale on all of $Y$. Its restriction to $U$ is the puncture of a finite complete local normal extension of $R$. The exceptional divisor upstairs need not have a tree as its dual graph. Let $\alpha\in H^2(U,\mu_n)$ have Brauer image $\beta$, and let $m_i$ be the order of the $i$th residue, with $m_i=1$ for zero residue. Then $m_i\mid m\mid n$, and the actual class $\alpha$ extends to \[ \mathcal X=\sqrt[m_1]{(Y,E_1)}\times_Y\cdots \times_Y\sqrt[m_v]{(Y,E_v)}. \tag{D.TR.2} \] At a node $E_i\cap E_j$, the restriction of its gerbe to $B(\mu_{m_i}\times\mu_{m_j})$ has zero geometric Brauer class. Its inertia is therefore a commutative diagonalizable extension of $\mu_{m_i}\times\mu_{m_j}$ by $\mu_n$. No nontrivial node commutator is discarded in this statement: the tree hypothesis forces that commutator to vanish.

statement: [Proved under stated hypotheses: one horizontal tame condition] Let $k$ be algebraically closed, let $C/k$ be a smooth proper connected curve, and choose distinct points $b_0,b_1,b_2\in\mathbb P^1(k)$ and distinct points $c_1,c_2\in C(k)$. There is a constant $A_R^{\rm sl}$ such that, for every open subgroup $H\subset\Gamma$ of index $t$, every $q=p^f$, every $r\ge1$, and every fixed continuous character \[ \chi:H\longrightarrow \operatorname{Gal}(\mathbb F_q/\mathbb F_p), \tag{D.SH.2} \] the representations \[ H\longrightarrow \operatorname{GL}_r(\mathbb F_q) \rtimes\operatorname{Gal}(\mathbb F_q/\mathbb F_p) \quad\text{with field projection }\chi \tag{D.SH.3} \] have at most $q^{A_R^{\rm sl}tr^2}$ conjugacy classes under $\operatorname{GL}_r(\mathbb F_q)$. There is no tameness condition on either cover, no bound on the field-image order, and no assumption that the field character extends over a resolution.

statement: [Proved: arbitrary field-character lifting classes] Let \(R\) be a fixed complete excellent normal local surface algebra over an algebraically closed coefficient and residue field \(k\) of characteristic \(p>0\), and put \(\Gamma=\pi_1(U_R)\), where \(U_R=\operatorname{Spec}R-\{\mathfrak m_R\}\). Let \(H\subset\Gamma\) be open of index \(t\), let \(q=p^f\), and fix a continuous field character \[ \chi:H\longrightarrow\operatorname{Gal}(\mathbb F_q/\mathbb F_p). \tag{D.WH.1} \] Write \(a=|\operatorname{im}\chi|\), \(\nu=f/a\), \(q_0=p^\nu\), and \(n=q-1\). Let \(U_H\) be the puncture corresponding to \(H\), and let \(V=U_V\to U_H\) be the connected cyclic cover corresponding to \(\ker\chi\). Its complete normal local cover ring \(A_V\) has degree \(ta\) over \(R\). Let \(\mathcal M_\chi\) be the locally constant sheaf with fibre \(\mathbb F_q^\times\) and its prescribed field action. There is a deck-equivariant SNC resolution of \(A_V\) with \(v_V=O_R(ta)\) exceptional components such that \[ \begin{aligned} |H^2_{\mathrm{cont}}(H,\mathbb F_q^\times(\chi))| &\le |H^2_{\mathrm{et}}(U_H,\mathcal M_\chi)|\\ &\le(q_0+1)^{\,4p_g(A_V)+3v_V} \le q^{c_Rt}. \end{aligned} \tag{D.WH.2} \] The constant \(c_R\) is independent of \(H,q,\chi,a\). Neither the cover nor the field character is assumed tame along an exceptional divisor; in particular \(p\mid a\) is allowed.

statement: [Proved: twisted scalar classes on arbitrary punctured covers] Let $R$ be a complete excellent normal local surface with algebraically closed coefficient and residue field $k$ of characteristic $p>0$, and put $\Gamma=\pi_1(\operatorname{Spec}R\setminus\{\mathfrak m\})$. Let $H\subset\Gamma$ be open of index $t$, let $q=p^f$, and fix a continuous field character \[ \chi:H\longrightarrow\operatorname{Gal}(\mathbb F_q/\mathbb F_p). \tag{D.WD.1} \] Write $d=|\operatorname{im}\chi|$, $q_0=p^{f/d}$, and $n=q-1$. Let $A_V$ be the normal complete local ring of the connected punctured cover corresponding to $\ker\chi$; its degree over $R$ is $td$. Let $v_V$ be the number of exceptional components on its minimal regular resolution. Use $v_V=0$ if $A_V$ is regular. Then \[ \bigl|H^1(H,\mathbb F_q^{\times}(\chi))\bigr| \le(q_0+1)^{2p_g(A_V)+v_V} \le q^{c_Rt}, \tag{D.WD.2} \] where $c_R$ is independent of $H,q,\chi$ and $d$. The action on the coefficient group is the prescribed field action. There is no tameness assumption, and $d$ is allowed to be divisible by $p$. In particular (D.WD.2) bounds the possible twisted scalar determinant classes of rank-$r$ representations into $\operatorname{GL}_r(\mathbb F_q)\rtimes\operatorname{im}\chi$ with fixed field character, independently of $r$. It does not assert a representation count for that group.

statement: [Proved: arbitrary-quotient linear crowns and bounded residual outer actions] Let $R$ be a complete excellent normal local surface with algebraically closed coefficient and residue field $k$ of characteristic $p>0$, and put $\Gamma=\pi_1(\operatorname{Spec}R\setminus\{\mathfrak m\})$. Let $A_R$ be the constant in Theorem~\ref{D:arbitrary-cover-ordinary-hereditary-growth}. Fix an integer $b_0\ge1$ and a real number $\kappa>0$. Let $S$ be a finite nonabelian simple group, identified with its inner automorphism group, and suppose \[ S\le\mathcal B_0\mathrel{\trianglelefteq}\mathcal B \le\operatorname{Aut}(S),\qquad [\mathcal B:\mathcal B_0]\le b_0. \tag{D.AL.1} \] Assume there is a faithful linear embedding \[ \mathcal B_0\hookrightarrow\operatorname{GL}_r(\mathbb F_q), \qquad q=p^f,\qquad r^2\log q\le\kappa\log|S|. \tag{D.AL.2} \] No embedding of $\mathcal B$ into an ambient matrix group is required. Let $\Omega$ have $t$ elements and let \[ P\le(\mathcal B/S)^\Omega\rtimes\operatorname{Sym}(\Omega) \tag{D.AL.3} \] have transitive permutation action. Let $L$ be its full inverse image in $\mathcal B^\Omega\rtimes\operatorname{Sym}(\Omega)$, and assume $L$ is monolithic primitive with socle $N=S^\Omega$. Write $L_k$ for its $k$th crown-based power, that is the fibre product of $k$ copies of $L$ over $P$. For every continuous surjection $\Gamma\twoheadrightarrow L_k$ one has \[ \begin{split} k&\le |N|^{c_R},\\ d(L_k)&\le\max\{2,d(P),c_R+2\},\\ c_R&=\max\{1,\lceil\kappa(A_Rb_0+1)+b_0-1\rceil\}. \end{split} \tag{D.AL.4} \] There is no ramification or resolution-extension condition on the induced quotient $\Gamma\twoheadrightarrow P$. Its generator number $d(P)$ is retained explicitly. In particular, take $\mathcal B_0=\mathcal B=S$. For every faithful $S\hookrightarrow\operatorname{GL}_r(\mathbb F_q)$ satisfying (D.AL.2), every transitive $P\le\operatorname{Sym}(t)$, and every quotient \[ \Gamma\twoheadrightarrow (S^t)^k\rtimes P \tag{D.AL.5} \] with pure permutation action, the same conclusions hold with $c_R=\max\{1,\lceil\kappa(A_R+1)\rceil\}$. If a chosen subfamily has $d(P)\le d_0$, then its crowns have at most $\max\{2,d_0,c_R+2\}$ generators. No uniform bound on $d(P)$, and no full finite-generation conclusion for $\Gamma$, is asserted without that hypothesis.

statement: [Proved: defining-characteristic symplectic and orthogonal crowns] Let $R$ be a complete excellent normal local surface ring with algebraically closed coefficient and residue field of characteristic $p>0$, and put $\Gamma=\pi_1(\operatorname{Spec}R\setminus\{\mathfrak m\})$. Write $A^{\rm ps}_{R,2}$ for the constant of Theorem~\ref{D:bounded-period-semilinear-hereditary-projective-growth} with period bound two. Let $S$ be one of the nonabelian simple groups in the following table, where $q=p^f$. The symbols $d$ and $Q$ specify the actual faithful projective-semilinear model used in the proof. \[ \begin{array}{c|c|c|c} S\text{ and range}&d&Q&[\operatorname{Aut}(S):\mathcal A_0]\\ \hline \operatorname{PSp}_{2\ell}(q),\ \ell\ge2, (\ell,q)\ne(2,2) &2\ell&q&2\ (\ell=2,\ p=2),\ 1\ \text{otherwise}\\ \operatorname{P}\Omega_{2\ell+1}(q),\ \ell\ge3, q\text{ odd} &2\ell+1&q&1\\ \operatorname{P}\Omega^+_{2\ell}(q),\ \ell\ge4 &2\ell&q&6\ (\ell=4),\ 2\ (\ell\ge5)\\ \operatorname{P}\Omega^-_{2\ell}(q),\ \ell\ge4 &2\ell&q^2&1 \end{array} \tag{D.SO.1} \] Here $\mathcal A_0$ is the normal inner-diagonal-field subgroup in the root-coordinate model of Corollary~\ref{D:classical-defining-characteristic-crowns}. Let $L$ be any finite monolithic primitive group with socle $N=S^t$, put $P=L/N$, and fix any continuous epimorphism $\beta:\Gamma\to P$. If $\Gamma\twoheadrightarrow L_k$ is a crown quotient over $\beta$, then \[ \begin{aligned} k&\le |N|^{c_R},\\ d(L_k)&\le\max\{2,d(P),c_R+2\},\\ c_R&=\max\{1,\lceil96A^{\rm ps}_{R,2}+21\rceil\}. \end{aligned} \tag{D.SO.2} \] The constant is independent of $q$, classical rank, $t$, the field-image orders and the prescribed permutation quotient. No radial-tameness or resolution-extension condition on that quotient is imposed. The term $d(P)$ is retained. Odd-dimensional orthogonal groups in characteristic two, when denoted separately, are included through their symplectic identification in the same range. The table makes no assertion about omitted low-rank repetitions or nonsimple exceptions.

statement: [Known: the invertible-prime arithmetic $K(\pi,1)$ theorem] Let $K$ be a number field, let $S$ be a finite set of finite places, and let $X=\operatorname{Spec}\mathcal O_K\setminus S$. For every prime $\ell$ invertible on $X$, the pro-$\ell$ completion of the \'etale homotopy type of $X$ is a $K(\pi,1)$. In particular, all of its higher homotopy pro-groups, including its second one, vanish. This includes $\ell=2$ when $K$ has real places, on the ordinary \'etale site.

statement: [Proved: arithmetic tame $K(\pi,1)$ for all permitted coefficients] Let $X_0=\operatorname{Spec}\mathcal O_K\setminus S$, let $D$ be any finite reduced divisor on $X_0$, and put $U=X_0\setminus D$. Let $\mathcal L$ be the set of rational primes invertible on $X_0$; equivalently, $\ell\in\mathcal L$ if and only if every place of $K$ above $\ell$ lies in $S$. Let $\pi=\pi_1^t(U/X_0)$ classify finite \'etale covers of $U$ tamely ramified along $D$. For every finite discrete $\pi$-module $M$ whose order has prime divisors in $\mathcal L$, and every $q\geq0$, the comparison is an isomorphism \[ H^q(\pi,M)\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }H^q_{\mathrm{et}}(U,M). \] The permitted-prime second tame homotopy pro-group is zero: $\Pi_2^{t,\mathcal L}(U/X_0)=0$. Thus every pair $(K,S)$ has the $K(\pi,1)$ property asked for with tame coefficients prime to all residue characteristics of $X_0$. For $K=\mathbb Q$ and $D$ empty, this gives $\Pi_2^t(\operatorname{Spec}\mathbb Z-S)=0$ in that coefficient convention, with allowed primes exactly $S$.

statement: [Proved: the exact criterion over an arbitrary base] Keep $f,X,Y,j,h,G$ as above, but let $S$ be an arbitrary scheme. Write $i:Y\hookrightarrow X$ and $g=f i$, and define the boundary cohomology complex \[ C_Y(G)=Rg_*i^*Rj_*G. \] Then all $R^q h_*G$ are locally constant if and only if the following two conditions hold: \begin{enumerate} \item Every cohomology sheaf $\mathcal H^q C_Y(G)$ is constructible (locally on $S$). \item The boundary hypercohomology in \eqref{D:boundary-condition} vanishes for every geometric specialization $\bar s\leftarrow\bar t$. \end{enumerate} In relative dimension one the second condition is pointwise vanishing on the finite geometric boundary. The first condition remains necessary on an arbitrary base, even for a relative curve.

statement: [Proved: the boundary vanishing-cycle criterion] Let $f:X\to S$ be proper and smooth. Assume that every quasi-compact open of $S$ has finitely many irreducible components. Let $Y$ be a relative normal-crossings divisor, let $j:V=X\setminus Y \hookrightarrow X$, and put $h=fj$. Let $G$ be a locally constant constructible sheaf of finite abelian groups annihilated by an integer invertible on $S$. Put $K=Rj_*G$. For each geometric point $\bar s$ of $S$ and each geometric point $\bar t$ of $S_{(\bar s)}$, pull $K$ back to $X_{S_{(\bar s)}}$, and define \[ B_{\bar s\leftarrow\bar t}(G)= \operatorname{Cone}\bigl(K|_{X_{\bar s}}\longrightarrow i_{\bar s}^{*}Rj_{\bar t*}(K|_{X_{\bar t}})\bigr). \] Here $j_{\bar t}:X_{\bar t}\to X_{S_{(\bar s)}}$ and $i_{\bar s}:X_{\bar s}\to X_{S_{(\bar s)}}$ are the natural maps; the arrow is the specialization arrow. This boundary complex is supported on $Y_{\bar s}$. Then all $R^i h_*G$ are locally constant if and only if \begin{equation} R\Gamma\bigl(Y_{\bar s}, B_{\bar s\leftarrow\bar t}(G)|_{Y_{\bar s}}\bigr)=0 \quad\hbox{for every }(\bar s,\bar t). \end{equation} If the relative dimension is one, this is equivalent to the vanishing of the boundary complex at each individual point of $Y_{\bar s}$. Thus in relative dimension one the criterion is precisely local acyclicity of $Rj_*G$ along the boundary. In higher dimension the hypercohomological condition, rather than pointwise vanishing, is the necessary and sufficient condition.

statement: [Proved: a quasi-projective neighborhood of the entire boundary] Let $X$ be normal, connected and proper over an algebraically closed field. If the closed subset $Y\subsetneq X$ is contained in one quasi-projective open subscheme $N\subset X$, then $Q(X,Y)$ is topologically finitely generated. In particular, D.2(ii) holds when the omitted set consists of a single closed point, even on a nonprojective singular proper scheme. More generally, D.2(ii) holds for a possibly nonnormal proper scheme $Z$ whenever its entire codimension-two omitted subset has a quasi-projective open neighborhood in $Z$.

statement: [Proved under stated hypotheses: projective representations with bounded central obstruction] Let $Q$ be a profinite group and fix a prime $p$. statement: [Proved: unitary quotients with bounded natural centre] Let $Q$ satisfy the hypotheses of Proposition~\ref{D:bounded-scalar-projective-growth}, and fix $B$. statement: [Proved: quadratic growth at bounded geometric Brauer period] Fix an integer $B\ge1$. Let $G$ be one of the following groups, over an algebraically closed field $k$ of characteristic $p>0$: \begin{enumerate} \item $G=Q(S,T)$, where $S$ is a normal proper connected surface, $T\subsetneq S$ is closed, and $U=S-T$; \item $G=\pi_1(U)$, where $U=\operatorname{Spec}R-\{\mathfrak m\}$ for a complete excellent normal local $k$-algebra $(R,\mathfrak m)$ of dimension two with residue field $k$. \end{enumerate} For a continuous representation $\rho:G\to\operatorname{PGL}_r(\mathbf F_q)$, $q=p^f$, write $\operatorname{br}(\rho)\in H^2(U,\mathbf G_m)$ for the Brauer class of the induced algebraic projective-linear torsor. There is a constant $C_{G,B}$, independent of $r$ and $f$, such that \[ \#\left( \left\{\rho:G\to\operatorname{PGL}_r(\mathbf F_q): \operatorname{ord}(\operatorname{br}(\rho))\le B\right\} /\operatorname{PGL}_r(\mathbf F_q)\right) \le q^{C_{G,B}r^2}. \tag{D.BP.1} \] The order of the zero class is one. Its choice can depend on $B$; no uniform bound on $[G:H_B]$ as $B$ grows is asserted.

statement: [Proved: projective semilinear crowns over arbitrary permutation quotients] Let $R,\Gamma$ be as in Theorem~\ref{D:bounded-period-semilinear-hereditary-projective-growth}. Fix integers $B_*,b_0\ge1$ and $\kappa>0$. Let $L$ be a finite monolithic primitive group with nonabelian socle $N=S^t$, where $S$ is nonabelian simple, and put $P=L/N$. Fix a continuous epimorphism $\beta:\Gamma\to P$. Choose one simple socle factor, and let $\mathcal B\le\operatorname{Aut}(S)$ be the image of its stabilizer in $L$. Suppose \[ \begin{gathered} S\le\mathcal B_0\le\mathcal B,\qquad [\mathcal B:\mathcal B_0]\le b_0,\\ \iota:\mathcal B_0\lhook\joinrel\longrightarrow \operatorname{PGL}_r(\mathbb F_q) \rtimes\operatorname{Gal}(\mathbb F_q/\mathbb F_p), \qquad r^2\log q\le\kappa\log|S|, \end{gathered} \tag{D.BS.1} \] where $q$ is a power of $p$. Here $S$ is identified with its group of inner automorphisms. Normality of $\mathcal B_0$ in $\mathcal B$ is not required. Let $H\subset\Gamma$ be the inverse image of the point stabilizer of the chosen factor. Its prescribed outer map is $\eta:H\to\mathcal B/S$; put $H_0=\eta^{-1}(\mathcal B_0/S)$. Perfectness of $S$ makes the field projection of $\iota$ factor through $\mathcal B_0/S$. Consequently the map $\eta|_{H_0}$ specifies one field character $\chi_0:H_0\to\operatorname{Gal}(\mathbb F_q/\mathbb F_p)$. Write $K_0=\ker\chi_0$. statement: [Proved: exact two-level recovery of canonical module jets] In the setting of Lemma~\ref{D:canonical-pullback-uniform-jet-loss}, put $r=\operatorname{rank}_A M$ and define the proper parameter-ideal thickenings and their spaces of sections by \[ T_b=V(I_b\mathcal O_Y),\qquad V_b(M)=H^0(T_b,F|_{T_b}),\qquad W_b(M)=\operatorname{im}\bigl(V_{b+1}(M)\longrightarrow V_b(M)\bigr). \tag{D.CJ.6} \] The thickenings $T_b$ need not be Cartier or Cohen--Macaulay. statement: [Proved: smallness for arbitrary codimension-two boundaries] Let $Z$ be proper over an algebraically closed field $k$, and let $Y\subset Z$ be closed, of codimension at least two in every irreducible component. Let $U$ be a connected component of $Z\setminus Y$. For every connected finite \'etale cover $V\to U$ and every finite group $F$, the set $H^1(V,F)$ is finite. Equivalently, every open subgroup of $\pi_1(U)$ is \emph{small}: it has only finitely many open subgroups of each fixed index. In positive characteristic, its maximal pronilpotent quotient is also topologically finitely generated. Normality, projectivity, and finiteness of the omitted set are not required.

statement: [Proved: a projective model with no additional divisors] Let $S$ be a normal proper connected scheme over an algebraically closed field. Suppose that there is a normal projective integral scheme $P$ and an isomorphism of nonempty opens \[ \phi:S^\circ\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }P^\circ \] such that $P\setminus P^\circ$ has codimension at least two. More generally, D.2(ii) holds for a proper scheme whose normalized irreducible components each admit such a projective model, for every closed omitted set of codimension at least two in every component it meets.

statement: [Proved: coherent extension of a realized tame-band lifting gerbe] Let $(Y_H,C_H,U_H)$ be the regular one-curve model of a connected radially tame cover of the fixed local puncture. Let $q=p^f$, $n=q-1>1$, and fix a tame field character $\chi:\pi_1(U_H)\to\operatorname{Gal}(\mathbb F_q/\mathbb F_p)$. Write $a=|\operatorname{im}\chi|$, $\nu=f/a$, and let $V\to U_H$ be the corresponding connected cyclic cover. Suppose a class in $H^2(\pi_1(U_H),\mathcal M)$ is realized by a projective semilinear finite representation, and let $\mathscr G_U$ be its actual central lifting gerbe on $U_H$. statement: [Proved: the two uniform bounds needed for profinite generation] Let $G$ be a profinite group. For a finite quotient $F$ and a non-Frattini chief factor $A$ of $F$, let $\delta_F(A)$ be the number of non-Frattini chief factors in its $F$-equivalence class. Equivalently, this is the multiplicity in the crown quotient $(L_A)_{\delta_F(A)}$; here $L_A$ is the associated monolithic primitive group and \[ (L_A)_m=\{(l_1,\ldots,l_m)\in L_A^m: l_1A=\cdots=l_mA\}. \] Then $G$ is topologically finitely generated if and only if there is an integer $c\geq1$ such that both conditions hold: \begin{enumerate} \item for every prime $\ell$ and every finite irreducible continuous $\mathbb F_\ell[G]$-module $V$, \[ \dim_{\mathbb F_\ell}H^1(G,V) \leq c\dim_{\mathbb F_\ell}V; \] \item for every finite quotient $F$ and every nonabelian chief factor $A$ of $F$, \[ \delta_F(A)\leq |A|^c. \] \end{enumerate} These conditions imply that $G$ is generated by at most $c+2$ elements. No assertion that either uniform condition is already known geometrically in the residual D.1/D.2(ii) cases is made.

For every connected component \(V\) of \(U\), one has \[ \#\operatorname{Hom}_{\rm cont} \bigl(\pi_1(V),\operatorname{PGL}_r(\mathbb F_{p^f})\bigr) /\operatorname{PGL}_r(\mathbb F_{p^f}) \leq p^{C_R f r^2} \tag{D.AP.1} \] for one constant \(C_R\), every \(f\geq1\), and every \(r\geq1\). Normality and reducedness of \(R\) are not required. No Brauer-vanishing or bounded-period condition is imposed. Fix \(\epsilon>0\). For each isomorphism type \(S\) in a collection of nonabelian finite simple groups, choose one embedding \[ S\hookrightarrow\operatorname{PGL}_{r_S}(\mathbb F_{q_S}), \qquad q_S=p^{f_S},\qquad |S|\geq q_S^{\epsilon r_S^2}. \] The quotient of \(\pi_1(V)\) formed by all distinct simple quotient kernels of those types is topologically finitely generated. Its multiplicity for type \(S\) is at most \(|S|^{C_R/\epsilon}\). This is a simple-product conclusion, not full finite generation of \(\pi_1(V)\).

statement: [Proved: arbitrary boundaries on complete toric varieties] Let $S$ be a complete toric variety over an algebraically closed field of arbitrary characteristic. For every proper closed subset $T\subset S$, without a torus-invariance assumption on $T$, $Q(S,T)$ is topologically finitely generated. Thus D.1 holds for every complete toric compactification, including nonprojective ones. If $T$ has codimension at least two, the full group $\pi_1(S\setminus T)$ is finitely generated. The corresponding D.2(ii) conclusion also holds for a proper scheme whose normalized irreducible components are complete toric varieties.

statement: [Proved: compressed minors give a bounded rational chart cover] Let $X$ be a finite-type scheme over an algebraically closed field $k$, with $\dim X\leq b$, and let $A$ be an $M\times N$ matrix of regular functions on $X$. On its scheme-theoretic rank-$\rho$ locus, there are $b+1$ pairs of constant matrices \[ U_\alpha\in\operatorname{Mat}_{\rho\times M}(k),\qquad V_\alpha\in\operatorname{Mat}_{N\times\rho}(k) \] such that the opens $\det(U_\alpha A V_\alpha)\ne0$ cover. On each open, image, kernel, and cokernel have explicit rational bases, with no matrix-valued moduli variables. If the entries of $A$ are rational functions in $b$ ambient coordinates, of numerator and denominator degree at most $E$, these bases have degrees bounded by a polynomial in $M,N,E$ after clearing the existing denominators. Here the rank-$\rho$ locus means that all $(\rho+1)$-minors vanish and at least one $\rho$-minor is invertible. These are scheme conditions, including over nonreduced coefficient rings. For $\rho=0$ no compression is needed.

statement: [Proved: a stable annihilator uniform over finite punctured covers] Let $R$ be a complete excellent normal local surface domain. Let $I\subset R$ be an ideal such that, for every maximal Cohen--Macaulay $R$-module $M$ and $z\in I$, multiplication by $z$ on $M$ factors through a finite free $R$-module. Let $A$ be any finite normal, $R$-torsion-free $R$-algebra which is etale over the punctured spectrum. Thus every component dominates $\operatorname{Spec}R$, as for normalization in a finite separable generic algebra. Then \[ I^2\subset\mathfrak N(A/R), \] where $\mathfrak N$ is the Noether different, defined without a flatness assumption. Moreover, for every maximal Cohen--Macaulay $A$-module $M$ and every finite $A$-module $N$, \[ I^3\operatorname{Ext}^1_A(M,N)=0. \] Equivalently, multiplication by every element of $I^3$ on $M$ factors through a finite free $A$-module. The same $I$ works for every such cover algebra, irrespective of its degree.

statement: [Proved: a fixed canonical-defect annihilator and linear geometric genus] Let $(R,\mathfrak m,k)$ be a complete equicharacteristic normal local domain of dimension two, with algebraically closed coefficient field $k$. There is a fixed $\mathfrak m$-primary ideal $J\subset R$ such that the following holds. Let $A$ be a finite normal local domain over $R$, of generic degree $n$, with $R\subset A$, and suppose that \[ \operatorname{Spec}A\setminus\{\mathfrak m_A\} \longrightarrow \operatorname{Spec}R\setminus\{\mathfrak m\} \] is etale. For a projective regular resolution $\pi:Z\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ which is an isomorphism on the puncture, use the natural trace inclusion $\pi_*\omega_Z\subset\omega_A$. Then \[ J\omega_A\subset\pi_*\omega_Z, \qquad JH^1(Z,\mathcal O_Z)=0. \tag{D.CD.1} \] If $Q=(x,y)\subset J$ is one fixed parameter ideal of $R$, then \[ p_g(A):=\dim_kH^1(Z,\mathcal O_Z) =\operatorname{length}_A(\omega_A/\pi_*\omega_Z) \le n\operatorname{length}_R(R/Q). \tag{D.CD.2} \] The constants and the annihilator are independent of the cover. For a finite normal $R$-torsion-free algebra, the corresponding assertions hold componentwise, and the sum of the geometric genera has the same bound with $n$ the total generic degree. No separability restriction on $n$ is imposed; etaleness on the puncture supplies generic separability.

statement: [Proved: tame ramification above a Gorenstein cusp cycle] Let $(S,s)$ be a normal Gorenstein log canonical surface singularity over an algebraically closed field $k$. Suppose that its minimal resolution has a rational nodal cycle as exceptional fibre. For a quasi-\'etale cover of an algebraic surface, we obtain this germ by shrinking away the other finitely many branch points.

statement: [Proved: explicit tame Heisenberg covers of a fixed cone] Let $k$ be algebraically closed of characteristic $p>0$, let $(E,O)$ be an elliptic curve over $k$, and put $N=\mathcal O_E(-3O)$. statement: [Refuted: a constant generator bound at an Azumaya boundary] The following constant-generator assertion is false: on one fixed normal complete local surface, if $\mathcal A=\operatorname{End}(G)$ is Azumaya off the closed point and $H=\operatorname{Hom}(G,F)$ is locally free of rank one as a right $\mathcal A$-module there, then $H$ has a bounded number of $\mathcal A$-generators independent of the common rank of $F$ and $G$. It remains false when both $F$ and $G$ are reflexive and Frobenius-periodic. More precisely, put $k=\overline{\mathbb F}_3$ and fix \[ R=k[[x,y,z]]/(y^2z-x^3+xz^2). \tag{D.EO.1} \] For every $r=2^m$, $m\ge1$, there are rank-$r$ reflexive $R$-modules $G_r,F_r$ and an integer $f_r>0$ such that \[ (F_R^{f_r})^{[*]}G_r\simeq G_r, \qquad (F_R^{f_r})^{[*]}F_r\simeq F_r. \tag{D.EO.2} \] Writing $\mathcal A_r=\operatorname{End}_R(G_r)$ and $H_r=\operatorname{Hom}_R(G_r,F_r)$, we have \[ \mu_{\mathcal A_r}(H_r)=3r. \tag{D.EO.3} \] Here generators are right-module generators, with the action given by precomposition. statement: [Proved: canonical energy on a minimal surface resolution] Let $A$ be a normal Noetherian local $k$-algebra of dimension two, with residue field the algebraically closed field $k$, and suppose that $A$ admits a dualizing complex. Write $E_1,\ldots,E_v$ for the exceptional integral curves, and set \[ b_i=-E_i^2,\quad g_i=p_a(E_i),\quad N=(-(E_i\cdot E_j))_{i,j},\quad \kappa_i=K_Z\cdot E_i=2g_i-2+b_i. \] When the exceptional set is empty, all the following sums and energies are zero. Otherwise $N$ is positive definite with nonpositive off-diagonal entries, $\kappa_i\ge0$, and \[ \mathcal E:=\kappa^{\mathsf t}N^{-1}\kappa \le 8p_g+2\sum_i b_i. \tag{D.CE.1} \] Let $\mathcal B$ be any union of exceptional components with $\kappa_i=0$, and let $\mathcal C$ be its complement. Every member of $\mathcal B$ is a smooth rational $(-2)$-curve. statement: [Proved: the infinitesimal Picard kernel of a surface resolution] Let $A$ be a complete excellent normal local surface algebra over an algebraically closed coefficient and residue field $k$. Let $\pi:Y\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ be a regular resolution, an isomorphism on $U=\operatorname{Spec}A-\{\mathfrak m\}$, and let $E$ be its closed-fibre support. Then \[ H^0(D,\mathcal O_D(D))=0\quad(D>0\text{ supported on }E), \qquad H^1_E(Y,\mathcal O_Y)=0. \tag{D.IP.1} \] In particular $H^1(Y,\mathcal O_Y)\to H^1(U,\mathcal O_U)$ is injective. For every finite local Artinian $k$-algebra $T$ with residue field $k$, the map \[ \ker\bigl(\operatorname{Pic}(Y_T)\to\operatorname{Pic}(Y)\bigr) \longrightarrow \ker\bigl(\operatorname{Pic}(U_T)\to\operatorname{Pic}(U)\bigr) \tag{D.IP.2} \] is injective. Here the subscript $T$ means scalar extension over $k$. More precisely, let $L_T,L'_T$ be line bundles on $Y_T$ and let $\varphi_U:L_T|_{U_T}\simeq L'_T|_{U_T}$ be specified. Let $D_0$, an integral exceptional divisor of either sign, be the divisor of its closed-fibre meromorphic extension. Then $\varphi_U$ has a unique meromorphic extension on $Y_T$ whose divisor is exactly the constant Cartier divisor $(D_0)_T$. In particular its pole divisor, and the pole divisor of its inverse, acquire no extra contribution depending on the nilpotence order of $T$.

statement: [Refuted: a positive uniform lower bound for fierce excess] The assertion that Galois extensions with inseparable residue have a positive uniform lower bound for $(\delta-e+1)/e$ is false. We fix an algebraically closed field $k$ of characteristic $p>0$. For every power $q=p^r>1$, there is a finite Galois extension of two-variable rational function fields over $k$, with a divisorial valuation having ramification index $e=q(q-1)$, purely inseparable residue degree $q$, and different exponent \[ \delta=q^2+q-3. \] Consequently \[ \frac{\delta-e+1}{e}=\frac2q\longrightarrow0. \] In particular, inseparability of the residue extension does not give a positive lower bound for this normalized excess different, even at a fixed characteristic and with a Galois extension between function fields of smooth surfaces. This is a local ramification example; we do not assert that it extends to a quasi-\'etale cover of a prescribed contracted surface.

statement: [Proved: linear resolutions of an entire bounded-slope flag] Fix a smooth projective curve $C\subset\mathbf P^N_k$ and real numbers $a\le b$. There are integers $m,K$ with the following property. For every flag of vector subbundles \[ 0=V_0\subset V_1\subset\cdots\subset V_l=V, \qquad l\le r=\operatorname{rk}V, \] whose nonzero grades $G_j=V_j/V_{j-1}$ have all slopes in $[a,b]$, the flag is the sheafification of a filtered graded free complex over $P=k[x_0,\ldots,x_N]$. This complex has length at most $N+1$, its term in homological degree $i$ is a sum of at most $Kr$ copies of $P(-m-i)$, and its differential is a matrix of linear forms preserving coordinate flags in all terms. The associated graded complex resolves the corresponding truncated section modules of the $G_j$. For fixed ranks and multiplicities, these filtered complexes are parameterized by a closed affine scheme with $O(r^2)$ variables and $O(r^2)$ quadratic equations. Exactness, flatness and the subbundle conditions are imposed by passing to an open subset after identifying the total cohomology with a prescribed bundle on $C$. The number of multiplicity arrays needed is at most $\exp(Kr)$.

Let $Y\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ be projective, and let $C$ be an effective Cartier divisor supported on the entire closed fibre. Assume that every $jC$ is proper over $k$, and put $I=\mathcal O_Y(-C)$. For an affine finite-type $k$-scheme $S=\operatorname{Spec}B$, use the completed base change and its formal completion along $C$ as in Proposition~\ref{D:intrinsic-integral-unit-Hom-jets}. The formal assertions below also apply after every change to an arbitrary coefficient $B$-algebra. Fix integers $b\ge0$, $N\ge1$, and $f\ge1$ with \[ pN-b>N,\qquad L=N+b. \tag{D.FO.1} \] On $LC\times_k S$, suppose that rank-$r$ vector bundles $E_a$, indexed modulo $f$, and maps \[ \alpha_a:F^*E_a\longrightarrow E_{a+1},\qquad \beta_a:E_{a+1}\longrightarrow (F^*E_a)(bC) \tag{D.FO.2} \] are given. Here $F$ is absolute $p$-Frobenius of the finite thickening, including coefficient Frobenius. Require the two exact finite equalities \[ \alpha_a(bC)\,\beta_a=\iota_{E_{a+1}},\qquad \beta_a\,\alpha_a=\iota_{F^*E_a}, \tag{D.FO.3} \] where $\iota_V:V\to V(bC)$ is the canonical Cartier map. It is not asserted to be injective on this nonreduced finite thickening. The construction is independent, up to a unique integral unit isomorphism inducing these specified $N$-jet identifications, of its local choices. A morphism of the finite data intertwining (D.FO.2) gives a unique integral unit morphism inducing its prescribed $N$-jet. These maps retain identities and compositions. The construction and these comparisons commute with all coefficient changes in this precise formal, marked sense. For finite-type or finite local Artinian coefficient algebras, the constructed formal bundles and arrows algebraize over the corresponding proper Noetherian completed base. The assertion retains the prescribed data on $NC$; it does not claim to retain the entire input bundle on $LC$. It does not assert that the constructed lattices are canonical full pullbacks or that their punctured pushforwards are coefficient flat.

statement: [Refuted: bounding rational chains by local degree and different] Let \(k\) be algebraically closed of characteristic two. For \(m\geq1\), put \(N=2m+1\) and \[ X_m=\operatorname{Spec} k[x,y,z]/(z^2+xz+y^N),\qquad \pi_m:X_m\longrightarrow\mathbb A^2_{x,y}. \] These are finite flat, generically separable degree-two normal coverings, etale away from the fixed divisor \(x=0\). statement: [Proved: linearization after Frobenius along a formal retraction] Let $C$ be a smooth proper connected curve of genus $g$ in a smooth surface $Y$ over an algebraically closed field $k$ of characteristic $p>0$. Write $N=N_{C/Y}$ and $\deg N=-d<0$. Suppose the entire formal completion $\mathfrak Y=\widehat Y_C$ admits a $k$-morphism \[ r:\mathfrak Y\longrightarrow C, \qquad r|_C=\operatorname{id}_C. \] Choose a power $q=p^a$ with $qd>2g-2$, and let $h:C'=C^{(-a)}\to C$ be the $k$-linear relative Frobenius. statement: [Proved: generated Morita-unit classes are open] Keep the fixed orders and Morita context above. Let an actual family of such ordinary order-module unit bundles be given over a finite-type coefficient base, on the complete proper surface family. Suppose every $E_a(-Z)$ is generated and every determinant line $\det E_a$ is fixed formally. It suffices to retain on $Z$ a specified generating quotient and a fixed determinant line: the weak-cycle lifting of Lemma~\ref{D:weak-cycle-generated-determinant-lifting} gives exactly these conditions. Then the locus of every punctured scalar-weight-one unit isomorphism class is open and closed. For a fixed comparison class, the unit-Isom functor is represented by an affine scheme of finite presentation and is etale over the parameter scheme on its image. Its pole bound may depend on the class, rank and determinant chart; its coordinates are not charged to the quantitative object atlas.

statement: [Proved: meromorphic unit-Isom openness for generated fixed-determinant families] Let $A$ be a complete excellent normal local surface with algebraically closed coefficient and residue field $k$ of characteristic $p>0$. Let $\pi:Y\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ be a projective regular resolution, an isomorphism over the puncture $U$. Let $C,Z$ be effective Cartier cycles with full exceptional support and $Z\le\alpha C$ for a fixed integer $\alpha$. Assume that $Z$ satisfies (D.GD.1). Let $S=\operatorname{Spec}B$ be of finite type over $k$. On the proper base change over the completion of $A\otimes_k B$, suppose there is an actual length-$f$ cycle of rank-$r$ bundles $F_a$ with meromorphic Frobenius unit arrows, regular and invertible on $U_S$, whose arrows and inverses have a fixed finite pole bound along $C$. For every phase assume that \[ F_a(-Z)|_{Z_S}\text{ has a specified generating quotient}, \qquad \det(F_a(-Z))|_{Z_S}\simeq L_a|_{Z_S}, \tag{D.GD.4} \] where each $L_a$ is one fixed line bundle on $Y$. No relative maximal-Cohen--Macaulay pushforward, coflatness, or canonical full-pullback property of $F_a$ is assumed. For each fixed punctured unit class represented by $S(k)$, there is a finite integer $d$, allowed to depend on that fixed comparison object, such that its punctured unit-Isom functor over all finite local Artinian coefficient points is exactly the functor of unit isomorphisms with both meromorphic directions bounded by $dC$. The latter bounded functor is represented over $S$ by an affine scheme of finite presentation and is etale. Its image is precisely the class in question and is open and closed. Consequently \[ \#\{\text{punctured unit classes represented by }S(k)\} \le\#\operatorname{Irr}(S). \tag{D.GD.5} \] The pole bound here need not be independent of rank, and no coordinate bound for the comparison scheme is asserted. Neither bound is needed for (D.GD.5).

Let $C,Z$ be effective Cartier cycles with full exceptional support and $Z\le\alpha C$ for a fixed integer $\alpha$. Assume that $Z$ satisfies (D.GD.1). Let $S=\operatorname{Spec}B$ be of finite type over $k$. On the proper base change over the completion of $A\otimes_k B$, suppose there is an actual length-$f$ cycle of rank-$r$ bundles $F_a$ with meromorphic Frobenius unit arrows, regular and invertible on $U_S$, whose arrows and inverses have a fixed finite pole bound along $C$. For every phase assume that \[ F_a(-Z)|_{Z_S}\text{ has a specified generating quotient}, \qquad \det(F_a(-Z))|_{Z_S}\simeq L_a|_{Z_S}, \tag{D.GD.4} \] where each $L_a$ is one fixed line bundle on $Y$. No relative maximal-Cohen--Macaulay pushforward, coflatness, or canonical full-pullback property of $F_a$ is assumed. For each fixed punctured unit class represented by $S(k)$, there is a finite integer $d$, allowed to depend on that fixed comparison object, such that its punctured unit-Isom functor over all finite local Artinian coefficient points is exactly the functor of unit isomorphisms with both meromorphic directions bounded by $dC$. The latter bounded functor is represented over $S$ by an affine scheme of finite presentation and is etale. Its image is precisely the class in question and is open and closed. Consequently \[ \#\{\text{punctured unit classes represented by }S(k)\} \le\#\operatorname{Irr}(S). \tag{D.GD.5} \] The pole bound here need not be independent of rank, and no coordinate bound for the comparison scheme is asserted. Neither bound is needed for (D.GD.5).

statement: [Proved: generation from the geometric generic fibre] Let $k$ be algebraically closed, let $X$ be a normal connected proper $k$-scheme, and let $f:X\to B$ be a dominant morphism to a smooth connected proper curve. Suppose the geometric generic fibre $X_{\overline\eta}$ is integral. Let $Y\subsetneq X$ be closed and put $U=X\setminus Y$. Then the following assertions hold. \begin{enumerate} \item If $\pi_1(U_{\overline\eta})$ is topologically finitely generated and $U$ meets every fibre of $f$, then $\pi_1(U)$ is topologically finitely generated. \item If $X_{\overline\eta}$ is normal and $Q(X_{\overline\eta},Y_{\overline\eta})$ is topologically finitely generated, then $Q(X,Y)$ is topologically finitely generated. In this assertion whole fibres may be contained in $Y$. \end{enumerate} No properness assumption is imposed on $U\to B$, and the generic fibre need not be smooth.

statement: [Proved: surface reduction with controlled exceptional centres] Let $k$ be algebraically closed, let $S$ be a normal proper integral $k$-scheme of dimension $d\ge2$, and let $T\subsetneq S$ be closed. Write $U=S\setminus T$. Suppose that there is a proper birational morphism \[ q:Y\longrightarrow S \] with $Y$ normal and projective over $k$, satisfying this condition: every prime divisor $E\subset Y$ whose image has codimension at least two in $S$ and is contained in $T$ has zero-dimensional image. Then there are an algebraically closed extension $K/k$ of finite transcendence degree, a normal proper integral surface $X/K$, and a finite morphism $g:X\to S_K$ onto its image, such that, with $T_X=g^{-1}(T_K)$, the induced map on the original-boundary tame quotients is surjective: \[ Q(X,T_X)\twoheadrightarrow Q(S,T). \tag{D.CB.1} \] Here tameness is required only at the original codimension-one boundary points in each of the indicated compactifications. If $T$ has codimension at least two in $S$, then $T_X$ is finite and there is a surjection of full fundamental groups \[ \pi_1(X\setminus T_X)\twoheadrightarrow\pi_1(U). \tag{D.CB.2} \] Thus, in characteristic $p>0$, all the already proved surface bounds for all-field $H^1$, defining-characteristic quadratic representation counts, and bounded-scalar projective representation counts hold for $Q(S,T)$ under the displayed geometric condition. Its maximal prosolvable quotient and the previously specified bounded-scalar simple-product quotients are finitely generated. For (D.CB.2) these conclusions concern the full group $\pi_1(U)$. We assert neither an $H^2$ transfer nor full finite generation of these groups.

statement: [Proved: a generic surface detects every original cover] Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field of arbitrary characteristic, let $S$ be a normal proper integral $k$-scheme of dimension $d\ge2$, and let $T\subset S$ be a finite closed subset. Put $U=S\setminus T$. There exist an algebraically closed extension $K/k$ of finite transcendence degree, a normal proper integral surface $X/K$, and a finite morphism $g:X\to S_K$ onto a closed integral surface, such that $T_X=g^{-1}(T_K)$ is finite and the composite morphism \[ X\setminus T_X\longrightarrow U_K\longrightarrow U \] induces a continuous surjection \[ \pi_1(X\setminus T_X)\twoheadrightarrow\pi_1(U). \tag{D.GS.1} \] The extension and surface are fixed independently of the finite cover of $U$. The target in (D.GS.1) is the fundamental group of the original $k$-scheme $U$; no surjectivity onto $\pi_1(U_K)$ is asserted. Consequently, full finite generation for normal proper surfaces with finite punctures over algebraically closed fields would imply full finite generation for normal proper schemes of every dimension with finite punctures.

statement: [Proved: global hereditary growth with bounded local periods] Let \(S\) be a fixed normal proper connected surface over an algebraically closed field \(k\) of characteristic \(p>0\), let \(T\subset S\) be finite, and put \(\Gamma=\pi_1(U)\), \(U=S-T\). Choose the fixed finite set \(F\supset T\), complete local sources \(R_s\), and detecting curve of Lemma~\ref{D:finite-puncture-detecting-curve-local-types}. Fix \(B_*\ge1\). For an open \(H\subset\Gamma\) of index \(t\), let \(U_H\to U\) be its connected finite etale cover. For each \(s\in F\), write the pullback to the fixed puncture \(U_{R_s}\) as its connected components: \[ U_H\times_U U_{R_s}=\coprod_i U_{s,i}, \qquad n_{s,i}=\deg(U_{s,i}/U_{R_s}),\qquad \sum_i n_{s,i}=t. \tag{D.GH.13} \] Each \(U_{s,i}\) is the puncture of its complete normal local normalization of \(R_s\). There is a constant \(A_{S,T,B_*}\) such that the homomorphisms \(\rho:H\to\operatorname{PGL}_r(\mathbb F_q)\), \(q=p^f\), for which every restriction to \(\pi_1(U_{s,i})\) has geometric Brauer period at most \(B_*\), have at most \[ q^{A_{S,T,B_*}t r^2} \tag{D.GH.14} \] projective conjugacy classes. It suffices to require the period condition at \(s\in T\); the other restrictions are trivial. In particular the conclusion covers every such representation if \(\gcd(r,q-1)\le B_*\). A bound \(B_*\) on the global geometric Brauer period on \(U_H\) is another sufficient condition. The detecting curve is chosen once for \((S,T)\). No constant belonging to a new unspecified curve or to a new surface resolution is used.

statement: [Proved: global hereditary semilinear growth with bounded local periods] Let \(S,T,U,\Gamma,F,R_s\) be the fixed data of Theorem~\ref{D:global-finite-puncture-hereditary-bounded-local-period}, and fix \(B_*\ge1\). It is automatic if \(\gcd(r,q-1)\le B_*\), or if the ordinary geometric Brauer period on the global field-kernel cover of \(U_H\) is at most \(B_*\). There is no tameness or bounded-order assumption on the field character or on the original cover. No ordinary geometric Brauer class is assigned on \(U_H\) to the nonconstant scalar band.

statement: [Proved: Bounded minimal extensions of periodic reflexive sheaves] Let $S$ be a normal proper surface over an algebraically closed field of characteristic $p>0$. Fix a projective resolution $\pi:Y\to S$, with smooth projective $Y$, an ample divisor $H$, and an effective exceptional divisor $Z$ with $Z\cdot E_i<0$ on every exceptional component. For reflexive sheaves $E$ of rank $r$ satisfying $F_S^{[p^f]*}E\simeq E$ for some $f\ge1$, their minimal extensions $F$ to $Y$ have the following bounds, with constants independent of $r$ and $f$: \begin{enumerate} \item their restrictions to the exceptional curves have fixed upper and lower slope windows; \item $|\chi(Y,F)|\le Cr$, and $c_1(F)$ is numerically an exceptional linear combination whose coefficients have absolute values at most $Cr$; \item $\mu_{\max,H}(F)$ and $\mu_{\max,H}(F^\vee)$ are bounded by a fixed constant, and the analogous bounds hold after restriction to a fixed sufficiently ample smooth curve; \item for each fixed $r$, these extensions form a bounded family. \end{enumerate} Ordinary isomorphism of their underlying reflexive sheaves, and the one-step relation $F_S^{[*]}E\simeq E'$, are constructible relations on one finite-type parameter space for each fixed rank.

statement: [Proved: all defining-characteristic Lie simple products in this scope] Let $\Gamma$ be any group covered by (D.GFP.1) or (D.GFP.3). statement: [Proved: Cartier two-level recovery on arbitrary complete covers] Let $R$ be a fixed complete excellent normal local surface over an algebraically closed coefficient and residue field $k$ of characteristic $p>0$. Fix the ideal $J$ and a separating parameter normalization $S=k[[x,y]]\subset R$, with $x,y\in J$, as in Lemma~\ref{D:canonical-pullback-uniform-jet-loss}. Put $Q=(x,y)R$. There is one fixed regular projective modification $Y_0\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ and an effective exceptional Cartier cycle $C_0$ of full support such that \[ Q\mathcal O_{Y_0}=\mathcal O_{Y_0}(-C_0). \tag{D.HC.1} \] For every finite normal cover domain $A/R$ of degree $t$, etale on the puncture, choose a regular projective resolution $\pi:Y\to \operatorname{Spec}A$ dominating the normalization above $Y_0$. Write $f:Y\to Y_0$ and $C=f^*C_0$. Then, for every $b\ge1$, \[ (x^b,y^b)\mathcal O_Y=\mathcal O_Y(-bC),\qquad C^2=tC_0^2. \tag{D.HC.2} \] The cycle $C$ is anti-nef and has full exceptional support. For a reflexive $A$-module $M$ of rank $r$, put $F=(\pi^*M)^{\vee\vee}$ and \[ V_b=H^0(bC,F|_{bC}),\quad W_b=\operatorname{im}(V_{b+1}\longrightarrow V_b),\quad K_b=H^0(Y,F(-bC)). \] With the same constant $c$ as in the cited saturation lemma, \[ W_b=M/K_b,\qquad W_b/(x^\ell,y^\ell)W_b\simeq M/(x^\ell,y^\ell)M \quad(b\ge2\ell-1+2c). \tag{D.HC.3} \] For each fixed $b$, both $h^0(bC,F|_{bC})$ and $h^1(bC,F|_{bC})$ are $O_b(tr)$, uniformly over all such complete cover rings. In particular \[ -C^2+|K_Y\cdot C|+h^0(\mathcal O_{bC})+ h^1(\mathcal O_{bC})=O_b(t). \tag{D.HC.4} \] The jet identifications are functorial for actual module maps. Consider finite normal quasi-etale cover domains $A/R$ of rank $n$ in the energy family of Corollary~\ref{D:punctured-cover-linear-energy}. Here the energy hypothesis means that the stated bounds for $p_g$, the canonical energy and the total exceptional self-intersection hold with constants depending only on the fixed base. In particular one may complete the algebraic local cover family in that corollary: excellence preserves regularity of the base-changed resolution, and proper flat base change preserves the exceptional curves, intersection numbers and coherent-cohomology lengths. No energy assertion for arbitrary nonalgebraizable complete covers is added here. Write $Y$ for the minimal regular resolution of $A$, and choose $Z$ as in Theorem~\ref{D:reflexive-pullback-uniform-generation} and Corollary~\ref{D:punctured-cover-antinef-cycle}. The choice depends on $A$, but not on a module or its rank. Fix $t\ge1$ and put $D=tZ$. Let $(M_a)_{a\in\mathbb Z/f\mathbb Z}$ be a cyclic system of rank-$r$ reflexive $A$-modules with $F_A^{[*]}M_a\simeq M_{a+1}$. Put \[ F_a=(\pi^*M_a)^{\vee\vee},\qquad V_a=F_a(-Z)|_D. \] There is a constant $c_t$, independent of $n,r,f$ and this system, such that \[ 0\le c_1(F_a)\cdot Z\le c_tnr, \qquad h^0(D,\det V_a)\le c_tnr. \tag{D.UG.9} \] Every $V_a$ is globally generated. For each fixed line bundle $L=\det V_a$ on $D$, all globally generated rank-$r$ bundles on $D$ with determinant isomorphic to $L$ occur as the universal quotients over an open subset of \[ H^0(D,L)^{\oplus(r+1)}. \tag{D.UG.10} \] In particular the relevant fixed-determinant object chart has at most $c_tnr(r+1)=O_t(nr^2)$ scalar coordinates. Its universal quotient is an actual vector bundle, also over nonreduced parameter schemes. This is a statement about the objects on one finite exceptional cycle. It asserts neither that every such bundle is the restriction of a desired reflexive unit object, nor that a unit object is determined by this restriction.

statement: [Proved: degree-linear determinant lists for ordinary unit cycles] Fix a complete normal local surface $(R,\mathfrak m,k)$ over an algebraically closed coefficient field $k$ of characteristic $p>0$. For every finite normal local cover $A/R$ of degree $t$, etale on the puncture, one can choose a projective regular resolution $\pi:Y\to\operatorname{Spec}A$, and full-support effective anti-nef Cartier cycles $C\le W$, with the following properties. The choices depend on $A$ and fixed base data, but not on a representation. The number $v$ of exceptional prime curves is $O(t)$. The actual Cartier powers and all bounds of Proposition~\ref{D:hereditary-Cartier-generation-budget} hold on this same model. Write $U_A=\operatorname{Spec}A\setminus\{\mathfrak m_A\}$, let $q=p^f$, and let $\mathcal E$ be the vector bundle with ordinary $q$-unit structure associated to any continuous $\mathbb F_q$ representation of $\pi_1(U_A)$ of rank $r\ge1$. For $0\le a<f$, let \[ M_a=j_*(F_{U_A}^{a*}\mathcal E),\qquad F_a=(\pi^*M_a)^{\vee\vee},\qquad V_{a,b}=F_a(-W)|_{bC},\quad L_{a,b}=\det V_{a,b}, \tag{D.UD.1} \] where $b\ge1$ is fixed and $j:U_A\hookrightarrow\operatorname{Spec}A$. Here $F_{U_A}$ denotes the absolute $p$-Frobenius, and $F_{U_A}^{a*}$ is its $a$-fold pullback. These are the canonical reflexive extensions and their full pullback bundles. The bundles $V_{a,b}$ and lines $L_{a,b}$ are globally generated, and \[ h^0(\mathcal O_{bC})+h^1(\mathcal O_{bC})=O_b(t),\qquad \deg L_{a,b}+h^0(L_{a,b})=O_b(tr). \tag{D.UD.2} \] There are constants $c_0,c_1$, depending only on the fixed base data, such that the number of ordered tuples of isomorphism classes of the lines $(L_{a,b})_{0\le a<f}$ arising in this way is at most \[ q^{c_0t}\exp\!\bigl(c_1ft\log(r+1)\bigr) \le p^{c_2ftr^2}. \tag{D.UD.3} \] The same bound covers any fixed finite list of thicknesses $b$: once the determinant lines on $Y$ are chosen, their restrictions at all those levels are determined. This statement enumerates the determinants of geometric ordinary unit objects. It does not assert that an arbitrary infinitesimal deformation of a line or bundle has a constant determinant.

statement: [Proved: whole-Cartier-cycle object and Hom budgets] Use the model and cycles of Lemma~\ref{D:hereditary-ordinary-unit-determinants}, and fix $b\ge1$. Put $D=bC$. For any fixed determinant lines $L_i$ occurring in that lemma, with respective ranks $r_i\le r$, the following is an actual finite-cycle presentation over every coefficient $k$-algebra $T$. There is an open subset of the affine space \[ H^0(D,L_i)^{r_i+1} \tag{D.UD.11} \] whose points specify exact locally split sequences \[ 0\longrightarrow (L_i^{-1})_T \xrightarrow{s_i}\mathcal O_{D_T}^{r_i+1} \longrightarrow V_i\longrightarrow0, \tag{D.UD.12} \] with $V_i$ locally free of rank $r_i$ and determinant $(L_i)_T$. Every globally generated geometric bundle of rank $r_i$ and determinant $L_i$ occurs. The object coordinates have number $O_b(tr_i^2)$. For each pair of these universal quotient bundles, their actual derived Hom is represented by a fixed graded finite-dimensional $k$-space tensored with $T$, with a differential polynomial of degree at most two in the object coordinates. Its total dimension is $O_b(tr_ir_j)$ and its degrees lie in $[-1,2]$. It is functorial in all coefficient rings, without any assumption that its cohomology is flat. In particular \[ h^0(D,\mathcal Hom(V_i,V_j))+ h^1(D,\mathcal Hom(V_i,V_j))=O_b(tr_ir_j) \tag{D.UD.13} \] at every geometric point. Actual arrows, equality of arrows, and inverse relations have finite polynomial witnesses. For a fixed pattern with $O(f)$ objects, arrows and bounded-length relations, the combined number of coordinates and scalar equations is $O_b(ftr^2)$, and their degrees are bounded independently of $t,r,f$. The chosen determinant lines and all linear splittings used below are fixed background data. For the geometric canonical bundles in (D.UD.1), twisting both arguments by $-W$ cancels in Hom. Thus (D.UD.13) is also the actual $H^0+H^1$ bound for $\mathcal Hom(F_a,F_{a'})|_{bC}$, not a bound inferred from a sandwich of lattices on the surface.

statement: [Proved: conditional realization on the uniform generation cycle] Fix the complete normal local surface $R$ and the data of Proposition~\ref{D:hereditary-Cartier-generation-budget}. For every finite normal punctured cover $A/R$ of degree $t$, choose its model and cycles $C\le W$ as in that proposition and Proposition~\ref{D:all-complete-cover-geometric-budgets}. They may be chosen independently of every representation. Then $W$ satisfies (D.WR.1) and the weak generic-generation condition. Consequently any finite local Artinian bundle on $(dW)_T$, $d\ge2$, satisfying the three retained hypotheses on $(2W)_T$, realizes an actual relative maximal Cohen--Macaulay module with all the conclusions of Proposition~\ref{D:weak-cycle-Artinian-full-realization}. For each fixed module-jet level $\ell$, choose the fixed integer $b\ge2\ell-1+2c$ from the established scalar clearing bound, and take $d\ge\max\{2,b+1\}$. The retained $(dW)_T$ bundle then determines its module jet as follows. Put $Q_j(T)=H^0(jC_T,\mathcal F_T|_{jC_T})$ and $B_b(T)=\operatorname{im}[Q_{b+1}(T)\to Q_b(T)]$. The exact formula is \[ B_b(T)/(x^\ell,y^\ell)B_b(T) \simeq M_T/(x^\ell,y^\ell)M_T. \tag{D.WR.7} \] Here $b,c,d$ depend only on the fixed base and $\ell$, not on $t$, the module rank, or the Artinian coefficient algebra. The recovered quotient commutes with the stated coefficient changes; the raw cohomology spaces and images need not do so.

statement: [Proved: hereditary counting through imprimitive wreath towers] Let $\Lambda$ be the fundamental group of the punctured spectrum of a fixed complete excellent normal local surface over an algebraically closed field of characteristic $p>0$. For every integer $m\ge2$, choose a finite collection \[ P_{m,j}\le S_m,\qquad P_{m,j}\hookrightarrow \operatorname{GL}_{r_{m,j}}(\mathbb F_{q_{m,j}}), \quad j\in\mathcal J_m, \tag{D.WO.1} \] where $q_{m,j}$ is a power of $p$ and the embeddings are part of the fixed models. Suppose that one constant $B$ satisfies \[ \log\max\{1,|\mathcal J_m|\}\le Bm\log(m+1),\qquad r_{m,j}^2\log q_{m,j}\le Bm\log(m+1). \tag{D.WO.2} \] Empty model collections are allowed. A tower certificate of degree $N\ge2$ consists of an ordered factorization $N=m_1\cdots m_h$, $m_i\ge2$, together with, at each level, either a chosen model $P_i=P_{m_i,j_i}$ or the unrestricted group $P_i=S_{m_i}$. Call these levels modelled and unrestricted respectively. Put \[ T_i=\prod_{j>i}m_j,\qquad W_h=P_h,\quad W_i=P_i\wr W_{i+1}\quad(i<h),\qquad \mathcal E=\sum_{i\text{ unrestricted}}T_i m_i^2. \tag{D.WO.3} \] The wreath products use their standard imprimitive actions, so $W_1\le S_N$. A transitive $\Lambda$-set admits this certificate if its action is permutation-conjugate into $W_1$. Define $e_{\mathcal J}(X)$ to be the minimum of $\mathcal E$ over its certificates. A singleton has cost zero. Every transitive $N$-set has a certificate and \[ 0\le e_{\mathcal J}(X)\le N^2, \tag{D.WO.4} \] by using the one-level unrestricted model $S_N$. There is a constant $C$, depending only on $\Lambda$ and $B$, such that, for all $N\ge2$ and integers $M\ge0$, \[ \#\{\text{transitive $N$-element $\Lambda$-sets up to isomorphism}:e_{\mathcal J}(X)\le M\} \le\exp\bigl(C(N\log(N+1)+M)\bigr). \tag{D.WO.5} \] In particular, arbitrary-height iterated modelled wreath actions have a factorial-order count without an orbit-size restriction. The estimate concerns actual permutation sets, not only their associated linear representations.

statement: [Proved: the horizontal residue order is its single node order] In the preceding setting, each irreducible horizontal component $D'_a$ is the spectrum of a complete discrete valuation ring isomorphic to $k[[z_a]]$. It meets $E$ at one transverse point $x_a$. For $n$ prime to $p$, the secondary-residue map at that point is, after fixing the usual Tate-twist identification, an isomorphism \[ H^1(k(D'_a),\mathbf Z/n)\xrightarrow{\ \partial_{x_a}\ } \mathbf Z/n. \tag{D.LDH.4} \] In particular every horizontal residue character has the same order as its secondary residue at $x_a$.

statement: [Proved: an integral anti-nef cycle with controlled energy] Let $N$ be a symmetric positive definite integral matrix with diagonal $b_i>0$ and nonpositive off-diagonal entries. Let $\kappa$ be an entrywise nonnegative integral vector. Assume that \[ b_i=2\quad\text{if }\kappa_i=0, \qquad b_i\le3\kappa_i\quad\text{if }\kappa_i>0, \tag{D.IC.1} \] and that each connected component of the off-diagonal incidence graph contains a vertex with $\kappa_i>0$. Put $B=\sum_i b_i$ and $\mathcal E=\kappa^{\mathsf t}N^{-1}\kappa$. For every integer $c\ge2$ there is an entrywise positive integral vector $z$ such that \[ \begin{split} &Nz\ge0,\qquad (Nz)_i\ge(c-3/2)\kappa_i\quad(\kappa_i>0),\\ &\bigl|(Nz-c\kappa)_i\bigr|\le b_i/2,\qquad z^{\mathsf t}Nz\le2c^2\mathcal E+B. \end{split} \tag{D.IC.2} \] In particular \[ \sum_i(Nz)_i\le c\sum_i\kappa_i+B/2. \tag{D.IC.3} \] The vector is integral from the outset; no common denominator of $N^{-1}$ is used.

statement: [Proved: fixed-loss lifting of intrinsic Hom jets] Let $\pi:Y\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ be a projective regular resolution of a complete normal local surface over an algebraically closed coefficient field $k$. Let $C$ be a nonzero effective exceptional Cartier divisor whose support is the entire closed fibre, and suppose two elements $x,y$ generate its invertible ideal: \[ (x,y)\mathcal O_Y=\mathcal O_Y(-C). \tag{D.HJ.1} \] Let $J$ be an ideal of the fixed base ring acting on $A$, with $x,y\in J$ and $JH^1(Y,\mathcal O_Y)=0$. Let $T$ be a finite-dimensional local Artinian $k$-algebra with residue field $k$, and let $F_T,G_T$ be vector bundles on $Y_T$. Assume that, for fixed positive integers $a,b$, each of $x^a\operatorname{Id}_{F_T}$ and $y^a\operatorname{Id}_{F_T}$ factors through a finite free $\mathcal O_{Y_T}$-module, and each of $x^b\operatorname{Id}_{G_T}$ and $y^b\operatorname{Id}_{G_T}$ does also. Put $\ell=a+b+1$ and $H_T=\mathcal Hom(F_T,G_T)$. For every integer $d$ and every $k\ge\max\{0,d\}$, the inclusion induces the zero map \[ H^1\bigl(Y_T,H_T((d-k-\ell)C)\bigr) \longrightarrow H^1\bigl(Y_T,H_T((d-k)C)\bigr). \tag{D.HJ.2} \] Consequently, for $k\ge\max\{1,d\}$, \[ \begin{split} &\operatorname{im}\bigl[ H^0((k+\ell)C_T,H_T(dC)|_{(k+\ell)C_T}) \longrightarrow H^0(kC_T,H_T(dC)|_{kC_T})\bigr]\\ &\hspace{12mm}= \operatorname{im}\bigl[ H^0(Y_T,H_T(dC)) \longrightarrow H^0(kC_T,H_T(dC)|_{kC_T})\bigr]. \end{split} \tag{D.HJ.3} \] Thus a map on the higher cycle has a global map with precisely its prescribed lower-cycle restriction. The assertion holds after every Artinian coefficient change, using the pulled-back factorizations. It does not assert that either raw image commutes with coefficient change. When $a=b=1$ and $d=0$, the loss is three. If a given higher-cycle map is an isomorphism, its global lift matching the lower cycle is an isomorphism on $Y_T$.

statement: [Proved: intrinsic finite jets of integral unit maps] Let $A$ be a complete Noetherian local $k$-algebra, with $k$ algebraically closed of characteristic $p>0$. Let $Y$ be projective over $A$, and let $C$ be an effective Cartier divisor whose support is the entire closed fibre. Assume that every $jC$ is a proper $k$-scheme. Put $I=\mathcal O_Y(-C)$. For an affine finite-type $k$-scheme $S=\operatorname{Spec}B$, use the completion of $A\otimes_k B$ along $\mathfrak m_A$, and the corresponding proper base change of $Y$. Suppose that two actual length-$f$ cycles of vector bundles $F_a,G_a$, with indices modulo $f$, are given on this completed base change. Their arrows are meromorphic isomorphisms \[ \phi_a:F_Y^*F_a\dashrightarrow F_{a+1},\qquad \psi_a:F_Y^*G_a\dashrightarrow G_{a+1}, \tag{D.IU.1} \] regular away from $C$, where $F_Y$ is absolute $p$-Frobenius, including coefficient Frobenius. Assume a fixed bound $bC$ for every arrow and its inverse. Set $H_a=\mathcal Hom(F_a,G_a)$ and choose $c\ge0$ such that \[ T_a(\eta)=\psi_a\,F_Y^*(\eta)\,\phi_a^{-1} \quad\hbox{maps }H_a\hbox{ into }H_{a+1}(cC). \tag{D.IU.2} \] Take $c$ to work also for the reverse comparisons and the two endomorphism cycles; $c=2b$ always does. Choose an integer $N\ge1$ with \[ pN-c>N. \tag{D.IU.3} \] Then the functor of integral formal unit morphisms between these cycles is represented by an affine scheme of finite presentation over $S$, using only their restrictions to a fixed finite thickening. More precisely, an integral unit morphism is uniquely determined by the tuple $\eta_a\in H^0(NC,H_a|_{NC})$. The exact finite equations are \[ \iota_N(\eta_{a+1})=T_{a,N}(\eta_a) \quad\hbox{in }H^0((N+c)C,H_{a+1}(cC)|_{(N+c)C}). \tag{D.IU.4} \] Here $\iota_N$ is induced by $H_{a+1}\hookrightarrow H_{a+1}(cC)$, and $T_{a,N}$ is obtained by Frobenius pullback to $pNC$, composition with the actual pole maps, and restriction to $(N+c)C$. The functor of integral formal unit isomorphisms is also affine of finite presentation: retain a reverse tuple with the reverse unit equations and require the two products to be the identity on $NC$. These descriptions are functorial over every coefficient $B$-algebra, in the category of formal bundles. Over finite-type coefficient algebras and finite local Artinian coefficient algebras, the formal maps algebraize on the proper Noetherian completed bases by Grothendieck existence. No arbitrary-ring algebraization or global lifting of an arbitrarily prescribed ordinary Hom jet is asserted.

statement: [Proved: uncharged orbits with intrinsically small defining-characteristic images] In either Theorem~\ref{D:alternating-compressed-local-orbits} or Theorem~\ref{D:original-boundary-matrix-alternating-count}, fix a sequence of positive integers $D_N$ with $D_N^4\le B N\log(N+1)$. Enlarge the admissible whole local orbits by allowing every degree-$N$ orbit whose finite image admits a faithful $\mathbb F_p$ representation of dimension at most $D_N$. Then all conclusions of the respective theorem remain valid, with the square-sum condition imposed only on the remaining orbits. In particular, for any fixed constants $c>0$ and $b\ge0$, all local orbit images of faithful $\mathbb F_p$ dimension at most $c(1+\log(N+1))^b$ may be left uncharged, regardless of the particular transitive action of that image. This is an intrinsic condition on the whole local permutation image, rather than a requirement that its action be one prescribed affine or flag action.

statement: [Proved: subgroup and point-stabilizer enumeration for small linear images] Fix a prime $p$ and a profinite group $\Lambda$ for which \[ |\operatorname{Hom}_{\rm cont} (\Lambda,\operatorname{GL}_D(\mathbb F_p))| \le p^{aD^2}\qquad(D\ge1) \tag{D.IM.1} \] with one constant $a$. For integers $N\ge2$ and $D\ge1$, let $\mathcal T_{N,D}(\Lambda)$ be the isomorphism classes of transitive $N$-element continuous $\Lambda$-sets whose finite permutation image admits a faithful representation over $\mathbb F_p$ of dimension at most $D$. Then \[ \log\max\{1,|\mathcal T_{N,D}(\Lambda)|\} \le \frac{2(\log p)^2}{\log2}D^4 +(a+2)(\log p)D^2. \tag{D.IM.2} \] No linear representation or identification of the permutation image is required as part of the given set. More explicitly, there is a fixed collection of faithful degree-$N$ permutation models, each embedded into $\operatorname{GL}_D(\mathbb F_p)$, that contains every action counted here. The logarithm of the maximum of one and its number is at most \[ \frac{2(\log p)^2}{\log2}D^4 +2(\log p)D^2. \tag{D.IM.3} \] Consequently, if positive integers $D_N$ satisfy $D_N^4\le B N\log(N+1)$ for a fixed $B$, these collections satisfy the hypotheses (D.MO.1)--(D.MO.2) of Lemma~\ref{D:permutation-matrix-model-count}, after enlarging its constant by an amount depending only on $p$ and $B$.

statement: [Proved: iterated fibrations with projective generic normalizations] Let $k$ be algebraically closed and suppose that \[ X_r\longrightarrow X_{r-1}\longrightarrow\cdots \longrightarrow X_0 \] is a sequence of dominant morphisms of normal connected proper $k$-schemes. Suppose $X_0$ is projective and, for each morphism in the sequence, the normalization of the reduced geometric generic fibre is projective. This normalization may have more than one connected component. Then $\mathcal H(X_i)$ holds for every $i$. In particular the conclusion holds if every morphism has generic fibre dimension at most one. Thus for every finite normal connected cover $Z\to X_r$ and every proper closed subset $Y\subset Z$, the group $Q(Z,Y)$ is topologically finitely generated. If $Y$ has codimension at least two, this is the full group $\pi_1(Z\setminus Y)$.
