statement: [Proved: log canonical omitted points on proper surfaces] Let $S$ be a normal proper surface over an algebraically closed field, and let $Y\subset S$ be finite. statement: [Proved: surface-detected Brauer-zero growth on complete local punctures] Let $(R,\mathfrak m,k)$ be a complete excellent normal local domain of dimension $d\ge2$, of equal characteristic $p>0$, with an algebraically closed coefficient field $k$. There is a constant $C_R$ such that, for every $q=p^f$ and $r\ge1$, \[ \#\left(\left\{\rho:\pi_1(U)\longrightarrow \operatorname{PGL}_r(\mathbf F_q): \operatorname{br}(h_i^*\rho)=0\text{ in } H^2(U_i,\mathbf G_m)\text{ for every }i \right\}/\operatorname{PGL}_r(\mathbf F_q)\right) \le q^{C_Rr^2}. \tag{D.LBT.1} \] In particular the bound holds for all representations with $\operatorname{br}(\rho)=0$ in $H^2(U,\mathbf G_m)$. statement: [Proved: linear-size Eisenstein charts and pointed isomorphism witnesses] Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field of arbitrary characteristic. For integers $e\ge2$ and $d\ge e-1$, put \[ N=\left\lfloor\frac{2d}{e}\right\rfloor+1. \tag{D.EA.1} \] There is an explicitly defined affine $k$-scheme $\mathcal E_{e,d}$ with the following properties; it is allowed to be empty. \begin{enumerate} \item Its coordinates are at most $e(N-1)\le2d$ polynomial coefficients and at most two auxiliary inverses. Its equations are linear coefficient vanishings and degree-two inverse equations. For every $k$-algebra $R$, a point determines a monic Eisenstein polynomial \[ f(X)=X^e+\sum_{i=1}^{e}a_i(t)X^{e-i},\qquad a_i(t)=\sum_{j=1}^{N-1}a_{ij}t^j. \tag{D.EA.2} \] The algebra $B_f=R[[t]][X]/(f)$ is finite free of rank $e$ over $R[[t]]$, is canonically a pointed formal disc $R[[\alpha]]$ over $R$, and satisfies \[ t=\alpha^e u,\qquad f'(\alpha)=\alpha^d v, \qquad u,v\in R[[\alpha]]^\times. \tag{D.EA.3} \] In particular $B_f[1/t]$ is finite etale over $R((t))$, and its discriminant ideal in $R[[t]]$ is $(t^d)$. \item Every separable extension of $k((t))$ of degree $e$ and different exponent $d$, with the valuation on its integer ring normalized to have value group $\mathbb Z$, is represented by a $k$-point of this chart. The same assertion holds after every algebraically closed extension of $k$. \item Over $\mathcal E_{e,d}\times\mathcal E_{e,d}$ there is an affine finite-presentation scheme $\mathcal W_{e,d}$ using, in total, at most $7d+6$ coordinates and equations of degree at most $e^2+1$. For every $k$-algebra $R$ and every pair $(f,g)$ over $R$, its fibre has an $R$-point if and only if there exists a continuous $R[[t]]$-algebra isomorphism $B_g\simeq B_f$ preserving the specified augmentations to $R$. Thus the witness is effective on arbitrary, including nonreduced, coefficient rings. \end{enumerate} Here a pointed formal disc means $R[[\alpha]]$ with its augmentation $\alpha\mapsto0$ and its $\alpha$-adic topology. The assertion about families is deliberately about augmentation-preserving isomorphisms; it makes no assertion that arbitrary nilpotent families of unpointed Laurent-series algebras have this presentation. At geometric points the distinction does not affect the represented local field extensions. The case $e=1,d=0$ is the single trivial extension and needs no parameters.

statement: [Proved: polynomial-complexity charts for bounded local branch data] Fix a finite ordered collection of nontrivial totally ramified branches over algebraically closed residue fields, with degrees $e_j\ge2$ and different exponents $d_j$. Put $D=\sum_jd_j$ and suppose $e_j\le n$. The product of the coefficient charts above uses at most $2D$ coefficient parameters, together with $O(D)$ inverse variables. The product pointed-isomorphism relation has an existential witness using $O(D)$ coordinates and equations of degree at most $n^2+1$. If $D\le cn$, allowing all such ordered degree/different lists and all their groupings into branch fibres requires at most $n^{O_c(n)}$ charts, still with $O_c(n)$ coordinates and polynomial degree in $n$. Unramified branches of degree one add no parameters. Every counted branch fibre is required to contain a nontrivial branch; arbitrarily many additional all-unramified marked fibres are not included in this combinatorial count. These are charts for local branch data, not a Hurwitz atlas for covers of a proper curve and not a bound for covers of a surface puncture.

statement: [Proved under stated hypotheses: local purity along the boundary] Let $Z$ be a normal connected proper scheme over an algebraically closed field, let $Y\subsetneq Z$ be closed, and put $U=Z\setminus Y$. statement: [Proved: Reduction of a complete local puncture to surfaces] Let $(A,\mathfrak m,k)$ be a complete excellent normal local domain of dimension $d\ge2$ with algebraically closed residue field, and let $U=\operatorname{Spec}A\setminus\{\mathfrak m\}$. statement: [Proved: the logarithmic fibration criterion] Let $k$ be algebraically closed, let $S$ be a normal connected proper surface, and let $f:S\to B$ be a morphism to a smooth connected proper curve. statement: [Proved: rational moving-line cohomology and Cech backgrounds] Fix a constant $c$ and an integer $h_0$. Let $m,s\geq1$, and let $X$ be a smooth projective connected curve over an algebraically closed field $k$, of genus at most $cm$, with a fixed finite separable map $x:X\to\mathbb P^1$ of degree at most $cm$. Fix at most $h_0$ moving line bundles with prescribed degrees of absolute value at most $cms$. There are ordered-divisor parameter charts with $O(ms)$ ambient coordinates, equations of degree polynomial in $m,s$, and open conditions, having the following properties. \begin{enumerate} \item Every collection of the prescribed lines over $k$ occurs. For every finite local Artinian $k$-algebra with residue field $k$, each collection of line-bundle deformations lifts to such a chart after a choice of a geometric divisor presentation. The chart formulas themselves are valid over arbitrary coefficient rings. \item Consider $O(m)$ line families obtained from this fixed number of moving lines by tensor products of bounded length, bounded positive or negative powers, one-step Frobenius in a fixed characteristic, and fixed deck translations preserving $x$, together with fixed line twists of degree $O(ms)$. Their section and cohomology complexes, evaluations, and fixed finite-pole restriction maps are represented by matrices of sizes and rational-entry degrees polynomial in $m,s$. No entries of these matrices are additional moduli coordinates. \item The base admits a cover by locally closed rational charts on which the relevant cohomology modules are free and all the specified matrices have rational splittings. The number of choices is at most \[ \exp\bigl(O(m\log(ms+1))\bigr). \tag{B.MB.2} \] The equations of these charts have degree polynomial in $m,s$. They can include all minors required for exact-rank conditions; no bound on the number of those minors is asserted or needed. \item On these charts one can choose actual representative, projection, and homotopy maps for the two-affine line Cech complexes, compatibly through all higher pole ranges. Through any prescribed pole range polynomial in $m,s$, all their coefficients are rational functions of degree polynomial in $m,s$. This construction introduces no new charts at each successive pole order. \end{enumerate} All implicit polynomials and constants depend only on $c,h_0$, the bounded tensor-word pattern, and the specified polynomial pole cutoff. Fixed curve coefficients and fixed line twists are background constants. For a chain of $f$ phases with a bounded number of moving lines per phase and only bounded-range interactions, the ambient background coordinates number $O(fms)$ and the chart count is $\exp(O(fm\log(ms+1)))$. The rank charts cover geometric points. An arbitrary noncoflat Artinian family is not asserted to factor through one exact-rank chart. All-ring splitting statements apply to points of the stated chart schemes. This distinction does not affect the Artinian surjectivity of the preceding ordered-divisor charts.

statement: [Proved: alternating socles outside the natural primitive action] Fix the characteristic $p$ and a finite collection $\mathcal F$ of nonabelian finite simple groups. For each $S_i$ of dimension at least two, assume that there is a proper birational morphism $q_i:Y_i\to S_i$, with $Y_i$ normal and projective, such that every prime divisor on $Y_i$ whose image is contained in $T_i$ and has codimension at least two in $S_i$ has zero-dimensional image. For an open subgroup $J$ the constant can be taken to be $c[Q:J]$. statement: [Proved: exact transport for a nonsplit automorphism preimage] Let $S$ be a finite nonabelian simple group, identify $S$ with $\operatorname{Inn}(S)$, and let $\Omega$ be a finite set. Put \[ W=\operatorname{Aut}(S)^\Omega\rtimes\operatorname{Sym}(\Omega), \qquad \overline W=\operatorname{Out}(S)^\Omega\rtimes \operatorname{Sym}(\Omega). \tag{D.NW.1} \] Let $P\leq\overline W$ act transitively on $\Omega$, and let $L$ be its full inverse image in $W$. For a continuous surjection $\beta:\Gamma\to P$ from a profinite group, choose $o\in\Omega$, put $H=\operatorname{Stab}_\Gamma(o)$, and define $\chi:H\to\operatorname{Out}(S)$ by the $o$-coordinate of $\beta|_H$. Then there is a bijection \[ \frac{\{\rho:\Gamma\to L:\overline\rho=\beta\}} {S^\Omega\text{-conjugacy}} \ \simeq\ \frac{\{\lambda:H\to\operatorname{Aut}(S): \overline\lambda=\chi\}} {S\text{-conjugacy}}. \tag{D.NW.2} \] All homomorphisms are continuous. No splitting of $1\to S^\Omega\to L\to P\to1$ is assumed. Every finite monolithic group with nonabelian socle $S^\Omega$ has precisely this form under its conjugation embedding, with $P=L/S^\Omega$. If $\Gamma\twoheadrightarrow L_k$ is a surjection to its $k$th crown power inducing the fixed quotient $\beta$, then $k$ is bounded by the cardinality on the right of (D.NW.2).

Let $S$ be a finite nonabelian simple group and suppose \[ S\leq\mathcal B_0\mathrel{\trianglelefteq}\mathcal B \leq\operatorname{Aut}(S),\qquad [\mathcal B:\mathcal B_0]\leq b_0. \tag{D.NP.1} \] Here $S$ is identified with its inner automorphism group. Assume there is an injective homomorphism \[ \iota:\mathcal B_0\hookrightarrow \operatorname{PGL}_r(\mathbb F_q) \rtimes\mathcal G_q, \qquad \iota(S)\subset\operatorname{PGL}_r(\mathbb F_q), \qquad \mathcal G_q=\operatorname{Gal}(\mathbb F_q/\mathbb F_p), \tag{D.NP.2} \] where $q=p^f$, such that \[ r^2\log q\leq\kappa\log|S|. \tag{D.NP.3} \] No embedding of $\mathcal B$ in an ambient projective semilinear group or extension of its outer action to that ambient group is assumed. Let $\Omega$ be a set of $t$ elements. Let $P\leq(\mathcal B/S)^\Omega\rtimes\operatorname{Sym}(\Omega)$ act transitively, and let $L$ be its full inverse image in $\mathcal B^\Omega\rtimes\operatorname{Sym}(\Omega)$. Assume $L$ is monolithic primitive, with socle $S^\Omega$. For every continuous surjection $\Gamma\twoheadrightarrow L_k$ whose induced quotient $\beta:\Gamma\twoheadrightarrow P$ is radially tame, one has \[ \begin{split} k&\leq |S^\Omega|^{c_R},\\ d(L_k)&\leq\max\{2,2g+1,c_R+2\},\\ c_R&=\max\{1,\lceil\kappa(A_Rb_0+1)+b_0-1\rceil\}. \end{split} \tag{D.NP.4} \] The field-image order inside $\mathcal B_0$ is unrestricted. There is also no independent order bound on $\mathcal B$. The normal-subgroup hypothesis (D.NP.1), the projective size comparison (D.NP.3), and tameness of the outer quotient remain explicit hypotheses.

statement: [Proved: Frobenius saturation of a finite normalization lattice] Let $A$ be a complete discrete valuation ring of characteristic $p>0$, with uniformizer $\pi$ and fraction field $K$. Let $B$ be its integral closure in a finite separable extension $L/K$. Write $e$ for the ramification index and $\delta$ for the different exponent. For every power $q$ of $p$, \[ \pi^{\lceil(q-1)\delta/e\rceil}B \subset A\cdot B^q\subset B. \tag{D.AG.6} \] No separability of the residue extension is assumed. Consequently, let $\rho:Y'\to Y$ be finite, dominant and generically separable between normal surfaces in characteristic $p$, with $Y$ smooth. Put $\mathcal B=\rho_*\mathcal O_{Y'}$. Suppose all ramification is supported on fixed prime divisors $D_j$, and at every prolongation of $D_j$ we have $\delta/e\le c_j$. Then $\mathcal B$ is locally free, and the relative Frobenius map gives actual inclusions \[ \mathcal B(-H)\subset \operatorname{im}(F_Y^*\mathcal B\longrightarrow\mathcal B) \subset\mathcal B, \qquad H=\sum_j\lceil(p-1)c_j\rceil D_j. \tag{D.AG.7} \] The divisor $H$ is independent of the degree of the covering.

statement: [Proved: the geometric-period root supports the coefficient gerbe] Use the complete local one-smooth-curve setting of Proposition~\ref{D:single-curve-Brauer-residue-cover}: $U=\operatorname{Spec}R-\{\mathfrak m\}$, $Y\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ is a projective regular resolution, $C$ is its single smooth exceptional curve, $g=g(C)$ and $C^2=-d<0$. Let $n$ be prime to $p$, and let $\alpha\in H^2(U,\mu_n)$. Write $\beta$ for its geometric Brauer class and $m$ for the order of $\beta$, taking $m=1$ when $\beta=0$. Then $m\mid n$, and the actual coefficient class $\alpha$ extends to a class \[ \overline\alpha\in H^2(\mathcal X,\mu_n),\qquad \mathcal X=\sqrt[m]{(Y,C)}. \tag{D.UJ.1} \] Let $\mathcal G\to\mathcal X$ be a gerbe for this class and $\mathcal D$ the reduced root divisor. The scalar-weight-one spectral torsor over $C$ for $\mathcal G_{\mathcal D}$ is connected of degree exactly $m$. Its class is the residue of $\beta$. In particular every scalar-weight-one vector bundle on $\mathcal G_U$ has rank divisible by $m$. There is an algebraic scalar-weight-one anchor $A$ of rank $m$ on $\mathcal G$, with all $m$ root characters once at each geometric point of $C$. Every scalar-weight-one bundle on $\mathcal G_U$ admits a vector-bundle lattice on $\mathcal G$. Every formal scalar-weight-one vector bundle along $\mathcal G_{\mathcal D}$ algebraizes, as do maps with any fixed divisor of poles. These algebraization assertions also hold after a finite local Artinian coefficient-base extension. The anchor is used for existence and descent, not as a rank-$mr$ coordinate presentation. Finally \[ |H^2(U,\mu_n)|=\gcd(n,d)\,n^{2g}. \tag{D.UJ.2} \] Consequently for $q=p^f$ and $n=q-1$ the number of coefficient classes of projective $\mathbb F_q$-representations is at most $dq^{2g}$. This includes their Kummer part, not only their geometric Brauer classes.

statement: [Proved: tame generators and twisted determinant classes] Let $\Gamma=\pi_1(U)$ and let $\Gamma^{\mathrm{rt}}$ be its quotient classifying radially tame finite etale covers. Then \[ d(\Gamma^{\mathrm{rt}})\leq 2g+1. \tag{D.RT.5} \] Let $A$ be a finite abelian group of order prime to $p$, endowed with a continuous $\Gamma$-action that factors through $\Gamma^{\mathrm{rt}}$. Inflation is an isomorphism and one has \[ H^1_{\mathrm{cont}}(\Gamma^{\mathrm{rt}},A) \xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }H^1_{\mathrm{cont}}(\Gamma,A), \qquad |H^1_{\mathrm{cont}}(\Gamma,A)| \leq |A|^{2g+1}. \tag{D.RT.6} \] In particular, let $V\to U$ be as in Lemma~\ref{D:radial-tame-cover-one-curve}, with $t=eu$, and put $H=\pi_1(V)$ and $g'=1+u(g-1)$. Fix $q=p^f$ and a field character \[ \chi:H\longrightarrow\operatorname{Gal} (\mathbb F_q/\mathbb F_p) \] that is radially tame on the smooth model $(Y',C')$. It need not extend etale over $Y'$. Then \[ |H^1_{\mathrm{cont}}(H,\mathbb F_q^*(\chi))| \leq(q-1)^{2g'+1}\leq q^{(2g+3)u} \leq q^{(2g+3)t}. \tag{D.RT.7} \] These are the semilinear determinant classes for the fixed field character. If the character is also allowed to vary subject to radial tameness, it has at most $f^{2g'+1}$ possibilities. Neither assertion requires the image order of $\chi$ to be prime to $p$.

statement: [Proved: quadratic projective counts with unrestricted geometric period] Let $R$ be a complete excellent normal local surface ring of characteristic $p>0$, with an algebraically closed coefficient and residue field $k$. Suppose a projective regular resolution $Y\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ has exceptional locus a single smooth connected curve $C$, with $C^2=-d<0$. Put $U=\operatorname{Spec}R-\{\mathfrak m\}$ and $\Gamma=\pi_1(U)$. Using the controlled-anchor construction of Lemma~\ref{D:controlled-one-curve-gerbe-anchors}, there is a constant $K_R$ such that, for every $q=p^f$ and every $r\geq1$, \[ \#\bigl(\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{cont}} (\Gamma,\operatorname{PGL}_r(\mathbb F_q)) /\operatorname{PGL}_r(\mathbb F_q)\bigr) \leq q^{K_Rr^2}. \tag{D.UP.1} \] The bound is uniform in the scalar order $q-1$ and in the geometric Brauer period. The latter need only divide $r$; it is not bounded in advance. This theorem is a local one-smooth-exceptional-curve statement. It does not assert finite generation of $\Gamma$ or settle general D.1 or D.2(ii).

statement: [Proved: failure of automatic radial tameness] Let $k$ be any algebraically closed field of characteristic $2$, and let $C/k$ be a smooth projective connected curve of genus $g\geq2$. There is a complete excellent normal local $k$-domain $R$ of dimension two, with residue field $k$, and a projective regular resolution \[ \pi_R:Y_R\longrightarrow\operatorname{Spec}R \tag{D.WS.1} \] whose reduced exceptional divisor is a single smooth curve $D$ of genus $g$ and square $D^2=1-g$. Its puncture $U=\operatorname{Spec}R\setminus\{\mathfrak m_R\}$ has a connected finite \'etale $\mathbb Z/2$-torsor which is not radially tame along $D$. In the corresponding extension of divisorial discrete valuation rings, the ramification index is $1$ and the residue extension is purely inseparable of degree $2$. The cover does not extend to a finite \'etale cover of $Y_R$. Consequently the hypothesis of a radially tame outer or permutation quotient in the one-curve crown results does not follow merely from the existence of one smooth exceptional curve. This example makes no claim against the representation-count bounds or finite generation.

statement: [Proved: matrix-model alternating bounds for original tame boundaries] Let $S$ be normal, proper and integral over an algebraically closed field of characteristic $p>0$, with $\dim S\ge2$, and let $T\subsetneq S$ be closed. In dimension greater than two, assume that either $T$ is finite or $(S,T)$ satisfies the controlled exceptional-centre hypothesis of Theorem~\ref{D:generic-surface-controlled-boundary}. Put $Q=Q(S,T)$, imposing tameness only along the original codimension-one components of $T$. There is one fixed finite collection of homomorphisms \[ \Lambda_x\longrightarrow Q \tag{D.OBM.1} \] in which each $\Lambda_x$ is a complete normal local surface puncture group, the original divisorial tame quotient of a complete normal local surface pair, a pro-prime-to-$p$ cyclic group, or the trivial group. These are precisely the fixed sources supplied by Lemma~\ref{D:tame-detecting-curve-local-pairs} after the stated surface reduction, as specified in the proof. For each source, choose finitely many fixed topologically finitely generated quotients, and choose finite permutation models satisfying (D.MO.1)--(D.MO.2), with fixed constants. Call a whole $\Lambda_x$-orbit on a finite $Q$-set admissible if its action factors through one of those quotients or is conjugate into one of its prescribed permutation models. For every fixed $K>0$, the number of isomorphism classes of degree-$n$ finite continuous $Q$-sets satisfying \[ \sum_x\ \sum_{\substack{O\in\Lambda_x\backslash X\\ O\text{ not admissible}}}|O|^2 \le K n\log(n+1) \tag{D.OBM.2} \] is at most $n^{A n}$, with $A$ depending only on the fixed data. Equivalently this counts all rank-$n$ finite etale covers of $S\setminus T$ belonging to the original tame quotient, including disconnected covers. For the first two kinds of source one may jointly choose the maximal pronilpotent and maximal pro-prime-to-$p$ quotients. For the last two, one may choose the whole source. One may simultaneously include all standard affine point and projective partial-flag models from Lemma~\ref{D:permutation-matrix-model-count}. Thus arbitrary sizes of all those orbit kinds are uncharged in (D.OBM.2). The local linear complements need not be solvable. The distinct natural $A_n$ quotient kernels satisfying (D.OBM.2) have multiplicity at most $|A_n|^c$ for one constant $c$, and the corresponding selected alternating simple-product quotient of $Q$ is topologically finitely generated. No exceptional-divisor tameness is imposed.

statement: [Proved: counting fixed permutation models through actual matrix homomorphisms] Let $\Lambda$ be the fundamental group of the punctured spectrum of a fixed complete normal local surface ring over an algebraically closed field of characteristic $p>0$. For every $N\ge2$, choose a finite collection of faithful permutation models \[ H_{N,j}\hookrightarrow S_N\qquad(j\in\mathcal J_N), \qquad H_{N,j}\hookrightarrow G_{N,j}, \quad G_{N,j}\in\{\operatorname{GL}_{r_{N,j}}(\mathbb F_{q_{N,j}}), \operatorname{PGL}_{r_{N,j}}(\mathbb F_{q_{N,j}})\}, \tag{D.MO.1} \] where every $q_{N,j}$ is a power of $p$. The two displayed embeddings are part of the fixed model. Assume that one constant $B$ satisfies \[ \log\max\{1,|\mathcal J_N|\}\le B N\log(N+1),\qquad \max_{j\in\mathcal J_N}r_{N,j}^{2}\log q_{N,j} \le B N\log(N+1). \tag{D.MO.2} \] An empty collection is allowed, with the empty maximum in (D.MO.2) interpreted as zero. Then the number of isomorphism classes of transitive $N$-element $\Lambda$-sets whose actions are conjugate into at least one model $H_{N,j}\le S_N$ is at most \[ \exp\bigl(C N\log(N+1)\bigr) \tag{D.MO.3} \] for a constant $C$ depending only on $\Lambda$ and $B$. This bound counts permutation sets, not merely their linearizations. The collections in (D.MO.1)--(D.MO.2) may include, simultaneously, all the following standard actions in characteristic $p$: \begin{enumerate} \item $\operatorname{AGL}_d(\mathbb F_q)$ on the $N=q^d$ vectors, for every $d\ge1$ and every power $q$ of $p$; \item $\operatorname{PGL}_d(\mathbb F_q)$ on all flags of any one fixed nonempty type of proper nonzero subspaces of $\mathbb F_q^d$, for every $d\ge2$ and every power $q$ of $p$. \end{enumerate} In particular the second family includes projective points and every Grassmannian. For the union of these standard families, the logarithm of the number of local $N$-element types is bounded by $C_p\bigl(1+\log^2(N+1)\bigr)$, with a constant also depending on $\Lambda$.

statement: [Proved: smallness and pronilpotent bounds do not imply finite generation] There is a small profinite group with trivial maximal prime-to-$2$ quotient such that every open subgroup has finite maximal pronilpotent quotient, but which is not topologically finitely generated. Set \[ m_n=|A_n|^n+1,\qquad G=\prod_{n\geq5}A_n^{m_n}. \] The alternating groups $A_n$ for $n\geq5$ are nonabelian simple groups of even order \cite[Theorem 1.1, p.~1, with proofs in sections 3--7]{ConradAnD}. For any fixed finite group $F$, a homomorphism $A_n\to F$ is trivial once $|A_n|>|F|$. A continuous homomorphism $G\to F$ consequently kills the whole corresponding tail: finite-support elements are dense there. It factors through a finite product of finite groups, so there are only finitely many such homomorphisms. Taking $F=S_r$ proves smallness. If $d$ elements generate $S^m$ for a finite group $S$, their coordinate $d$-tuples must all differ. Otherwise the generated subgroup lies in the proper equality diagonal between two coordinates. Hence $m\leq |S|^d$. The finite quotient $A_n^{m_n}$ therefore requires more than $n$ generators, proving that $G$ is not finitely generated. An open subgroup $H$ contains the entire product of the blocks with $n>N$ for some $N$. Every finite nilpotent quotient kills that tail, because each $A_n$ is perfect and a finite nilpotent perfect group is trivial. Thus $H$'s maximal pronilpotent quotient factors through the finite quotient by that tail. Every odd-order quotient of $G$ is trivial by simplicity and even order of the factors. This proves all the asserted restrictions. The attached \texttt{check\_small\_group\_obstruction.py} checks the eleven finite coordinate-count certificates for $5\leq n\leq15$. The separate \texttt{check\_pronilpotent\_obstruction.py} exhaustively checks the $A_5$ base facts, including all products, commutators and nontrivial normal closures. These programs do not replace the proof for arbitrary $n$ or the infinite product argument. The construction is an abstract obstruction to an inference, not a geometric counterexample to D.1 or D.2(ii).

statement: [Proved: degree-linear size of punctured-cover resolutions] Let $(S,s)$ be a normal algebraic surface germ over an algebraically closed field of positive characteristic. Fix a projective resolution $Y\to S$ which is an isomorphism away from $s$, with nonempty exceptional curves $E_i$, and a strictly anti-nef positive cycle \[ A=\sum_i a_iE_i,\qquad c_i=-A\cdot E_i>0. \] Put \[ a=\sum_i a_i,\qquad b=K_Y\cdot A+a,\qquad c=3b+a, \qquad \lambda=\max_i\frac{b}{a_ic_i}. \tag{D.LR.1} \] For any connected finite etale cover of $S\setminus\{s\}$ of degree $n$, normalize $Y$ in its field, resolve, and contract all smooth rational $(-1)$-curves which map to points of $Y$. Let $f:Z\to Y$ be the resulting proper generically finite morphism. The cover need not be Galois. Then \[ \#\operatorname{Irr}\bigl((f^*A)_{\mathrm{red}}\bigr) \le n(b+a)+(95+93\lambda)nc. \tag{D.LR.2} \] In particular the number of exceptional components, the sum of their arithmetic genera, and the sum of the negatives of their self-intersections are all bounded linearly in $n$, with constants depending only on the fixed germ, resolution, and cycle. The same assertion holds for covers of the punctured strict henselization, with the same constants. This is an estimate for resolutions of covers unramified outside the isolated point. It does not assert an object atlas, a bound on the number of covers, or finite generation of the local group.

Then $R'$ is a complete normal local domain with residue field $k$, $Y'\to\operatorname{Spec}R'$ is a projective regular resolution, and its puncture is exactly $V$. Its reduced exceptional fibre is one smooth connected curve $C'$. There are integers $e,u\geq1$ such that $e$ is prime to $p$, the map $C'\to C$ is finite etale of degree $u$, and \[ h^*C=eC',\qquad t=eu,\qquad g(C')-1=u(g-1),\qquad (C')^2=-\frac{u\delta}{e}. \tag{D.RT.1} \] In particular $u\delta/e$ is a positive integer. The map $h$ is finite locally free. No Galois hypothesis is needed.

statement: [Proved: degree-two classes with tame cyclic coefficients] Retain the complete one-smooth-exceptional-curve setting of Lemma~\ref{D:radial-tame-cover-one-curve}. Let $\mathcal M$ be a finite locally constant sheaf on $U$ whose fibres are cyclic groups of order $n$, with $n$ prime to $p$. Suppose its monodromy is radially tame along $C$. Then \[ |H^2_{\mathrm{et}}(U,\mathcal M)|\leq n^{2g+1},\qquad |H^2_{\mathrm{cont}}(\pi_1(U),M)|\leq n^{2g+1}, \tag{D.T2.1} \] where $M$ is a geometric fibre with its monodromy action. For $n=1$ both groups are trivial. No prime-to-$p$ condition is imposed on the order of the entire monodromy image; only the coefficient order and radial tameness are assumed. For a degree-$t=eu$ radially tame cover $U_H\to U$ and a tame field character $\chi:H=\pi_1(U_H)\to\operatorname{Gal}(\mathbb F_q/\mathbb F_p)$, where $q=p^f$, this gives \[ |H^2_{\mathrm{cont}}(H,\mathbb F_q^*(\chi))| \leq(q-1)^{2g(C_H)+1}\leq q^{(2g+3)t}. \tag{D.T2.2} \] This bounds the scalar obstruction classes for projective semilinear representations with that fixed field character. It does not assert inflation in degree two through the radial tame quotient.

statement: [Proved: a rank-period generator after subdividing root nodes] Let \(R\) be a complete excellent normal local surface algebra over an algebraically closed coefficient and residue field \(k\) of characteristic \(p>0\), and put \(U=\operatorname{Spec}R-\{\mathfrak m\}\). Let \(n\) be prime to \(p\), and let \(\alpha\in H^2(U,\mu_n)\) be realized by a positive-rank scalar-weight-one twisted bundle. Write \(\beta\) for its geometric Brauer image and \(M\) for the order of \(\beta\). Fix a regular resolution with SNC exceptional divisor \(E=\bigcup_i E_i\). Let \(m_i\) be the order of the generic residue of \(\beta\) on \(E_i\); order one is allowed. At a node \(x\in E_i\cap E_j\), let \(h_x\) be the order of its secondary residue. Blow up every node once, writing \(Y'\to Y\) for the result. On \(Y'\), give the strict transform of \(E_i\) root order \(m_i\), and give the new exceptional curve over \(x\) root order \(h_x\). Omit roots of order one. Let \(\mathcal X'\) be this regular mixed-root stack. There is an actual \(\mu_n\)-gerbe \(\mathcal G'\to\mathcal X'\) restricting to the prescribed coefficient gerbe of \(\alpha\) on \(U\), and a scalar-weight-one locally free sheaf \(\mathcal A\) of rank exactly \(M\) on \(\mathcal G'\) with the following properties. \begin{enumerate} \item \(\mathcal A\) contains every scalar-weight-one geometric inertia simple at every point. Thus it is a generating bundle for the weight-one category. \item If \(\mathcal F\) is a scalar-weight-one locally free sheaf of rank \(r\), then \(M\mid r\). Put \(s=r/M\), let \(q:\mathcal G'\to Y'\) be the coarse map, and set \[ \mathcal B=q_*\mathcal End(\mathcal A),\qquad \mathcal E=q_*\mathcal Hom(\mathcal A,\mathcal F). \tag{D.RA.1} \] The ordinary algebra \(\mathcal B\) is locally free of rank \(M^2\), and \(\mathcal E\) is locally free as a right \(\mathcal B\)-module of rank \(s\), locally for the etale topology on \(Y'\). For this fixed \(\mathcal A\), the corresponding Morita functors are exact and commute with extension of coefficient rings. Their restriction identifies weight-one vector-bundle families of rank \(r\) with locally free right \(\mathcal B\)-module families of rank \(s\). \item If the original SNC model has \(v\) components and \(e\) nodes, the construction adds \(e\) curves and replaces its nodes by \(2e\) nodes. It therefore uses \(O_R(t)\) centres on the controlled SNC models of degree-\(t\) covers. Pullbacks of the previously chosen cycles retain their already proved cohomology and intersection budgets. \end{enumerate} The construction of \(\mathcal A\) is qualitative. It asserts no uniform bound for the cohomology, generation, or formal pole constants of the particular order \(\mathcal B\).

statement: [Proved under stated hypotheses: rational exceptional trees] Let $A$ be the local ring of a normal surface over an algebraically closed field $k$ of characteristic $p>0$. Let $f:Y\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ be a projective resolution, isomorphic away from the closed point. Assume that its reduced exceptional divisor $E=\bigcup_{i=1}^rE_i$ has simple normal crossings, that each $E_i$ is isomorphic to $\mathbf P^1_k$, and that its dual graph is a tree. Then $A$ is $\mathbf Q$-factorial. More precisely, there is an integer $a\geq0$, depending on this resolution, such that \[ |\det(E_i\cdot E_j)|p^a\,\operatorname{Cl}(A)=0. \] The proposition does not require that $A$ have a rational singularity. For a regular local ring the conclusion holds with annihilator one.

statement: [Known correspondence: full-module realization and determination on a reduction cycle] Let $A$ be a complete excellent normal local surface $k$-algebra with algebraically closed coefficient and residue field $k$, of arbitrary characteristic. Let $\pi:Y\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ be a projective regular resolution, an isomorphism away from the closed point, and let $Z>0$ have full exceptional support. Assume that $\mathcal O_Z(-Z)$ and $\omega_Z^{-1}$ are generically generated by their global sections and that $H^1(Z,\mathcal O_Z(-Z))=0$. For a finite reflexive $A$-module $M$, put \[ \mathcal F_M=(\pi^*M)^{\vee\vee},\qquad R_Z(M)=\mathcal F_M|_Z. \] The functor $R_Z$ is injective on isomorphism classes. A vector bundle $V$ on $Z$ is in its essential image if and only if: \begin{enumerate} \item $V$ is generically generated by global sections; \item there is a vector bundle $V_2$ on $2Z$, with $V_2|_Z\simeq V$, for which the boundary map \[ \delta_0:H^0(Z,V(Z))\longrightarrow H^1(Z,V) \tag{D.KR.6} \] is injective. This is the boundary of $0\to V\to V_2(Z)\to V(Z)\to0$. \end{enumerate} In addition, for a full bundle $\mathcal F=\mathcal F_M$ and $V=\mathcal F|_Z$, restriction induces \[ H^1(Y,\mathcal End\mathcal F) \simeq H^1(Z,\mathcal End V), \quad\text{equivalently}\quad \operatorname{Ext}^1_Y(\mathcal F,\mathcal F) \simeq\operatorname{Ext}^1_Z(V,V). \tag{D.KR.7} \] The object correspondence is the known Kahn--Gavran theorem. The proof below records its precise complete-ring scope and the characteristic-independent marking and tangent-space verification; no new classification theorem is claimed. These are pointwise object and tangent-space statements. They do not assert fullness on morphisms, lifting of a prescribed isomorphism on $Z$, or an equivalence for arbitrary Artinian parameter families.

statement: [Proved: uniform generation of reflexive pullbacks] Let $(A,\mathfrak m,k)$ be an excellent normal local surface $k$-algebra with algebraically closed residue field $k$ and a dualizing complex. Let $\pi:Y\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ be a proper regular resolution, with exceptional curves $E_i$, and let $Z>0$ be an effective exceptional Cartier divisor of full support. Assume that \[ -Z\cdot B\ge 2p_a(B) \quad\text{for every nonzero effective exceptional cycle }B. \tag{D.UG.1} \] If $F$ is a vector bundle on $Y$ admitting a map $\mathcal O_Y^a\to F$ which is surjective at every exceptional generic point, then \[ H^1(Y,F(-Z))=0,\qquad H^1(Y,F(-Z)\otimes I_{P,Y})=0\quad(P\in E), \tag{D.UG.2} \] and $F(-Z)$ is generated by its global sections. Here $P$ ranges over closed points of the exceptional fibre. In particular the assertion applies to $F=(\pi^*M)^{\vee\vee}$ for every finite reflexive $A$-module $M$, with a single choice of $Z$ independent of $M$ and its rank. On a minimal resolution with $\kappa_i=K_Y\cdot E_i\ge0$, it suffices to choose the cycle in Lemma~\ref{D:integral-antinef-energy-cycle} so that \[ -Z\cdot E_i\ge3\kappa_i\quad(\kappa_i>0), \qquad -Z\cdot E_i\ge0\quad(\kappa_i=0). \tag{D.UG.3} \] An entirely zero-canonical connected component can instead be given its rational-double-point fundamental cycle.

statement: [Proved: exact realization of relative Artin module data] Set \(S=k[[x,y]]\), let \(d=\operatorname{rank}_S R\), and fix \(L\geq3\). Put \(J_L=(x^L,y^L)\subset S\). An action of \[ R_A/I_L^2 \quad\hbox{on}\quad (S_A/J_L^2)^{dr} \] extending its given \(S_A/J_L^2\)-module structure has a reduction \(T_A\) modulo \(I_L\) which is the exact reduction of a relative maximal Cohen--Macaulay \(R_A\)-module \(M_A\). Its closed fibre has rank \(r\) over \(R\), and it is free of rank \(dr\) over \(S_A\). Conversely every rank-\(r\) maximal Cohen--Macaulay \(R\)-module supplies such data. Over \(k\), the isomorphism class of \(M\) is determined by \(M/I_LM\). At fixed \(L\), the action data above are described by \(O(r^2)\) scalar variables and \(O(r^2)\) polynomial equations of bounded degree, with constants depending on \(R,L\), not on \(r\).

statement: [Proved: relative Noether-different parameters and prescribed jets] There is a system of parameters \(x,y\) of \(R\) with the following properties. Put \(I_b=(x^b,y^b)R_A\). For every relative maximal Cohen--Macaulay module \(M_A\), multiplication by \(x\) and by \(y\) factors through finite free \(R_A\)-modules. Consequently, if \(N_A\) is any finite \(R_A\)-module on which \(x,y\) is a regular sequence, every homomorphism \[ M_A/I_bM_A\longrightarrow N_A/I_bN_A,\qquad b\geq2, \] lifts to a homomorphism \(M_A\to N_A\) agreeing with the prescribed map modulo \(I_{b-1}\). The target is not required to be flat over \(A\). For \(H=\operatorname{Hom}_{R_A}(M_A,N_A)\) and \(K_c=\operatorname{Hom}_{R_A}(M_A,I_cN_A)\), we also have \[ I_cH\subset K_c \subset (x^c,y^c,x^{c-1}y^{c-1})H \subset I_{c-1}H \qquad(c\geq2). \tag{L1} \]

statement: [Proved: a uniform bound for residual inseparability] Let $M/F$ be a finitely generated extension of fields of characteristic $p>0$. There is a finite purely inseparable extension $F_0/F$, depending only on $M/F$, with the following property: for every finite extension $L/F$ in a common overfield for which $LM/M$ is separable, we have \[ [L:F]_{\mathrm{insep}}\mid [F_0:F]. \] We may choose any $F_0$ for which $MF_0/F_0$ is separable. In characteristic zero the corresponding bound is one.

statement: [Proved: normalized line comparisons and Frobenius transport] Use the setting and choices of Proposition~\ref{D:residual-twisted-spectral-category}. Fix $f\ge1$ with $q=p^f\equiv1\pmod n$, and put $u_a=p^a\pmod n$, $0\le a\le f$. Choose universal lines $\Lambda_a$ on $\mathcal G_{R_{u_a}}$, with the same choice at $a=f$ as at $a=0$. Their choices may be normalized so that their rational degrees on every connected component lie in $[0,1)$. Tensoring a line by its $p$th power induces an isomorphism \[ \sigma_a:R_{u_a}\longrightarrow R_{u_{a+1}} \tag{D.RF.4} \] over $C$. There is a line bundle $B_a$ on $R_{u_a}$ with \[ \Lambda_a^{\otimes p} \simeq \sigma_a^*\Lambda_{a+1}\otimes\pi_{u_a}^*B_a, \qquad 0\le\deg(B_a|_Z)\le p-1 \tag{D.RF.5} \] for every connected component $Z$ of $R_{u_a}$; the first pullback in this display includes the identity on $\mathcal G$. Although $R_{u_f}=R_{u_0}$, the composite $\sigma=\sigma_{f-1}\cdots\sigma_0$ need not be the identity. It is an automorphism of the $\mathbb Z/n$-torsor $R_{u_0}$. A Frobenius cycle must retain this final automorphism.

statement: [Proved: the composite-order residual spectral category] Let $C$ be a smooth proper connected curve over an algebraically closed field $k$ of characteristic $p>0$, and let $n$ be prime to $p$. Let $\mathcal X\to C$ be a banded $\mu_n$-gerbe and let $\mathcal G\to\mathcal X$ be a second banded $\mu_n$-gerbe. Call the band of the second gerbe the scalar band. For $u\in\mathbb Z/n$, let $\mathcal P_u$ be the relative stack of invertible sheaves on $\mathcal G$ on which the scalar band acts with character $u$. There is a finite etale $\mathbb Z/n$-torsor $h_u:R_u\to C$ such that $\mathcal P_u\to R_u$ is a $\mathbb G_m$-gerbe. This gerbe is neutral. Choose a corresponding universal line $\Lambda_u$ on $\mathcal G_{R_u}=\mathcal G\times_C R_u$, and write $\pi_u:\mathcal G_{R_u}\to R_u$ and $j_u:\mathcal G_{R_u}\to\mathcal G$. Then the functors \[ \begin{split} \mathcal V&\longmapsto (\pi_u)_*\mathcal Hom(\Lambda_u,j_u^*\mathcal V),\\ W&\longmapsto (j_u)_*(\Lambda_u\otimes\pi_u^*W) \end{split} \tag{D.RF.1} \] are inverse equivalences between scalar-weight-$u$ vector bundles on $\mathcal G$ and vector bundles on $R_u$. Their evaluation maps and the equivalence commute with arbitrary coefficient-base change, including nonreduced Artinian bases. If the class of $R_u$ has order $m$ in $H^1(C,\mathbb Z/n)$, then $R_u$ has $n/m$ connected components, each of degree $m$ over $C$. For a bundle $W$ of rank $s_j$ on the $j$th component, the corresponding bundle in (D.RF.1) has rank \[ m\sum_j s_j. \tag{D.RF.2} \] This is a statement about the residual gerbe category. It does not assert a rank drop for a representation of a whole punctured surface group after restriction to a Brauer-splitting cover.

statement: [Proved: the root-stack interpretation of Example 2] Let $D_1,\ldots,D_m$ be effective Cartier divisors on $S$, and let $n_i$ be positive integers invertible on $S$, as imposed in 29/200--201. statement: [Proved: explicit Newton lifting and averaging for scaled-separable actions] Let $S$ be a commutative ring, complete and separated for $(z)$, where $z$ is a nonzerodivisor. Let $P$ be a finite projective unital associative $S$-algebra of positive rank at every point, and suppose that an actual tensor \[ e=\sum_i a_i\otimes b_i\in P\otimes_S P, \qquad (a\otimes1)e=e(1\otimes a),\qquad \sum_i a_i b_i=z^s\,1 \tag{D.SN.7} \] is fixed, for an integer $s\ge0$. Let $V$ be a finite projective $S$-module. Suppose a unital $S$-linear map $\rho:P\to\operatorname{End}_S(V)$ has multiplicativity defect in $z^N\operatorname{End}_S(V)$, with $N>2s$. Then the explicit iteration below produces a unital algebra map $\rho_\infty$ with \[ \rho_\infty\equiv\rho\pmod {z^{N-s}}. \tag{D.SN.8} \] In particular a sufficiently precise truncated action on a locally free module admits, locally after lifting its underlying unital linear map, an exact formal action with the stated loss of precision. It does not assert that the whole original $N$-jet is retained. If $\rho$ on $V$ and $\sigma$ on $W$ are already exact actions, and $f:V\to W$ is $S$-linear with intertwining defect divisible by $z^N$, $N\ge s$, then \[ \operatorname{Av}(f)=z^{-s}\sum_i\sigma(a_i)f\rho(b_i) \tag{D.SN.9} \] is an integral exact intertwiner, congruent to $f$ modulo $z^{N-s}$. If $N>s$ and $f$ is invertible modulo $z$, then $\operatorname{Av}(f)$ is an isomorphism. Consequently two exact actions on the same module which are congruent modulo $z^N$, $N>s$, are conjugate by an automorphism congruent to the identity modulo $z^{N-s}$. The constructions work with nilpotent coefficient rings and are compatible with coefficient changes for which $z$ remains regular and the prescribed adic completions are taken. For the fixed full orders of the preceding lemma the local action loss has $s=2$, and for their Frobenius pullbacks it has $s=2p$. This is local algebra-action and intertwiner effectivity, not simultaneous global object, Morita-unit or cocycle effectivity.

statement: [Proved: Brauer residues and period-degree covers for one exceptional curve] Let $(R,\mathfrak m,k)$ be a complete excellent normal local $k$-algebra of dimension two, with algebraically closed coefficient and residue field $k$ of characteristic $p>0$. Put $U=\operatorname{Spec}R-\{\mathfrak m\}$. Suppose that there is a projective regular resolution $\pi:Y\to\operatorname{Spec}R$, an isomorphism over $U$, whose reduced exceptional fibre is one smooth connected curve $C$. Write $g=g(C)$ and $C^2=-d<0$. For every positive integer $n$ prime to $p$, residue gives a canonical isomorphism \[ \operatorname{Br}'(U)[n] \simeq H^1(C,\mathbf Z/n\mathbf Z), \qquad |\operatorname{Br}'(U)[n]|=n^{2g}, \tag{D.RC.1} \] where $\operatorname{Br}'$ denotes cohomological torsion Brauer classes. If $\alpha$ has order $m$ prime to $p$, there is a connected cyclic finite etale cover $Y'\to Y$ of degree exactly $m$ such that its restriction $V\to U$ kills $\alpha$. The cover $V$ is the puncture of a complete excellent normal local ring $R'$ finite over $R$. The induced resolution $Y'\to\operatorname{Spec}R'$ has a single smooth connected exceptional curve $C'$, with \[ g(C')-1=m(g-1),\qquad (C')^2=-md. \tag{D.RC.2} \] Thus the splitting cover is etale on the entire resolution, not only on the puncture. No assertion about a representation count uniform in $m$ is part of this proposition.

statement: [Proved: fixed Cartier-cycle recovery on etale resolution covers] Use the preceding proposition with the fixed canonical-defect and Noether-different ideal $J$ of Proposition~\ref{D:cover-uniform-canonical-defect}. Let $h:Y'\to Y$ be a connected finite etale cover of degree $n$, and let $A=H^0(Y',\mathcal O_{Y'})$ be its complete normal local Stein ring. Put $C'=h^*C$. For every reflexive $A$-module $M$ of rank $r$, set $F=(\pi'^*M)^{\vee\vee}$ on the resolution $\pi':Y'\to\operatorname{Spec}A$. There is a fixed integer $c\ge0$ such that, for $b\ge2\ell-1+2c$, the natural section image \[ W_b=\operatorname{im}\bigl( H^0((b+1)aC',F|_{(b+1)aC'}) \longrightarrow H^0(baC',F|_{baC'})\bigr) \] satisfies \[ W_b/(f^\ell,g^\ell)W_b \simeq M/(f^\ell,g^\ell)M. \tag{D.CP.5} \] The identification is functorial for actual module maps. In particular the multiple of $C'$ needed to recover a fixed module jet is independent of $n,r$ and of the Brauer period of a splitting cover.

statement: [Proved: finite flat sparse charts and exact finite isomorphism witnesses] Fix a field $\kappa$, integers $e,f\ge1$, a monic irreducible polynomial $\psi\in\kappa[U]$ of degree $f$, and an integer $\delta\ge0$. Put \[ n=ef,\qquad N=\left\lfloor\frac{2\delta}{e}\right\rfloor+2. \tag{D.SD.1} \] There is an affine polynomial chart over $\kappa$ with at most $(3N+2)n$ coordinates, and a polynomial witness for equivalence of two chart objects with at most $(8N+4)n+1$ coordinates including both objects. All equations may be taken of degree at most \[ (4N+12)n^3+1. \tag{D.SD.2} \] The assertions have the following precise meaning. For every $\kappa$-algebra $R$, a chart point gives a finite free $R[[t]]$-algebra $C$ of rank $n$, with elements $u,s$ such that $s^e=t$ times a unit, $s$ is a nonzerodivisor, $C/(s)=R[U]/(\psi)$, and $C[1/t]$ is finite etale over $R((t))$. Its relative K\"ahler different is $(s^\delta)$. Every $\kappa$-valued object is a complete DVR with uniformizer $s$, ramification index $e$, residue field $\kappa[U]/(\psi)$, and different exponent $\delta$. For two chart points over any $R$, the finite witness has an $R$-point if and only if their complete algebras are continuously isomorphic over $R[[t]]$. This is an existence test, not an assertion that a prescribed truncated isomorphism lifts without loss of precision. No marking of the residue algebra or augmentation is imposed on the isomorphisms. Finally, every finite complete DVR $B$ over $\kappa[[t]]$ with separable fraction field, these invariants, and residue field generated by a root of $\psi$, is isomorphic to a chart object.

statement: [Proved: symplectic and orthogonal simple quotients] Let $Q$ and $p$ satisfy the hypotheses of Proposition~\ref{D:bounded-scalar-projective-growth}. statement: [Proved: Boundedness of the canonical parabolic lattices] Let $S$ be a normal proper connected surface over an algebraically closed field $k$ of characteristic $p>0$, and let $D$ be a reduced divisor. Put $S^\circ=S\setminus\Sigma$, $U^\circ=S^\circ\setminus D$, and let $Q^\circ$ be the quotient of $\pi_1(U^\circ)$ classifying covers tame at the generic points of the original components of $D$. Fix a projective resolution $\pi:Y\to S$, an isomorphism over $S^\circ$, and a positive exceptional divisor $Z$ with $Z\cdot E_i<0$ for every exceptional component. statement: [Proved: radially tame projective semilinear hereditary count] Let $R$ be a complete excellent normal local surface algebra over an algebraically closed field $k$ of characteristic $p>0$, with residue field $k$. Put $g=g(C)$, $C^2=-\delta<0$, and $\Gamma=\pi_1(U)$. There is a constant $A_R$ with the following property. Then \[ N_\chi(H,r,q)\leq q^{A_Rtr^2}. \tag{D.PS.1} \] No bound on $|\operatorname{im}\chi|$, the scalar order $q-1$, or the geometric Brauer period is assumed. Only the cover of $H$ and the specified field character are required to be radially tame; the projective representation itself may have wild geometric inertia.

statement: [Proved: killing a degree-zero obstruction] Let $C/k$ be a smooth proper connected curve over an algebraically closed field of characteristic $p>0$, let $L$ be a torsion line bundle of degree zero, and let $e\in H^1(C,L)$. There is a finite map $h:C'\to C$, obtained by a sequence of finite \'etale covers and relative Frobenius morphisms, such that $h^*L\simeq\mathcal O_{C'}$ and $h^*e=0$. If the product of the \'etale degrees is $s$ and the product of the Frobenius degrees is $q$, then \[ \deg h=qs,\qquad g(C')-1=s(g(C)-1). \] The Frobenius degree can be increased arbitrarily after these two vanishing properties have been achieved.

statement: [Proved: uniform normal depth and quadratic Hom cohomology] Use the preceding setting. Normalize their universal lines to rational degrees in $[0,1)$, as in Proposition~\ref{D:residual-twisted-Frobenius-transport}. statement: [Proved: twisted determinant classes on etale resolution covers] Let $(R,\mathfrak m,k)$ be a complete excellent normal local $k$-algebra of dimension two, with algebraically closed coefficient and residue field $k$ of characteristic $p>0$. In particular, let $q=p^f$, and fix a continuous field character \[ \chi:\pi_1(U_t)\longrightarrow \operatorname{Gal}(\mathbb F_q/\mathbb F_p) \] that factors through $\pi_1(Y_t)$. For a sufficiently general Lefschetz pencil of hyperplane sections, its vanishing cycles in the middle $\mathbb Z_\ell$-cohomology of a smooth member, with the usual Tate twist, form one orbit under the geometric monodromy group. statement: [Proved: arbitrary-dimensional vertical boundary] Let $X$ be a normal connected proper scheme over an algebraically closed field and let $f:X\to B$ be a nonconstant morphism to a proper curve. Let $Y\subsetneq X$ be a closed subset with $f(Y)$ finite. Then $Q(X,Y)$ is topologically finitely generated. statement: [Proved: birational and finite-normalization descent of the fibration criterion] Let $S$ be a normal connected proper surface over an algebraically closed field, and let $V\subset S$ be a nonempty open. Suppose a proper birational map $q:X\to S$ from a smooth proper surface has a curve fibration for which $U=q^{-1}(V)$ satisfies either Proposition~\ref{D:vertical-fibration-exact} or Proposition~\ref{D:vertical-fibration-multiplicity}. Then $\pi_1(V)$ is topologically finitely generated, and inherits any generator bound supplied by the relevant case. In particular, the same is true of any fixed-boundary tame quotient of $\pi_1(V)$. For a possibly nonnormal proper scheme of dimension at most two, the same conclusion holds if its reduced components have finite normalizations and their inverse-image opens satisfy this condition, with lower-dimensional components having finitely generated fundamental groups. In particular, the latter requirement is automatic for a boundary of codimension at least two in every component.

statement: [Proved: vertical boundary meeting every fibre] Let $k$ be algebraically closed, let $X$ be a normal connected proper surface, and let $f:X\to B$ be a morphism to a smooth connected proper curve. Suppose that over a nonempty open $B^\circ\subset B$ the morphism is flat with geometrically reduced, geometrically connected one-dimensional fibres. Let $U\subset X$ be an open containing $X^\circ=f^{-1}(B^\circ)$ and meeting every fibre of $f$. Then $\pi_1(U)$ is topologically finitely generated. No restriction on the multiplicities of the exceptional fibres is required. More precisely, let $N$ be the image of $\pi_1(X_{\overline\eta})$ in $\pi_1(U)$ and put $Q=\pi_1(U)/N$. For each $b\in B\setminus B^\circ$, let $m_b$ be the gcd of the multiplicities of the fibre components whose generic points lie in $U$. The image in $Q$ of the full inertia group at $b$ is finite of order dividing $m_b$. If all $m_b$ equal one, then $Q=\pi_1(B)$ and the homotopy sequence in Proposition~\ref{D:vertical-fibration-exact} is exact. If the geometric generic fibre is smooth of genus $g$, $B$ has genus $h$, and every $m_b$ is prime to the positive characteristic, then $\pi_1(U)$ has at most $2g+2h+r$ generators, where $r=\#(B\setminus B^\circ)$.

statement: [Proved: generation and determinants from one weak cycle] Let $Y$ be projective over a complete Noetherian local $k$-algebra, and let $Z$ be an effective Cartier divisor with the entire closed fibre as support. Assume that $Z$ is a proper one-dimensional $k$-scheme and that \[ H^1(Z,\mathcal O_Z(-jZ))=0\qquad(j\ge1). \tag{D.GD.1} \] For a $k$-algebra $B$, work on the formal coefficient base change of $Y$ along $Z$. Let $\mathcal F$ be a formal vector bundle of rank $r$. Suppose that $V=\mathcal F(-Z)|_{Z_B}$ is supplied with a surjection $\mathcal O_{Z_B}^{h}\to V$. Then $\mathcal F(-Z)$ is generated by $h$ formal global sections extending those specified generators. Restriction on isomorphism classes of line bundles from the formal coefficient base change to $Z_B$ is injective. In particular, if $L$ is a fixed line bundle on $Y$ and an isomorphism $\det V\simeq L|_{Z_B}$ is supplied, it extends to an isomorphism \[ \det(\mathcal F(-Z))\simeq L_B \quad\hbox{on the formal coefficient base change}. \tag{D.GD.2} \] The extending generators and determinant isomorphism need not be unique. After choosing them over $B$, their pullbacks have the same properties over every coefficient $B$-algebra. For finite-type or finite local Artinian coefficient algebras, these assertions algebraize on the proper Noetherian completed base.

statement: [Proved: weighted component bound with arbitrary characteristic] Let $k$ be algebraically closed, let $x_1,\ldots,x_N$ have positive integral weights $w_1,\ldots,w_N$, and let $D\geq\max_i w_i$ be an integer. If a closed subscheme $V\subset\mathbb A^N_k$ is defined by any finite number of polynomials of weighted degree at most $D$, then \[ \#\operatorname{Irr}(V) \leq (N+1)\frac{D^N}{\prod_{i=1}^N w_i}. \tag{D.WB.1} \] The same bound applies to an open subscheme of $V$ and to the number of nonempty clopen parts in any partition of that open subscheme. The weights may be divisible by $\operatorname{char}k$.

statement: [Proved: weighted compression of the exceptional graph] Retain the notation and hypotheses of Proposition~\ref{D:exceptional-degree-linear-core}, including the degree $n$ and constants $a,b,c=3b+a$. For a component $F$ of the exceptional support, let $m_F$ be its positive integral coefficient in $f^*A$. Mark a noncore vertex if its curve meets the core. Then \[ \sum_{F\in\mathcal K}m_F(-F^2)\le nc, \qquad \sum_{Q\text{ marked}}m_Q\le nc. \tag{D.WC.1} \] Every connected noncore block meets the core, so there are at most $nc$ such blocks. Each noncore block is a path, or a tree with one trivalent vertex. In the latter case its three arm lengths are either $(1,1,h)$, with $h\ge1$, or $(1,2,h)$, with $h\in\{2,3,4\}$. Let $P$ consist of the marked vertices together with all trivalent vertices. Then \[ \#P\le2nc, \qquad \sum_{Q\in P}m_Q\le31nc. \tag{D.WC.2} \] Add a virtual endpoint of weight zero one edge beyond each unmarked terminal leaf. Decompose the graph into maximal segments whose endpoints belong to $P$ or are these virtual endpoints. The weights on each segment form an integral arithmetic progression. The sum of the lengths in edges of all nonconstant segments is at most $93nc$. There are at most $3nc$ constant segments, all with two endpoints in $P$ and the same positive weight at both ends. On replacing each constant segment by one edge, the number of remaining actual noncore vertices is at most $95nc$. Thus the only unrestricted graph data in this estimate are the lengths of at most $3nc$ constant-multiplicity rational $(-2)$-chains. The proposition does not assert a bound for those lengths, an object atlas, or a representation-count consequence.

statement: [Proved: a polynomial normal-layer presentation of actual bundles] Let $\mathcal Z_J$ be a nilpotent thickening of a proper one-dimensional tame stack $\mathcal Z_0$ over a field $k$. Suppose its ideal $I$ is locally principal, $I^{J+1}=0$, and $I^j/I^{j+1}$ is invertible on $\mathcal Z_0$ for $0\leq j\leq J$. Fix two cohomologically affine opens as above and reference bundles $K^\circ,A^\circ$ on $\mathcal Z_J$. Put $K_0=K^\circ|_{\mathcal Z_0}$ and $A_0=A^\circ|_{\mathcal Z_0}$. There is a polynomial family of marked bundles $K$ on $\mathcal Z_J$ with $K|_{\mathcal Z_0}=K_0$, using \[ h^1\bigl(\mathcal Z_0, \mathcal End(K_0)\otimes I^j/I^{j+1}\bigr) \tag{D.WF.1} \] variables of weight $j$ at every $1\leq j\leq J$. It covers every marked bundle over every $k$-algebra, up to isomorphism preserving the marking. This assertion is about actual bundles on the fixed thickening, not only their tangent spaces. Over this family there is a finite polynomial complex computing $R\Gamma\mathcal Hom(K,A^\circ)$ over every coefficient algebra. Its underlying graded vector spaces are the direct sum, over $0\leq j\leq J$, of \[ H^0\bigl(\mathcal Hom(K_0,A_0)\otimes I^j/I^{j+1}\bigr),\qquad H^1\bigl(\mathcal Hom(K_0,A_0)\otimes I^j/I^{j+1}\bigr). \tag{D.WF.2} \] A coordinate in the first space at level $j$ is assigned weight $\max(1,j)$. Its cycle equations have weighted degree at most $j+1$ at output level $j$. The resulting cycles parameterize \emph{actual global maps} $K\to A^\circ$. Restricting to the open locus where the residual map is a subbundle inclusion produces actual locally free cokernels over every coefficient algebra. For a fixed finite list of such quotient complexes $P=[K\to A^\circ]$, in internal degrees $-1,0$, their derived Hom complexes, equality-of-map witnesses, and bounded-length composition or inverse diagrams also admit finite polynomial presentations. Their vector-space sizes are bounded by the corresponding sums of $H^0,H^1$ of the four associated-graded termwise Hom bundles. If all term and arrow coordinates at layer $j$ have weight $\max(1,j)$, the weighted degrees are at most $J+c$, where $c$ depends only on the fixed diagram length. One-step absolute Frobenius increases this bound by a fixed factor depending on $p$, without assuming that Frobenius is flat on the coefficient algebra.

statement: [Proved: a Q-factorial extraction for a formally graded surface germ] Let $k$ be algebraically closed of characteristic $p>0$, and let $(A,\mathfrak m)$ be an excellent normal local $k$-algebra of dimension two with residue field $k$. Suppose that its completion is isomorphic, as a complete local $k$-algebra, to the completion at $R_+$ of a finitely generated normal positively graded domain \[ R=\bigoplus_{d\geq0}R_d,\qquad R_0=k,\qquad \dim R=2. \] There is a projective birational morphism $h:Y\to\operatorname{Spec}A$, an isomorphism on the punctured spectrum, with the following properties. The surface $Y$ is normal and locally Q-factorial, its exceptional locus has exactly one irreducible curve, and every finite cover of the punctured spectrum is tame at the valuation of that curve. The exceptional valuation, after completion at $\mathfrak m$, is the radial valuation of the grading.

statement: [Proved: polynomial background coefficients can be separated] Fix positive constants $A,K,h$ and an integer $a\geq1$. Let $m,s,f\geq1$, $r=ms$, $q=p^f$, and let $E$ be a positive integer with $E\leq K(ms)^h$. Consider a polynomial presentation with the following variables: \begin{itemize} \item at most $Afms$ background variables of weight one; \item at most $Afms^2$ variables at each weight $Ej$, $1\leq j\leq am$; \item at most $Afms^2$ further bundle variables of weight $E$. \end{itemize} Suppose every equation has weighted degree at most $KEm$, enlarging $K$ so that $K\geq a$. Then its number of irreducible components, and the number of nonempty clopen classes on any open part, is at most $q^{Cr^2}$, with $C$ depending only on $A,K,h,a,p$. In particular, this numerical bound permits polynomially growing degrees in a smaller block of background variables, provided the actual mixed polynomials satisfy the displayed weighted-degree condition. That condition is not implied by separate tangent-space dimensions.

statement: [Proved: the normal-layer product has a quadratic exponent] Fix positive constants $A,K$ and an integer $a\geq1$. Let $m,s,f$ be positive integers, put $r=ms$, and put $q=p^f$ for any fixed prime $p$. Suppose an affine polynomial presentation has at most $Afms^2$ variables at each weight $j\in\{1,\ldots,am\}$, and at most $Afms^2$ additional variables of weight at least one. Suppose the additional weights are at most $Km$, and every equation has weighted degree at most $Km$. Enlarging $K$ so that $K\geq a$, its number of irreducible components is at most \[ q^{C r^2}, \tag{D.WB.3} \] where $C$ depends only on $A,K,a,p$. The same conclusion holds for any open part and for a partition of it into nonempty clopen classes. This statement is conditional on an actual polynomial presentation with those weights. It does not construct a presentation of bundles, deformation torsors, or Frobenius objects from a bound on their tangent spaces.

It is a hypersurface and hence Cohen--Macaulay, and its only singular point is the vertex $[0:0:0:1]$, also in characteristic two. It is therefore normal and $S_2$. These assertions persist after extending $k$.

exact_statement: Let $A$ be the henselization at a prime of an algebra of finite type over a field or an excellent DVR, and let $X$ be proper over $A$. Artin's Theorem~3.5 \cite{Artin1969}, pp.~31--32, says that \[ \operatorname{Pic}(X)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Pic}(X_{\widehat A}) \] is injective with dense image for the topology of restriction to the closed fibre thickenings. If $X_{\widehat A}$ is projective, approximate an ample line bundle on it modulo the maximal ideal. The resulting line bundle on $X$ is ample on the closed fibre. Openness of relative ampleness makes it relatively ample on a neighbourhood of the closed point of $\operatorname{Spec}A$; that neighbourhood is the entire local spectrum. Thus $X/A$ is projective. This proves C1 under the stated approximation hypotheses in all characteristics.

exact_statement: For arbitrary elliptic schemes $E/S$ in characteristic $2$ and ordinary $Q/S$ with a chosen nonzero étale $2$-torsion section, the usual Igusa quotient $X=(E\times Q)/\langle(-1,+P)\rangle$ satisfies \[ \operatorname{Pic}^{\tau}_{X/S}=Y^\vee\times E^\vee[2]. \] It is flat, and the fibrewise Picard variety is $Y^\vee$, compatibly with base change. Both first Hodge numbers are $2$. The torsion Néron--Severi group is $\mathbb Z/2$ on an ordinary fibre of $E$ and zero on a supersingular fibre, since it is the component group of $E[2]$. In the family \eqref{dgj:elliptic-family}, torsion therefore disappears under specialization. This product family is not the full deformation family of the surface. A first-order nonflatness assertion is stated in accessible published literature, but the proof audit below identifies a gap, and D4o subsequently refutes the assertion by computing the full ordinary deformation. For the ordinary Igusa surface $X_0$ put $I=H^1(X_0,T_{X_0})^\vee$ and $R_1=k\oplus I$ with $I^2=0$, and take the first-order deformation whose Kodaira--Spencer class is the identity of $H^1(X_0,T_{X_0})$. Here $T_{X_0}=\mathcal O_{X_0}^{\oplus2}$ and $h^1(\mathcal O_{X_0})=2$, so $\dim_k I=4$. Chai--Oort, \S3.9(iv), printed p.~35 \cite{DGJ_ChaiOort2017}, states that $\operatorname{Pic}^{\tau}_{X_1/R_1}$ is not flat. The source identifies this assertion with Mumford's example. The surface deformation can be taken projective: the obstruction to lifting the square of an ample line bundle is twice its square-zero obstruction, hence zero in characteristic two, and ampleness over an Artinian base is detected on the special fibre.

statement: A flat mu2 torsor over a characteristic-two Artinian base has different absolute tangent dimension and tangent-map rank from the trivial torsor, disproving the inference used in Chai’s final argument.
exact_statement: The proof argues that the off-neutral component cannot be a flat torsor under the neutral component because their absolute tangent dimensions are five and six, respectively, and their tangent maps to the base have different ranks. That inference is false for torsors under a nonsmooth group. Here is a complete example with exactly those dimensions. Over an algebraically closed field $k$ of characteristic two put \[ R=k[e_1,e_2,e_3,e_4]/(e_i e_j:1\leq i,j\leq4), \qquad P=\operatorname{Spec}R[z]/(z^2-e_1). \] It is finite free of rank two over $R$, with basis $1,z$. The unit $1+z$ satisfies $(1+z)^2=1+e_1$; multiplication on this unit makes $P$ a $\mu_2$-torsor. Explicitly, with $y^2=0$ the coordinate of $\mu_2$, the torsor map is $z_1\mapsto z$, $z_2\mapsto z+y+zy$. On the two free rank-four coordinate modules over $R$ its determinant is $1+e_1$, a unit. This proves the torsor condition, including faithful flatness.

Indeed $(1+\epsilon)^2=1$ and the second row is $(1,1)$. This gives an actual smooth projective quotient deformation $X/R$ and a finite étale double cover $\pi:A\to X$. exact_statement: \textbf{Status: Proved.} Root and fhi independently audited the complete argument. This section treats the remaining case in D4o. All bases in the deformation calculation are local Artinian $W(k)$-algebras with residue field an algebraically closed field $k$ of characteristic two; all deformations and isomorphisms are marked on the closed fibre. Let $E_0$ be supersingular, let $F_0$ be ordinary, and choose $0\ne P\in F_0[2](k)$. exact_statement: There exists a smooth projective family of geometrically connected surfaces $X/R$, with $R=W(k)$ and $k$ an algebraically closed field of characteristic $2$, such that \[ \operatorname{Pic}^{\tau}_{X/R} \simeq\mu_{2,R}^{\,2}\times_R K, \qquad K=\operatorname{Spec}R\amalg\operatorname{Spec}k. \tag{E4.H.1} \] The second summand of $K$ has the group law inherited from the nonzero component of the constant group $(\mathbf Z/2)_R$; its product with itself lands in the identity summand. Consequently $\operatorname{Pic}^{\tau}_{X/R}$ is not open over $R$, even though $X/R$ is smooth. Over $A=R/4R$, its fibrewise neutral subgroup is represented by $\mu_{2,A}^{\,2}$ and is finite flat, whereas its tau-part is not flat. This refutes both the normal-family universal-openness question on 57:310(3) and the implication written on 57:311, even with represented neutral part.

exact_statement: The manuscript asks for ``existence du pr\'esch\'ema quotient'' $\underline{\mathrm{Pic}}_{X/S}/\underline{\mathrm{Pic}}^\tau_{X/S}$. In this generality the answer is negative, even when the tau-part is flat. Let \[ S=\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf R[[t]],\qquad X=V(x^2+y^2-tz^2)\subset\mathbf P^2_S . \tag{E4.Q.1} \] This is Mumford's example as proved in \cite[Example~4.14, pp.~31--33]{Kleiman2005}. Its Picard fppf sheaf $P$ is an algebraic space, not a scheme. After the finite \'etale base change $S'=\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf C[[t]]$, its component of total degree $n$ is obtained by gluing copies $S'_{a,b}$, $a+b=n$, along their generic point. Complex conjugation interchanges the origins $(a,b)$ and $(b,a)$. For $a\ne b$ these origins have no common affine neighborhood: their two trait sections agree generically, contrary to separatedness of such an affine neighborhood. If $P$ were a scheme, an affine neighborhood of their common descended point would pull back to just such an affine neighborhood.

exact_statement: Let $\mathcal P$ be the normalized Poincaré bundle on $A\times_S B$. For a relatively ample line bundle $L$ of class $\delta$, write \[ \Phi(L)=R\operatorname{pr}_{B*} (\mathcal P\otimes\operatorname{pr}_A^*L),\qquad F_\delta(L)=\det\Phi(L)^{-1},\qquad \chi=\chi(L). \] These are relative constructions. The complex is perfect; in the ample case it is a vector bundle of rank $\chi$. Tensoring $L$ by a bundle from $S$ changes its determinant by a bundle from $S$ only, so $F_\delta$ defines a morphism of relative Picard sheaves. The theorem of the square gives, up to bundles from the base, \[ (1,\lambda_L)^*\mathcal P =m^*L\otimes\operatorname{pr}_1^*L^{-1} \otimes\operatorname{pr}_2^*L^{-1}. \] Changing variables $(x,a)\mapsto(x+a,a)$ therefore gives $\lambda_L^*\Phi(L)=\pi_*L\otimes L^{-1}$ up to the same harmless base factors. Taking determinants shows $\lambda_L^*F_\delta(L)=L^\chi$ in the relative Picard sheaf. Consequently, if $\delta'$ is the class of $F_\delta(L)$, then \[ \lambda_\delta\lambda_{\delta'}=[\chi]_B, \qquad \lambda_{\delta'}\lambda_\delta=[\chi]_A. \] Indeed the formula for a pulled-back line bundle first gives $\lambda_\delta\lambda_{\delta'}\lambda_\delta =\chi\lambda_\delta$; the isogeny $\lambda_\delta$ is faithfully flat and can be cancelled on the right. Duality gives the other equality. Thus $\delta'$ is positive, whereas the determinant itself has class $\varphi(\delta)=-\delta'$. This proves precisely the negative sign in the box of 59:10.

exact_statement: Let $k$ be algebraically closed, of any characteristic. Let $j:Y\hookrightarrow X$ be a smooth hyperplane section of a smooth projective $n$-fold, and use the incidence abelian varieties of J1i. Fix $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}k$ and put $r=2i-1$. For a smooth projective $d$-fold $W$, write $L_W$ for cup product by the chosen hyperplane class. The convention for the Lefschetz lowering operator is \[ \Lambda_W(L_W^a v)= \begin{cases}L_W^{a-1}v,&a>0,\\0,&a=0,\end{cases} \qquad v\in H^b_{\rm prim}(W,\mathbb Q_\ell). \] Thus $\Lambda_W$ lowers degree by two and Tate twist by one; it has no extra $\mathfrak{sl}_2$ coefficient. Let $B(W)$ mean that this operator is induced by a rational algebraic correspondence in $\operatorname{CH}^{d-1}(W\times W)_{\mathbb Q}$. With this explicit convention the following implications hold: \begin{enumerate} \item If $2i\leq n-1$ and $B(X)$ holds, then $j^*:P^i_{\rm inc}(X)\to P^i_{\rm inc}(Y)$ is an isogeny. \item If $2i\geq n+1$ and $B(Y)$ holds, then the same homomorphism is surjective. \end{enumerate} Only the relevant degree of $\Lambda_X$, respectively $\Lambda_Y$, is needed. The cohomological inputs are Deligne's hard Lefschetz theorem \cite[Theorem 4.1.1, p.~217]{DGJ_Deligne1980} and weak Lefschetz \cite[(4.1.6), pp.~218--219]{DGJ_Deligne1980}. The coefficient-free lowering convention is also spelled out in \cite[Section 4.1, pp.~6--7]{DGJ_Peters2026}. No integral inverse, equality of incidence and universal regular equivalence, or middle-degree fixed-part assertion is part of this conclusion.

exact_statement: \label{A4:finite-descent-theorem} Keep the notation and hypotheses of Proposition~\ref{A4:finite-rank-equivalence}, and put \[ B^{(n)}=H^0(A'_n/A_n),\qquad B=H^0(A'/A). \] The equivalent conditions in that proposition are also equivalent to: for every $n$, $\operatorname{Spec}A'_n\to\operatorname{Spec}B^{(n)}$ is an effective descent morphism for all flat quasi-coherent modules. Under these conditions, \[ H^1(A'/A,\mathbf G_a)=0,\qquad H^1(A'/A,\mathrm{GL}_r)=\{1\}\quad(r\geq1), \] and $\operatorname{Spec}A'\to\operatorname{Spec}B$ is an effective descent morphism for finite flat modules. If $A$ is Artinian, then for every flat $B$-scheme $X$, the base change $X\times_B\operatorname{Spec}A'\to X$ is an effective descent morphism for all flat quasi-coherent modules. These are exactly parts (a), (b), and (c) of the theorem on scans 26--30; the proof uses vanishing, not the false canonical comparison. In particular, we distinguish three quantifiers. A single fixed finite rank $r\geq1$ suffices in the hypothesis, vanishing then holds in every finite rank, and the Artinian assertions (a) and (c) concern free modules of every cardinal rank. We assert no arbitrary-rank analogue of (b) over a non-Artinian semilocal base.

exact_statement: \label{A4:flatclosure} Let $A$ be Artinian, $Y=\operatorname{Spec}A$, $f:X\to Y$ any morphism of schemes, and $j:U\hookrightarrow X$ a retrocompact open immersion. Let $\mathcal F$ be a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module and let $\mathcal F|_U\twoheadrightarrow\mathcal G_U$ be a quasi-coherent quotient which is flat over $Y$. Suppose there is a morphism $Y'\to Y$ with $A\to\Gamma(Y',\mathcal O_{Y'})$ injective, and on $X'=X\times_Y Y'$ a quasi-coherent quotient $\mathcal F_{Y'}\twoheadrightarrow\mathcal G'$ such that $\mathcal G'|_{U'}=\mathcal G_{U'}$, $\mathcal G'$ is $Y'$-flat, and $\mathcal G'\to j'_*\mathcal G_{U'}$ is universally injective under base change on $Y'$. Then \[ \mathcal G=\operatorname{im}(\mathcal F\longrightarrow j_*\mathcal G_U) \] is $Y$-flat, its restriction map is universally injective under base change on $Y$, and its formation as this image commutes with every base change on $Y$. In particular $\mathcal G_{Y'}\simeq\mathcal G'$ as quotients of $\mathcal F_{Y'}$. It is the unique quotient having the required properties. If $\mathcal G'$ is of finite presentation, so is $\mathcal G$.

exact_statement: \label{A5:projectivity} Let $f:A\to S$ be an abelian scheme and let $S$ be normal and locally noetherian. There exists an $f$-ample invertible sheaf $L$ on $A$. In fact $A$ admits a polarization $\lambda:A\to A^\vee$, and one may take $L=(1,\lambda)^*\mathcal P$, where $\mathcal P$ is the normalized Poincar\'e bundle on $A\times_S A^\vee$. The sheaf $V=f_*(L^{\otimes3})$ is finite locally free, its formation commutes with base change, and evaluation gives a closed immersion \[ A\lhook\joinrel\longrightarrow\mathbf P_S(V). \] Here $\mathbf P_S(V)$ parametrizes invertible quotients of $V$. Thus the assertion on cote 131, scan 17, is correct in the relative ample-bundle, or projective-bundle, sense of projectivity.

exact_statement: \label{B:positive-closure} Let $\mathcal Q$ be the class of quasisyntomic $\mathbb F_p$-algebras. Rings locally admitting a $p$-basis, and excellent noetherian local complete intersection rings, belong to $\mathcal Q$. The class $\mathcal Q$ is stable under finite direct products, arbitrary filtered colimits, and \'etale localization and descent. Let $\mathcal P_F$ be the class of reduced $F$-finite PD-torsion-free $\mathbb F_p$-algebras, and let $\mathcal P_E$ be the class of reduced excellent noetherian PD-torsion-free $\mathbb F_p$-algebras. Each of these two classes is stable under finite direct products, adjoining finitely many polynomial variables, and \'etale localization. PD torsion freeness itself is stable under \'etale descent and arbitrary filtered colimits of characteristic-$p$ rings. Define the literal ring-class union and its \'etale local closure by \begin{align*} \mathcal U&=\mathcal Q\cup\mathcal P_F\cup\mathcal P_E,\\ \mathcal U_{\text{ét}} &=\{R:\operatorname{Spec}R\text{ has an \'etale cover by spectra of rings in }\mathcal U\}. \end{align*} The ordinary crystalline functor is fully faithful on $\mathcal U_{\text{ét}}$. This class is stable under finite direct products and \'etale localization and descent. Here a direct product means a product of rings; the corresponding finite schemes form a disjoint union, not a fibre product over $\mathbb F_p$.

exact_statement: \label{B:positive-crystals} The ordinary crystalline Dieudonn\'e functor is fully faithful in each of the following cases: \begin{enumerate} \item $S$ is locally the spectrum of a quasisyntomic $\mathbb F_p$-algebra; \item $S$ locally admits a $p$-basis, without a finiteness restriction on that basis or a noetherian hypothesis; \item $S$ is an excellent locally noetherian local complete intersection scheme; \item $S$ is reduced, $F$-finite, $F$-nilpotent, and PD torsion free. \end{enumerate} Here $F$-finite means that absolute Frobenius is finite; $F$-nilpotent means that its kernel ideal is locally nilpotent; PD torsion free means that the $p$-complete universal PD envelopes of affine presentations are $p$-torsion free. In (1), the essential image consists exactly of the crystals admitting the filtration \eqref{B:admissibility}; this filtration is unique and every crystal morphism preserves it. In (2) every object of $\operatorname{DC}(S)$ belongs to the essential image. In (4) the essential image is again exactly the crystals admitting \eqref{B:admissibility}. The same essential-image assertion holds for $F$-finite local complete intersections.
