Theorem~\ref{C:all_algebraic_fields_WG} gives the full answer over every algebraic extension of a finite field: finite Frobenius orbits, Schur index one, integer coordinates and a possible determinant bit. Its finite operation procedures state the precise subfield-degree access. Theorem~\ref{C:artinian_effective_imperfect_C1} gives complete recursive indices and all operations over every finite-dimensional algebra over an effective countable $C_1$ field, including imperfect fields when factorization over finite towers is supplied. Projectivity is decided by a linear splitting test, and the dual throughout is $\operatorname{Hom}_R(-,R)$. The stated arithmetic access is not deduced from the abstract $C_1$ property. Theorem~\ref{C:function-field-WG} removes the factorization hypothesis for every explicitly presented finite tower over $\overline{\mathbb F}_p(t)$: the preceding three lemmas prove the needed ordinary terminating algorithms, including inseparable extensions. For every perfect field and every finite-dimensional coefficient algebra over it, Theorems~\ref{C:perfect_Galois_indices} and \ref{C:artinian_perfect_Galois_indices} classify all indecomposables by finite geometric Galois orbits, with explicit Schur-index data. Corollary~\ref{C:perfect-residue-Artin-reduction} includes every Artin ring of prime characteristic with perfect residue fields. Their residual hermitian groups now have explicit scalar presentations and finite operation-extraction formulas in Theorem~\ref{C:hermitian_scalar_presentation} and Corollary~\ref{C:WG_hermitian_scalar_operations}. The separate division-index and primitive-idempotent arithmetic remains explicitly supplied input; an arbitrary-field word-problem algorithm is not asserted. Theorems~\ref{C:complete-finite-canonical}--\ref{C:complete-finite-products} give exact coordinates for all complete Noetherian local rings with finite odd residue field and arbitrary products of such rings. Their image in the solved finite-ring coordinates is characterized by one uniform bound on the ranks and coefficient degrees of representing pairs of forms. The fixed finite-coordinate tests terminate; the theorem does not assert a finite test for the unbounded quantifiers. Theorem~\ref{C:profinite-WG} removes both locality and Noetherianity: it gives the exact bounded finite-coordinate answer for every profinite commutative ring with two invertible. The rank bound is replaced by a uniform size for an ambient projective idempotent matrix. Directed-system compactness proves the image and injectivity without assuming cancellation over the limiting ring. Theorems~\ref{C:complete_algclosed_indices} and \ref{C:complete_algclosed_WG} settle complete Noetherian local algebras with a specified countable algebraically closed odd-characteristic coefficient field and effective finite quotient tables. Their canonical indices are compatible infinite arrays, and their integer operation coefficients are object-dependent eventual constants. Proposition~\ref{C:complete_unbounded_detection} proves that no fixed rank-and-degree truncation cutoff can replace this qualification, and that coefficient streams alone do not decide equality. Theorems~\ref{C:finite-field-henselization-WG} and \ref{C:arithmetic-henselization-WG} give ordinary terminating classification and operation algorithms for every henselization of a finitely presented integer algebra at a supplied finite odd-residue point. This includes singular, nonreduced and mixed-characteristic local rings, without a factorization or stabilization oracle. Theorem~\ref{C:arithmetic-strict-henselization-WG} supplies the full ordinary answer for their strict henselizations as well, with a specified computable algebraic closure of the finite residue field. Theorem~\ref{C:effective-henselian-flat-unions} removes Noetherianity for computable flat local unions with unchanged residue field. Corollary~\ref{C:infinite-variable-henselian-WG} includes the henselizations and strict henselizations of local polynomial rings in countably many variables over finite fields and over the integers at a finite odd-residue point; these have infinite Krull dimension. Theorem~\ref{C:henselian-products-WG} gives the exact answer for arbitrary products of these solved local factors. Its image is specified by the three explicit minimal positive-rank, negative-rank and coefficient-degree bounds of Proposition~\ref{C:henselian-minimal-form-bounds}. Theorems~\ref{C:C1-henselization-WG} and \ref{C:function-field-henselization-WG} extend the ordinary answer to the stated effective, possibly imperfect, $C_1$ residue fields and all explicitly supplied finite towers over $\overline{\mathbf F}_p(t)$. Theorem~\ref{C:effective-coherent-henselization-WG} uses finite matrix kernels instead of Noetherianity. Its lexicographic valuation examples have nonzero infinitely divisible elements and cannot be flat local unions of Noetherian local stages, so they remove a further family. Theorem~\ref{C:C1-coherent-products-WG} gives exact bounded product coordinates with the full square-class coordinate at symmetric factors. Theorems~\ref{C:global-function-field-arithmetic}-- \ref{C:global-function-hermitian-isometry} now compute factorization, all places, actual division algebras, reduced norms, and every hermitian isometry problem over explicit global function fields of odd characteristic, including inseparable towers and wild division degree. The quaternion skew-hermitian argument retains the rank-one norm obstruction, rather than invoking false local-global isometry. Theorems~\ref{C:global-function-coefficient-WG} and \ref{C:global-function-henselization-WG} consequently give complete ordinary canonical representation and form coordinates, equality, tensor products and exterior operations over every finite-dimensional coefficient algebra over those fields, all stated effective local henselizations, and effective valuation henselizations. No division-index or hermitian-isometry oracle remains in this family. Theorems~\ref{C:henselian-global-field-arithmetic} and \ref{C:henselian-global-coefficient-WG} further give complete ordinary answers over all supplied finite extensions of henselized global-place fraction fields, their finite coefficient algebras and the stated effective local henselizations. The projective-point and regular-completion arguments decide every required division index and hermitian isometry. Corollary~\ref{C:henselian-global-new-families} explicitly separates these non-$C_1$, nonglobal positive-characteristic fields from the earlier completed families. Theorems~\ref{C:separably-closed-effective-arithmetic} and \ref{C:separably-closed-coefficient-WG} remove the explicit finite-imperfection separably closed fields and their stated coefficient algebras and coherent local henselizations. Computable $p$-components and Haran's quantifier elimination give actual arithmetic; the computed division fields may be purely inseparable, and the form blocks have free integer coordinates. For imperfection degree at least two, the anisotropic quasilinear form proves these fields are not $C_1$. Theorems~\ref{C:infinite-residue-henselian-arithmetic} and \ref{C:infinite-residue-henselian-WG} further settle all finite towers over the explicit one-variable henselian fields with these infinite residue fields. A certified whole residue-field table and an actual integral basis give each finite quotient; Haran and Lemma~\ref{C:Greenberg-congruence-decisions} decide the required congruence, division-index and hermitian-isometry questions. Corollary~\ref{C:infinite-residue-new-families} proves their separation from the earlier global and finite-residue families. No unproved iteration over these new henselian residue fields is asserted. Thus the remaining task concerns coefficient bases outside the completed families and residual division-index arithmetic or word-problem access not supplied by the stated effective hypotheses. This is not made into a uniform ordinary equality algorithm by a formal matrix presentation: Theorem~\ref{C:locally-finite-equality-obstruction} proves such an algorithm impossible from arbitrary computable field arithmetic alone. The special-$\lambda$ criterion remains complete over every affine base with two invertible; low ranks and all rational algebras were already determined. The infinite generation in Proposition~\ref{C:BO3_not_finitely_generated} is compatible with all these infinite canonical index sets.

No effective bound for the required congruence precision is assumed or claimed.

statement: Equation (C.1.1) is an exact obstruction reduction, not a claim to have classified every commutative ring; The results above classify all $\mathbb Q$-algebras and all regular coherent rings, exclude every positive-characteristic ring, and establish stability under filtered colimits; Theorem~\ref{C:regular-coherent-criterion} removes the Noetherian and finite-dimensional hypotheses, and Corollary~\ref{C:valuation-domain-criterion} covers all valuation domains of arbitrary rank and value group; Theorem~\ref{C:coherent-regular-modular-locus} further allows every characteristic-zero singularity [full statement in exact_statement_tex].
exact_statement: \label{C:allrings_open}\label{C:allrings_gate} Equation (C.1.1) is an exact obstruction reduction, not a claim to have classified every commutative ring. The results above classify all $\mathbb Q$-algebras and all regular coherent rings, exclude every positive-characteristic ring, and establish stability under filtered colimits. Theorem~\ref{C:regular-coherent-criterion} removes the Noetherian and finite-dimensional hypotheses, and Corollary~\ref{C:valuation-domain-criterion} covers all valuation domains of arbitrary rank and value group. Theorem~\ref{C:coherent-regular-modular-locus} further allows every characteristic-zero singularity in a coherent ring and requires local regular coherence only on the positive-characteristic locus. They also disprove the proposed criteria of locality, $K_0(k)=\mathbb Z$, connected regular rational fibre, and even $K_0(k[1/N])=\mathbb Z$ for every integer $N$, in the stated examples. Theorem~\ref{C:normal_trivialK0_kernel} further shows that normality together with trivial integer-localized $K_0$ does not eliminate the left obstruction: its two-dimensional normal local domain has a regular principal generic ring and an explicitly detected nonzero kernel. Theorem~\ref{C:dyadic_normal_node_criterion} also gives the exact answer for every local polynomial or formal node $xy=2^n u$ over a DVR with maximal ideal $(2)$: the full polynomial map is an isomorphism exactly when $n=1$, equivalently when the ring is regular. What remains is to calculate both groups in (C.1.1) for arbitrary mixed-characteristic rings outside this coherent modular-locus criterion and the further explicit families below. Proposition~\ref{C:noncoherent-positive-boundary} gives a normal local, noncoherent, nonvaluation positive example. Thus regular coherence is not necessary in the full arbitrary-ring problem; this example is already obtained by the filtered-colimit theorem. Theorem~\ref{C:shallow-full-support-three-torsion} bounds the remaining mixed shallow classes by three, but does not prove their vanishing or the existence of a nonzero class. Proposition~\ref{C:ramified-A2-MF-cancellation} proves cancellation of the specified standard matrix-factorization lattice on every ramified exponent-three dyadic node. It does not decide the full comparison map. Proposition~\ref{C:odd-node-MCM-comparison-boundary} shows that the whole generic Swan kernel is invisible to the ordinary MCM Grothendieck group on odd-exponent dyadic nodes. The true category retained by Swan lattices is the relative matrix-factorization category of Lemma~\ref{C:relative-Swan-MF-bridge}; its required Grothendieck group has not been calculated. Neither comparison settles polynomiality. Proposition~\ref{C:flat_nilpotent_kernel} now settles the previously undecided flat dual-number ring over $\mathbb Z_{(2)}$ negatively, and proves that even flatness does not remove the generic kernel. Theorem~\ref{C:dualnumber_C2_ring} calculates that entire degree-two kernel over any characteristic-zero DVR with maximal ideal $(2)$: there is one independent order-two class for each nonzero irreducible polynomial over the residue field, and their internal tensor products are zero. This resolves this family completely in degree two but does not supply the missing criterion for arbitrary singular bases. Proposition~\ref{C:divisible_nil_invariance} removes nil ideals that are uniquely divisible by all integers, without any noetherian hypothesis, and gives nonreduced mixed-characteristic positive examples. The remaining gap concerns integral nil directions as well as reduced singular bases; unrestricted nilpotent invariance and generic-fibre injectivity are both false. Proposition~\ref{C:reduced_regular_fibres} also excludes a criterion using regularity of the arithmetic fibres alone: the reduced local ring $\mathbb Z_{(2)}[x]_{(2,x)}/(2x)$ has regular generic and special fibres but an infinite degree-two comparison kernel. Regularity of the total ring along the positive-characteristic locus in Theorem~\ref{C:regular_modular_locus} must not be confused with this weaker fibrewise condition. Theorems~\ref{C:squarezero_intrinsic_criterion} and~\ref{C:ramified_squarezero_criterion} give an intrinsic necessary-and-sufficient answer for every square-zero extension $A\ltimes J$ of a characteristic-zero DVR with residue characteristic two, including arbitrary ramification: multiplication by $2$ on $J$ must be bijective. This covers arbitrary modules $J$ and every square-zero thickening of $\mathbb Z_{(2)}$. It removes that whole class from the open gate; higher nilpotent thickenings and general reduced singular mixed-characteristic rings are not classified by it. Proposition~\ref{C:derived_fibre_twins} further shows that the complete family of derived prime fibres, the rational fibre, and all integer-localized $K_0$ groups together are insufficient: the two local orders displayed there have identical such data and opposite answers. A general criterion must retain additional information about the total ring or its arithmetic thickenings. Theorem~\ref{C:allprime_squarezero_criterion} removes the whole square-zero class over every unramified mixed-characteristic DVR: for every prime $p$ and every module $J$, the condition is that $p:J\to J$ be bijective, and every failure is detected in degree $p$. Proposition~\ref{C:odd_torsion_allheights} includes torsion of every finite height and $p$-divisible torsion; its proof detects the same fixed class at every finite stage by a primary curvature-length invariant over $A/p^m$. Theorem~\ref{C:ramified_torsion_infinite} further excludes every ramified square-zero module containing torsion of the full ramification height, at every prime, and proves that its explicit induced class has infinite order even modulo the polynomial image. This strengthens every unramified torsion witness to infinite order. In contrast, Proposition~\ref{C:cyclotomic_torsion_cancellation} proves that the rank-one witness cancels after induction when the base contains a primitive odd-prime root of unity and the ideal is killed by that root minus one. Proposition~\ref{C:cyclotomic_matrix_cancellation} extends this cancellation to every infinitesimal deformation of a direct sum of constant cyclotomic characters. It does not prove polynomiality in that remaining case. Theorem~\ref{C:cyclotomic_flat_criterion} uses a nonsplit integral lattice to settle every flat module over a DVR with $\zeta_p-1$ a uniformizer: again $pJ=J$ is necessary and sufficient. Thus the square-zero DVR gate is now the ramified odd-prime directions not excluded by the stated tests, including this cyclotomic residue-torsion case. Higher nilpotent thickenings and arbitrary reduced singular bases remain outside these classification theorems.

For an orthogonal generator of alternating type divide that multiplicity by $2$; for a symmetric or paired generator take it unchanged. exact_statement: \label{C:distinguished_ring} The following give the complete additive and multiplicative description of the Grothendieck ring $\mathcal D$ of distinguished functors modulo the manuscript's eventual equivalences. \begin{enumerate} \item Each distinguished functor is uniquely of the form $\mathcal F_X$ up to isomorphism of finite species. An eventually bijective natural transformation between distinguished functors is bijective at every finite set. Even if zigzags through arbitrary functors are allowed, eventual equivalence identifies no two nonisomorphic distinguished functors. \item As an abelian group, \[ \mathcal D=\bigoplus_{n\geq0}B(\mathfrak S_n) =\bigoplus_{n\geq0}\ \bigoplus_{[H]\subseteq\mathfrak S_n}\mathbb Z\,[\operatorname{Inj}([n],-)/H], \] where $[H]$ runs through conjugacy classes of subgroups. \item Pointwise product is the union-of-supports product \[ (X\star Y)[I]=\coprod_{A,B\subseteq I,\ A\cup B=I}X[A]\times Y[B]. \] In particular this is not the usual species product that requires $A\cap B=\varnothing$. The unit is the constant singleton functor. \item Composition on effective functors is given explicitly by taking, among the elements of $\mathcal F_X(\mathcal F_Y(I))$, those for which the union of the supports in $I$ of all selected $Y$-structures is $I$. This gives a finite species of degree at most $\deg(X)\deg(Y)$. Composition extends uniquely to virtual classes, additively in its outer argument and polynomially in its inner argument, and remains associative. Its unit is $E\mapsto E$, not the constant singleton. \end{enumerate}

exact_statement: \label{C:field_WG_structure} Let $k$ be a field with $2\in k^\times$ and $G$ an affine group scheme. For every self-dual indecomposable finite-dimensional representation $U$, choose an invariant nondegenerate $\varepsilon_U$-symmetric form $q_U$, where $\varepsilon_U\in\{1,-1\}$. Such a choice always exists. Put \[ E_U=\operatorname{End}_G(U),\qquad D_U=E_U/\operatorname{rad}(E_U), \] and let $\sigma_U$ be the involution on the division algebra $D_U$ induced by the $q_U$-adjoint involution. The result is independent of the lifts. This applies in particular to $G=O_m$ over every such field. The radical quotient of the representation category need not be a tensor quotient: tensor products in this rule are taken before reduction.

statement: Let $V$ be a countable valuation domain with exact finite names and decidable arithmetic and equality, decidable divisibility and computable division whenever one element divides another; Suppose its residue map and field have the effective data required in Theorem~\ref{C:effective-coherent-henselization-WG}; Then that theorem gives complete ordinary canonical classification, equality and all split $WG$ operations over $V^h$; Here are actual uniform families supplying all this access; For $r\geq2$, take either \[ \begin{array}{ll} K=\mathbf F_q(x_1,\ldots,x_r), &v(K^\times)=\mathbf Z^r_{\rm [full statement in exact_statement_tex].
exact_statement: \label{C:lexicographic-valuation-henselization-WG} Let $V$ be a countable valuation domain with exact finite names and decidable arithmetic and equality, decidable divisibility and computable division whenever one element divides another. Suppose its residue map and field have the effective data required in Theorem~\ref{C:effective-coherent-henselization-WG}. Then that theorem gives complete ordinary canonical classification, equality and all split $WG$ operations over $V^h$. Here are actual uniform families supplying all this access. For $r\geq2$, take either \[ \begin{array}{ll} K=\mathbf F_q(x_1,\ldots,x_r), &v(K^\times)=\mathbf Z^r_{\rm lex},\quad v(x_i)=e_i,\\ K=\mathbf Q(x_1,\ldots,x_{r-1}), &v(K^\times)=\mathbf Z^r_{\rm lex},\quad v(x_i)=e_i,\quad v(p)=e_r, \end{array} \tag{C.3.NH4} \] where $q$ is an odd prime power and $p$ an odd prime. In the first line the valuation of a polynomial is its least exponent vector in lexicographic order. In the second line it is the least exponent vector in the variables, followed by the $p$-adic valuation of that term's nonzero rational coefficient. Extend to rational functions by subtraction, and put $V=\{0\}\cup\{f\in K^\times:v(f)\geq0\}$. These $V^h$ are countably infinite non-Noetherian henselian local domains, with residue field $\mathbf F_q$ or $\mathbf F_p$, respectively. Their maximal ideals are generated by $y=x_r$ in the first family and $y=p$ in the second, yet \[ 0\ne x_1\in\bigcap_{n\geq0} y^nV^h. \tag{C.3.NH5} \] They are therefore not separated for their maximal-ideal-adic topology, and cannot be filtered colimits of Noetherian local rings along flat local transition maps. In particular these complete ordinary answers are outside the earlier flat-Noetherian-stage families.

exact_statement: \label{C:locally-finite-equality-obstruction} There is no uniform ordinary algorithm which, from a computable presentation of a locally finite field of odd characteristic with exact arithmetic and equality, decides all equalities in $WG_{\mathrm{sp}}(BO_m/K)$, for any fixed $m\geq0$. This failure already occurs for the two trivial-action forms $\langle1\rangle$ and $\langle2\rangle$ over uniformly computable locally finite fields of characteristic $3$. More precisely, a computable increasing tower of finite fields can be constructed uniformly from a Turing machine $e$, such that the difference $\delta_e=[\langle2\rangle]-[\langle1\rangle]$ is zero in the union if and only if $e$ halts on its fixed input. The claim is a uniform obstruction across presentations. It does not assert that the equality problem is undecidable for every one of these individual fields. A root-decision or splitting oracle supplies additional information and is not ruled out by this statement.

exact_statement: \label{C:noncoherent-positive-boundary} Let $A$ be any mixed-characteristic discrete valuation ring, with uniformizer $\pi$, residue field $\kappa$ of characteristic $p>0$, and fraction field $K$. Let $x,y$ be algebraically independent over $K$. In $K(x,y)$ put \[ P_n=\pi/x^n,\qquad Y_n=y/x^n,\qquad R_n=A[x,P_n,Y_n]_{(x,P_n,Y_n)}\quad(n\geq0), \qquad S=\bigcup_{n\geq0}R_n. \tag{C.1.NC1} \] Here $P_0=\pi$, so $R_0=A[x,y]_{(\pi,x,y)}$. Then $S$ is a characteristic-zero normal local domain with maximal ideal $xS$, residue field $\kappa$, and $K_0(S)=\mathbb Z$. The map $\vartheta_S$ is an isomorphism in every degree, although $S$ is not coherent and is not a valuation domain. In particular its localization at its positive-residue-characteristic closed point is not regular coherent. Thus regular coherence at all positive-residue-characteristic points cannot be a necessary condition for the intrinsic all-ring C.1 criterion. This statement does not decide necessity of modular regularity within the class of coherent rings. Its positive comparison assertion is an application of the already proved filtered-colimit theorem, not a new family beyond that theorem.

statement: Let $(R,\mathfrak m)$ be any henselian local ring with $2\in R^\times$; Let $E$ be an associative unital algebra finite as an $R$-module, with central $R$-action, and put $J=\operatorname{rad}E$; Then $E$ is semiperfect and idempotents lift through every two-sided ideal contained in $J$; For an $R$-linear involution $*$ and a self-adjoint $a$ with $a-1\in J$, there exists a self-adjoint $b\equiv1\pmod J$ with $b^2=a$; Consequently nonsingular hermitian forms of either sign on a fixed finite projective $E$-module are classified up to isometry by reduction modulo $J$; The same semisimple-block [full statement in exact_statement_tex].
exact_statement: \label{C:nonnoetherian-henselian-lifting} Let $(R,\mathfrak m)$ be any henselian local ring with $2\in R^\times$. Let $E$ be an associative unital algebra finite as an $R$-module, with central $R$-action, and put $J=\operatorname{rad}E$. Then $E$ is semiperfect and idempotents lift through every two-sided ideal contained in $J$. For an $R$-linear involution $*$ and a self-adjoint $a$ with $a-1\in J$, there exists a self-adjoint $b\equiv1\pmod J$ with $b^2=a$. Consequently nonsingular hermitian forms of either sign on a fixed finite projective $E$-module are classified up to isometry by reduction modulo $J$. The same semisimple-block form classification applies to any category of finite free rational representations whose actual endomorphism rings are finite over $R$.

exact_statement: \label{C:odd-node-MCM-comparison-boundary} Let $A$ be a characteristic-zero DVR with uniformizer $\pi$, residue field $\kappa$ of characteristic two, and $2=v\pi^e$, where $v\in A^\times$ and $e\geq1$. Let $u\in A^\times$, $n\geq1$, and take either \[ R=\bigl(A[x,y]/(xy-u\pi^n)\bigr)_{(\pi,x,y)} \quad\text{or}\quad R=A[[x,y]]/(xy-u\pi^n). \] Put $B=R[C_2]$ and \[ K=\ker\bigl(R_R(C_2)\longrightarrow R_{R[1/2]}(C_2)\bigr), \qquad c:R_R(C_2)\longrightarrow G_0(B), \tag{C.1.MB1} \] where $c$ is induced by inclusion into all finitely generated $B$-modules. Then: \begin{enumerate} \item The entire group $\ker(G_0(B)\to G_0(B[1/\pi]))$ is cyclic of exponent dividing $n$. Tensoring with the sign representation acts as the identity on this group. \item The subgroup $c(K)$ is killed by both $2$ and $n$. In particular, if $n$ is odd then $c(K)=0$. \item If $\mathcal M$ is the exact category of finitely generated $B$-modules that are maximal Cohen--Macaulay over $R$, then $K_0(\mathcal M)\simeq G_0(B)$ under inclusion. Consequently the inclusion from $R$-free $C_2$-lattices to $\mathcal M$ also kills $K$ when $n$ is odd. \end{enumerate} The latter inclusion need not be injective even for these reduced normal domains: it is not injective on every unramified node with odd $n\geq3$, by Theorem~\ref{C:dyadic_normal_node_criterion}. This is a boundary of the ordinary MCM comparison; it does not assert that $K=0$ on any unresolved ramified node.

exact_statement: \label{C:perfect_Galois_indices} For every perfect $k$ as above, $\mathscr O_k$ is in bijection with the indecomposable finite-dimensional rational $O_{m,k}$-modules. Write $M_\Omega$ for the module attached to the orbit $\Omega$. There is a positive integer $s_\Omega$ such that \[ (M_\Omega)_{\bar k} \simeq\bigoplus_{i\in\Omega}U_i^{\oplus s_\Omega}. \tag{C.3.G1} \] The integer is the degree of the residue division algebra $D_\Omega=\operatorname{End}(M_\Omega)/\operatorname{rad}$ over its center $K_\Omega$: \[ [K_\Omega:k]=|\Omega|,\qquad s_\Omega^2=\dim_{K_\Omega}D_\Omega. \tag{C.3.G2} \] All this data can be obtained from one explicitly constructed finite-dimensional endomorphism algebra over $k$: choose a finite Galois extension $L/k$ defining one $U_i$, form the restriction of scalars $W=\operatorname{Res}_{L/k}U_i$, and compute $E=\operatorname{End}_{O_{m,k}}(W)$ by linear equations. Then $E/\operatorname{rad}E\simeq M_r(D_\Omega)$ for some $r$, and the image on $W$ of any lifted primitive idempotent of this simple algebra is $M_\Omega$. Different choices give isomorphic modules and the same index and division-algebra isomorphism class. The least coefficient degree is constant on $\Omega$ and is also the least coefficient degree of $M_\Omega$.

exact_statement: \label{C:profinite-WG} Let \[ R=\varprojlim_{\alpha\in\Lambda} R_\alpha \] be a directed inverse limit of finite commutative rings with $2$ invertible and surjective transition maps. Thus $R$ is an arbitrary profinite commutative ring with $2$ invertible, in a chosen finite quotient presentation. Put $G_\alpha=WG_{\rm sp}(BO_{m,R_\alpha})$, in the explicit canonical coordinates of Theorem~\ref{C:Om-finite-base-algorithm}. There is an injective homomorphism preserving all exterior operations, \[ WG_{\rm sp}(BO_{m,R})\longrightarrow \varprojlim_\alpha G_\alpha. \tag{C.3.PF4} \] Its image is exactly the set of compatible canonical coordinate families $(\xi_\alpha)$ satisfying \[ \begin{split} \exists B,D\ \forall\alpha:\quad \xi_\alpha\text{ is the difference of the classes}\\ \text{of two records (C.3.PF1)--(C.3.PF2) over }R_\alpha\text{ of the same bounds }B,D . \end{split} \tag{C.3.PF5} \] For fixed $B,D,\alpha$, this is a finite decidable test. Hence (C.3.PF4)--(C.3.PF5) give the entire split ring as a literal bounded subset of compatible explicitly solved finite-coordinate groups, without an unclassified isomorphism quotient. No ordinary finite decision procedure for equality of arbitrary infinite families is asserted. This includes genuinely non-Noetherian local profinite rings, for example \[ R=\mathbf F_p\ltimes\prod_{j\geq1}\mathbf F_p\epsilon_j, \qquad \left(\prod_{j\geq1}\mathbf F_p\epsilon_j\right)^2=0, \qquad p>2, \tag{C.3.PF6} \] with the topology of truncation in the $\epsilon_j$.

exact_statement: \label{C:profinite-projective-data} Fix $B,D\geq0$ and a commutative ring $A$ with $2$ invertible. A nonsingular symmetric rational $O_{m,A}$-representation on an idempotent summand of $A^B$, with coefficient bound $D$, has a finite polynomial record \[ (e,\rho,q,q^\sharp), \tag{C.3.PF1} \] where $e,q,q^\sharp$ are $B$-square matrices over $A$ and $\rho$ is a $B$-square matrix with entries in $C_D(A)$. Its exact defining equations are \[ \begin{gathered} e^2=e,\qquad \rho=e\rho e,\qquad \varepsilon(\rho)=e,\qquad \Delta(\rho_{ij})=\sum_k\rho_{ik}\otimes\rho_{kj},\\ q=e^tqe,\qquad q^t=q,\qquad q^\sharp=e q^\sharp e^t,\qquad q^\sharp q=e,\qquad qq^\sharp=e^t,\qquad \rho^t q\rho=q . \end{gathered} \tag{C.3.PF2} \] The final identity is in $C_{2D}(A)$, with its right side multiplied by the unit function. There are equivalences of triangulated categories \[ \underline{\mathcal E} \simeq \ker\bigl(D_{\rm sg}(B)\longrightarrow D_{\rm sg}(R)\bigr) \simeq D_{\rm sg}^{\rm rel}(Q\twoheadrightarrow B) \simeq [\operatorname{MF}(Q,q)]. \tag{C.1.RM1} \] The kernel in (C.1.RM1) is the full subcategory of objects whose restriction to $R$ is zero in $D_{\rm sg}(R)$. statement: Let $\lambda:J\xrightarrow{\sim}J^\vee$ be the principal polarization; The map \[ \mu=q\lambda^{-1}q^\vee:(J')^\vee\longrightarrow J' \] is the induced polarization on the dual quotient; Its inverse $\lambda'_{\mathbf Q}=\mu^{-1}$ is a positive rational polarization $J'\to(J')^\vee$; The form $Q$ in Theorem~\ref{D:height} is its height pairing; To check this, restrict $q$ to the $\lambda$-orthogonal complement of $B$; it is an isogeny, and the pullback of $\lambda'_{\mathbf Q}$ is the restriction of $\lambda$; Functoriality of canonical heights and the zero height of the trace give exactly [full statement in exact_statement_tex].
exact_statement: \label{D:quotient-polarization} Let $\lambda:J\xrightarrow{\sim}J^\vee$ be the principal polarization. The map \[ \mu=q\lambda^{-1}q^\vee:(J')^\vee\longrightarrow J' \] is the induced polarization on the dual quotient. Its inverse $\lambda'_{\mathbf Q}=\mu^{-1}$ is a positive rational polarization $J'\to(J')^\vee$. The form $Q$ in Theorem~\ref{D:height} is its height pairing. To check this, restrict $q$ to the $\lambda$-orthogonal complement of $B$; it is an isogeny, and the pullback of $\lambda'_{\mathbf Q}$ is the restriction of $\lambda$. Functoriality of canonical heights and the zero height of the trace give exactly the transported form. An integral polarization $N\lambda'_{\mathbf Q}$ gives $NQ$. Consequently the manuscript's phrase ``canonical polarization inherited from $J$'' needs this rational normalization: an unspecified integral choice cannot justify an equality with coefficient one. There is a separate factor of two if one calls $\widehat h_\Theta$ itself the bilinear height.

statement: Generator invariance, flat ascent, fpqc descent, and composition of Koszul-regular immersions.
exact_statement: Suppose $I\subset R$ is generated by a Koszul-regular sequence of length $r$. \begin{enumerate} \item Every other length-$r$ generating sequence of $I$ is Koszul-regular. In particular the property is invariant under permutation. \item For a flat map $R\to R'$, Koszul regularity ascends to $R'$. For a faithfully flat map it also descends. The same assertions hold with arbitrary module coefficients $M$ and $M\otimes_R R'$. \item The property that an ideal is locally generated by a finite Koszul-regular sequence, and the corresponding property of an immersion of schemes, descend for fpqc coverings. \item If $f$ is Koszul-regular in $R$ and the images of $g=(g_1,\ldots,g_s)$ are Koszul-regular in $R/I$, then $(f,g)$ is Koszul-regular in $R$. Thus compositions of Koszul-regular immersions are Koszul-regular. For $J=(f,g)$ their conormal sequence $0\to I/IJ\to J/J^2\to J/(I+J^2)\to0$ is split exact locally. \end{enumerate} These statements agree with \cite[VII, 1.4.2--1.5 and Proposition 1.7(i), pp.~419--423]{algSGA6}.

statement: Exact Noetherian local scope and the homology-finiteness replacement for Nakayama.
exact_statement: For finite modules over Noetherian local rings and sequences in the maximal ideal, ordinary, Koszul, and quasi-regularity are equivalent (Stacks Project, Lemma 15.31.7, tag \texttt{062D}; opened). \cite[Lemma 15.31.7]{algStacksKoszul} The word ``local'' cannot be dropped for sequences: in the Noetherian ring $k[x,y]\times k[x,y]$ the sequence $((x,1),(y,0))$ is regular, whereas the reversed sequence begins with a zerodivisor. Its final quotient is $k$. The failure in Example~\ref{SA23-C-5} is the failure of Nakayama for an infinitely generated homology module: $xM=M\ne0$. For a sequence in the maximal ideal of a local ring $R$, if the positive Koszul homology modules of every prefix are finite, acyclicity of the full sequence does imply ordinary $R$-regularity. Indeed, the cone long exact sequence shows that multiplication by the last element is surjective on the positive homology of the preceding complex; Nakayama kills it. Repeating this argument reduces to a one-element complex. This gives a valid finiteness replacement for the false unrestricted converse. The Noetherian case satisfies that replacement. SGA 6 VII, Proposition 1.7(iii), explicitly retains a Noetherian hypothesis for precisely this converse; Proposition 1.7(i)--(ii) records the two unrestricted transitivities proved above. \cite[Expos\'e VII, Proposition 1.7, p.~422]{algSGA6} For comparison, a different local nonpermutation example is \cite[Example 10.68.3]{algStacksNonpermutation}; the scheme-theoretic transitivities are also stated in \cite{algStacksImmersions}.

statement: Deligne Sym-Tor characterization of regular ideals over a Noetherian ring.
exact_statement: Let $R$ be Noetherian and $I\subset R$ an ideal. statement: Sharp-cardinal closure equivalence and failure without it.
exact_statement: For infinite regular cardinals $\kappa<\lambda$, the following are equivalent: \begin{enumerate} \item For every set $X$ of size less than $\lambda$, the poset $[X]^{<\kappa}$ has a cofinal subset of size less than $\lambda$. \item In every $\kappa$-directed poset, every subset of size less than $\lambda$ is contained in a $\kappa$-directed subset of size less than $\lambda$. \end{enumerate} This condition is often written $\kappa\mathrel{\triangleleft}\lambda$. statement: Relative cocycle groupoid classifies sections extending fixed alpha0.
exact_statement: Fix a subgroup $\pi\subset\Gamma$ and a section $\alpha_0:\pi\to E|_\pi$. Choose an arbitrary set-theoretic lift $s:\Gamma\to E$ extending $\alpha_0$, and put \[ \theta_\gamma(h)=s(\gamma)h s(\gamma)^{-1},\qquad t(\gamma,\delta)=s(\gamma)s(\delta)s(\gamma\delta)^{-1}\in H. \] No homomorphism or continuous lift is assumed in making this choice. The whole solution groupoid, including the possibility that it is empty, is the groupoid of functions $c:\Gamma\to H$ satisfying \[ c|_\pi=1,\qquad c(\gamma)\theta_\gamma(c(\delta))t(\gamma,\delta) =c(\gamma\delta), \] modulo the action $c(\gamma)\mapsto h c(\gamma)\theta_\gamma(h^{-1})$ of $H^\pi=Z_H(\alpha_0(\pi))$. In the topological case require that $\gamma\mapsto c(\gamma)s(\gamma)$ be continuous; if $s$ is continuous this is equivalent to continuity of $c$. Thus existence itself is expressed by explicit equations from the given extension, without choosing a solution in advance. If an extending section $\alpha:\Gamma\to E$ exists, let $\gamma\cdot h=\alpha(\gamma)h\alpha(\gamma)^{-1}$ be the resulting action on $H$. Then the groupoid of extending sections, with conjugations that preserve $\alpha_0$, is \[ \bigl[Z^1(\Gamma,H;\pi)/H^\pi\bigr], \quad Z^1(\Gamma,H;\pi)= \{c:\Gamma\to H:\ c(\gamma\delta)=c(\gamma) (\gamma\cdot c(\delta)),\ c|_\pi=1\}. \] Here $h\in H^\pi$ acts by $c(\gamma)\mapsto h c(\gamma)(\gamma\cdot h^{-1})$. If $\pi$ is normal, this groupoid is canonically $[Z^1(\Gamma/\pi,H^\pi)/H^\pi]$; its set of isomorphism classes is $H^1(\Gamma/\pi,H^\pi)$. The identifications depend on the reference section $\alpha$; changing it twists the coefficient action.

statement: Full rank-one quotient and algebraically closed residue-field slope classification.
exact_statement: Let $k$ be any perfect field of characteristic $p$, $L=W(k)[1/p]$, and $\sigma$ Witt Frobenius. statement: A derivation is a differential iff its square vanishes on degrees0 and1.
exact_statement: Let $P$ be an $A$-module. The data defining a degree-one graded derivation $d$ of $\Lambda_A^\bullet P$ are an additive derivation $d_0:A\to P$ and an additive map $d_1:P\to\Lambda_A^2P$ satisfying \[ d_1(a\omega)=d_0(a)\wedge\omega+a d_1(\omega). \] There is a unique such extension $d$. It is a differential if and only if \[ d_1d_0=0\quad\hbox{and}\quad d_2d_1=0, \qquad d_2=d|_{\Lambda_A^2P}. \] The first equation alone is insufficient, even for a free module of rank three over $\mathbf Q$.

statement: Arbitrary-flat formal-category/Lie-coalgebroid equivalence.
exact_statement: Over a ringed topos of $\mathbf Q$-algebras, the functor taking an adic formal category in the preceding pro-algebra sense, with flat $I/I^2$, to its invariant de Rham complex is an equivalence with the category of pairs \[ (P,d),\qquad P\text{ flat},\quad d:\Lambda_A^qP\longrightarrow\Lambda_A^{q+1}P, \quad d^2=0, \] where $d$ is a degree-one derivation. The arrow convention on the formal side is a continuous coordinate-proalgebra map $B\to B'$ over $A$, respecting source, target, identity and composition. On the differential side it is a map $\Lambda_A^\bullet P\to\Lambda_A^\bullet P'$ over $A$ commuting with the differential. Thus if arrows on the formal side are instead written as geometric maps $G\to H$, the equivalence is contravariant: their pullbacks go from the coordinate algebra and invariant forms of $H$ to those of $G$. The construction is also functorial for compatible changes of $A$. The inverse integrates the Lie coalgebroid. Finite projectivity is unnecessary.

statement: Finite-order and derived formal Poincare lemma.
exact_statement: Filter the relative de Rham complex of the source map by total order, where an augmentation-ideal factor and a one-form both have order one. statement: Precise formal descent site and smooth characteristic0 crystalline equivalence.
exact_statement: For a flat formal groupoid, let its formal descent site mean the site of the nilpotent jets of its simplicial nerve, with all simplicial and jet-transition maps as morphisms, and coverings induced by the chosen topology on the base. A crystal on this site means a module cartesian for these transition maps. Such crystals are exactly stratified modules and hence, by Theorem~\ref{cat:L6}, modules with integrable coalgebroid connection. The finite-order resolution and its derived completion are those of Proposition~\ref{cat:L7}. More concretely, if $X\to S$ is a smooth morphism of $\mathbf Q$-schemes and the groupoid is the formal completion of $X\times_SX$ along its diagonal, this equivalence is the usual crystalline starting equivalence: crystals of $\mathcal O$-modules on the nilpotent infinitesimal site of $X/S$ are equivalent to $\mathcal O_X$-modules with integrable $S$-connection. In characteristic zero the nilpotent divided-power crystalline site has the same objects, because divided powers are uniquely $x^{[n]}=x^n/n!$.

statement: The explicit ternary-quadratic discriminant verifies the required integral division at the prime2.

statement: The asserted coefficient degree is corrected and the plane-cubic discriminant has the elliptic Hodge-line weight12.

The relative Euler sequence on the quotient projective bundle gives $\omega_{\mathbf P(E)/S}=\mathcal O(-3)\otimes\pi^*\det E$. The cubic conormal is $\mathcal O_X(-3)\otimes p^*M$, so taking determinants of its conormal sequence gives $\omega_{X/S}=p^*(\det E\otimes M^{-1})=p^*L^{-1}$ on the smooth locus in the base. Pushing forward $0\to\pi^*M\otimes\mathcal O(-3)\to\mathcal O\to\mathcal O_X\to0$ gives $p_*\mathcal O_X=\mathcal O_S$: the zeroth and first direct images of $\mathcal O(-3)$ on $\mathbf P^2_S$ vanish, as the standard three-chart \v Cech calculation shows over any base ring. Hence the Hodge line $p_*\omega_{X/S}$ is $L^{-1}$ by the projection formula, and the discriminant line above is its twelfth tensor power. Both the coefficient degree and the determinant weight are needed for this check.

statement: The universal discriminant has primitive integral normalization, degree N(d−1)^(N−1), and determinant weight d(d−1)^(N−1).
exact_statement: Let $F=\sum_{|\alpha|=d}c_\alpha X^\alpha$ over $U=\mathbf Z[c_\alpha]$, in $N\geq1$ variables. statement: Finite locally free torsors are classified by the explicit Hopf-comodule groupoid, with constant-group and alpha_p specializations distinguished.
exact_statement: For a connected scheme $X$ with geometric point $\bar x$ and a finite constant group $G$, its $G$-torsors are classified by continuous homomorphisms $\pi_1^{\mathrm{\acute et}}(X,\bar x)\to G$ modulo conjugacy. A chosen point of the torsor above $\bar x$ removes conjugacy. For an arbitrary finite locally free group scheme $G=\operatorname{Spec}B$ over an affine $X=\operatorname{Spec}R$, including noncommutative and non-\'{e}tale groups, its complete torsor groupoid consists of finite locally free faithfully flat $R$-algebras $C$ with an algebra coaction $\rho:C\to C\otimes_R B$ such that \[ C\otimes_R C\longrightarrow C\otimes_R B, \qquad a\otimes c\longmapsto(a\otimes1)\rho(c) \] is an isomorphism. Morphisms are coaction-preserving algebra isomorphisms, with the direction reversed when passing to torsor schemes. The coaction identities are $(\rho\otimes1)\rho=(1\otimes\Delta)\rho$ and $(1\otimes\varepsilon)\rho=1_C$. These data glue over affine covers of a general $X$. For a ring $R$ of characteristic $p$ one instead has \[ H^1_{\mathrm{fppf}}(\operatorname{Spec}R,\alpha_p)=R/R^p. \] Thus ``finite'' cannot silently be replaced by ``finite \'etale''.

statement: Vector bundles on a projective line have the field splitting theorem and the stated exact relative projective-chart and Laurent-gluing classification.
exact_statement: Every rank $n$ vector bundle on $\mathbf P^1_k$, for any field $k$, is $\bigoplus_{i=1}^n\mathcal O(a_i)$, with its integers determined up to permutation. Over an arbitrary affine base $Y=\operatorname{Spec}R$, the complete classification is instead the groupoid of triples \[ (P_0,P_\infty,\phi),\qquad \phi:P_0\otimes_{R[t]}R[t,t^{-1}] \xrightarrow{\sim}P_\infty\otimes_{R[t^{-1}]}R[t,t^{-1}], \] where the two modules are finitely generated projective of rank $n$; morphisms are pairs of module isomorphisms intertwining $\phi$. Equivalently, all objects can be specified explicitly by idempotent matrices $e_0\in M_r(R[t])$ and $e_\infty\in M_s(R[t^{-1}])$ of constant rank $n$, and rectangular Laurent matrices $U\in M_{s\times r}(R[t,t^{-1}])$, $V\in M_{r\times s}(R[t,t^{-1}])$ satisfying \[ U=e_\infty Ue_0,\quad V=e_0Ve_\infty,\quad VU=e_0,\quad UV=e_\infty. \] Here $r,s$ range over all finite integers; they are not extra invariants of the bundle. Morphisms are invertible maps between the images of the two pairs of idempotents which commute with $U$ on the overlap. Thus the classification does not presuppose that projective modules over $R[t]$ or $R[t^{-1}]$ have already been classified or are free. For general $Y$, these data are descended along an affine open covering. Principal $\mathrm{GL}_n$-bundles have exactly this classification.

statement: Suppressing the base-line-bundle term in the relative square formula is false.
exact_statement: Let $S$ be a complex elliptic curve $E$, take $A=E\times S$, let $L=\operatorname{pr}_1^*\mathcal O_E(0)$, and take $x=y$ to be the diagonal section. The base line bundle in Theorem~\ref{geo-Kj} has degree $4-1-1=2$, and is nontrivial. Its pullback to $A$ is nontrivial because the zero section pulls it back to itself. Thus the absolute equality in $\operatorname{Pic}(A)$ without that base factor is false even for a projective constant family. Over a field the factor is a one-dimensional vector space and becomes trivial as a line bundle, which explains the usual field-valued formulation.
